en.lead: Answer to open the thread. You can change your answer any time.
en.bars: You can change your answer any time.
en.footer: Every position here is inferred from what the thinker actually wrote, and summarised by AI. Only the quotations are their own words — each one exact, and sourced.

zh.lead: 作答后即可展开讨论。你可以随时更改答案。
zh.footer: 这里的每个立场，都是根据本人著作推断、并由 AI 概述的。只有引文是他们自己的原话 — 逐字准确，并注明出处。

title.en: Can You Still Love the Work of Someone Who Did Terrible Things?
title.zh: 一个人做过可怕的事，你还能爱他的作品吗？

why.en: A song you have loved for years, a film that shaped you, a book you still quote — and then you learn what its maker did. Does that knowledge change what the work is, or only whether you can still enjoy it with a clear conscience?
why.zh: 一首你爱了多年的歌、一部塑造过你的电影、一本你至今还会引用的书——然后你得知了它的作者做过什么。这份知道，改变的是作品本身，还是只改变了你能否心安理得地继续喜欢它？

label.en: Yes — judge the work, not the maker
label.zh: 能——评判作品，而不是作者

label.en: Yes, but only while remembering what they did
label.zh: 能，但必须同时记得他们做过什么

label.en: No — what they did taints the work
label.zh: 不能——他们做过的事玷污了作品

title.en: Do You Owe Your Parents Care When They Grow Old?
title.zh: 父母老了，你欠他们一份照顾吗？

why.en: People live longer, families scatter across cities and countries, and more of the care of the old falls on their grown children. Some parents earned that care many times over; some did real harm. Is the care owed by birth, earned by upbringing, or never owed at all?
why.zh: 人们活得更久，家人散落在不同的城市和国家，照顾老人的担子越来越多地落在成年子女身上。有的父母早已加倍挣得了这份照顾，有的却造成过真实的伤害。这份照顾是因出生而亏欠，因养育而挣得，还是根本谈不上亏欠？

label.en: Yes — whatever kind of parents they were
label.zh: 欠——无论他们是怎样的父母

label.en: Only if they cared for you
label.zh: 只有他们照顾过你，才欠

label.en: No — care can be given, never owed
label.zh: 不欠——照顾可以给予，但谈不上亏欠

title.en: Should Children Have Smartphones Before Sixteen?
title.zh: 孩子十六岁之前，该有智能手机吗？

why.en: Countries and schools are banning phones for children, and every family still has to pick an age. Underneath is an older question: does a child learn to govern itself by being protected, or by being trusted?
why.zh: 一些国家和学校正在禁止孩子用手机，可每个家庭仍得自己定一个年龄。底下是一个更老的问题：孩子学会管住自己，靠的是被保护，还是被信任？

label.en: No — keep them out until sixteen
label.zh: 不——十六岁之前别给

label.en: Yes, with limits set by adults
label.zh: 可以，但由大人设限

label.en: Yes, freely — they learn by using them
label.zh: 可以，放手——用了才学得会

title.en: Should You Marry for Love?

why.en: For most of history people married for land, money, family or survival; love as the expected reason is recent. Now that it is expected, marriages also end more easily. Is love the right foundation, the wrong one, or is the institution itself the problem?
why.zh: 在历史的大部分时间里，人们为土地、金钱、家族或生存而结婚；把爱情当作理所当然的理由，是很晚近的事。而它成为理由之后，婚姻也更容易结束。爱情是对的地基、错的地基，还是婚姻这个制度本身就有问题？

label.en: Yes — love is the only good reason
label.zh: 是——爱情是唯一正当的理由

label.en: No — marry for character and a shared life
label.zh: 不——为品格和共同的生活而结婚

label.en: Don't marry at all
label.zh: 干脆不要结婚

title.en: Would You Take a Meaningless Job for Twice the Pay?
title.zh: 一份毫无意义的工作，薪水翻倍，你会接吗？

why.en: Plenty of well-paid work produces nothing anyone would miss, and plenty of work that matters barely pays. If the hours are the same and the money is double, what exactly would you be giving up by taking it?
why.zh: 很多高薪工作产出的东西，没了也没人在意；很多真正有意义的工作，却几乎养不活人。如果工时一样、薪水翻倍，接下它，你究竟放弃了什么？

label.en: Yes — the pay buys the life outside work
label.zh: 接——薪水买回工作之外的生活

label.en: No — the hours are your life
label.zh: 不接——上班的时间就是你的人生

label.en: Yes, and give the extra away
label.zh: 接，然后把多出来的钱送出去

title.en: Should People Be Judged for What They Posted Ten Years Ago?
title.zh: 一个人十年前发的帖子，今天还该拿来评判他吗？

why.en: People lose jobs and offers over things they posted years ago, often dug up and passed around by strangers. Under the news sits an old question: is a person still answerable for who they were?
why.zh: 有人因为多年前发的帖子丢了工作、丢了录用，翻出来转发的往往是陌生人。新闻底下是一个老问题：一个人还要为过去的自己负责吗？

label.en: Yes — what you said is still yours
label.zh: 该——说过的话仍然是你的

label.en: Only if they have never owned it
label.zh: 只在他从未认账时才该

label.en: No — judge the person they are now
label.zh: 不该——评判现在的这个人

title.en: Is It Selfish Not to Have Children?

why.en: Birth rates are falling across much of the world, and more people say plainly that they do not want children. Some call that selfish, a refusal of what each generation owes the next. Others say it needs no defence, and some ask whether it is the decision to have children that needs the stronger reason.
why.zh: 世界上许多地方的出生率都在下降，越来越多的人直言自己不想要孩子。有人说这是自私，是拒绝了每一代人对下一代的亏欠。也有人说这无需辩护，还有人问：需要更充分理由的，难道不是生孩子这个决定吗？

label.en: Yes — we owe the world a next generation
label.zh: 是——我们欠这个世界下一代

label.en: No — neither choice needs defending
label.zh: 不是——两种选择都无需辩护

label.en: No — having them is the harder choice to justify
label.zh: 不是——要孩子才更需要理由

title.en: If You Could Live Forever in Good Health, Would You?
title.zh: 如果可以健康地永远活下去，你愿意吗？

why.en: Some research now treats ageing as a process that might be slowed, perhaps one day stopped. Set the science aside and suppose it worked: would endless healthy life be the greatest gift there is, or would it take away something that makes a life a life?
why.zh: 如今有些研究把衰老看作一个也许可以减缓、甚至有一天能够停止的过程。先把科学放在一边，假设它真的成功了：无尽的健康生命会是世上最好的礼物，还是会夺走让人生成为人生的某样东西？

label.en: Yes, gladly
label.zh: 愿意，求之不得

label.en: No — an end is what gives a life its shape
label.zh: 不愿意——有终点，人生才有形状

label.en: Only if I could still choose to end it
label.zh: 只有在我仍能选择结束它时才愿意

title.en: Should Everyone Work Four Days a Week, for Four Days' Pay?
title.zh: 每个人都该每周工作四天，拿四天的工资吗？

why.en: Companies and governments are trialling the four-day week. The version that costs a fifth of your pay asks the harder question: what is a day of your life worth against a day's wages, and should one answer be set for everyone?
why.zh: 一些公司和政府正在试行每周四天工作制。要你少拿五分之一工资的那个版本，问的是更难的问题：你生命中的一天，和一天的工资相比，值多少？这个答案应该由所有人统一定下吗？

label.en: Yes — time is worth more than the money
label.zh: 是——时间比钱更值

label.en: No — keep the work and the pay
label.zh: 不——工作和工资都保留

label.en: Let each person choose their own hours
label.zh: 让每个人自己选工时

title.en: Should You Tell a Friend a Hard Truth They Didn't Ask For?
title.zh: 朋友没问，你该告诉他一个难听的真相吗？

why.en: You can see something your friend cannot: the relationship, the habit, the plan that is going wrong. Saying so may help them, or may cost you the friendship and change nothing. Is candour what friendship is for, or does it wait for an invitation?
why.zh: 你看得见朋友看不见的东西：一段关系、一个习惯、一个正在出错的计划。说出来也许能帮到他，也许会让你失去这段友谊，却什么也改变不了。坦率是友谊的本分，还是应当等对方开口？

label.en: Yes — that is what a friend is for
label.zh: 该说——朋友就是干这个的

label.en: Only if it will actually help them
label.zh: 只有真能帮到他时才说

label.en: No — wait until they ask
label.zh: 不说——等他来问

title.en: If You Have Nothing to Hide, Should You Mind Being Watched?
title.zh: 如果你没有什么可隐瞒的，你还会介意被监视吗？

why.en: 'If you've done nothing wrong, you have nothing to fear' is the standard defence of cameras, data collection and monitoring. Is privacy only for people with something to hide?
why.zh: 「没做坏事就不用怕」是为摄像头、数据收集和监控辩护的标准说法。隐私只属于有东西要藏的人吗？

label.en: No — being seen keeps everyone honest
label.zh: 不——被看见让每个人都诚实

label.en: Yes — anyone's constant watching changes you
label.zh: 会——无论谁一直盯着，都会改变你

label.en: Yes — when it's the state: its job is to let you alone
label.zh: 会——如果是国家：它的本分就是不打扰你

title.en: Would You Rather Be Led by Someone Good, or Someone Who Gets Things Done?
title.zh: 你宁愿被一个好人领导，还是被一个能办成事的人领导？

why.en: We are often offered a trade: a leader with clean hands who may achieve little, or one who delivers but cuts moral corners. Is that a real choice — or a false one?
why.zh: 我们常常被摆在一个交换面前：一个双手干净却可能一事无成的领导，或者一个能出成绩却在道德上走捷径的领导。这是真实的选择，还是一个伪命题？

label.en: Someone good — character is how a leader leads
label.zh: 选好人——品格本身就是领导力

label.en: Someone effective — results matter more than clean hands
label.zh: 选能办事的——结果比清白更重要

label.en: False choice — real wisdom is both
label.zh: 这是个伪命题——真正的智慧二者兼有

title.en: Is a Billionaire's Success Earned, or Just Luck Dressed Up as Genius?
title.zh: 亿万富翁的成功是挣来的，还是被包装成天才的运气？

why.en: Some fortunes come from rare talent and years of work; others from being in the right place when a market took off. From the outside they look the same, and the story told afterwards is always about genius. Which is it, usually?
why.zh: 有些财富来自罕见的才能和多年的努力；另一些则来自在市场起飞时恰好站对了位置。从外面看，两者一模一样，而事后讲的故事总是关于天才。通常是哪一种？

label.en: Earned — it follows from what they did
label.zh: 挣来的——结果来自他们的所作所为

label.en: Partly — real skill, but the genius story overstates it
label.zh: 部分是——有真本事，但天才的故事夸大了它

label.en: Mostly not — it rests on others' labour
label.zh: 大多不是——靠的是别人的劳动

title.en: Would You Want to Know Everything Your Partner Hides From You?
title.zh: 你想知道伴侣对你隐瞒的一切吗？

why.en: Phones, messages and shared accounts make it newly possible to know almost everything about a partner. Would complete knowledge make love safer, or make it impossible?
why.zh: 手机、消息和共享账户让人们第一次几乎可以知道伴侣的一切。完全的了解会让爱更安全，还是让爱变得不可能？

label.en: Yes — knowing beats imagining
label.zh: 想——知道比猜想好

label.en: No — some things should stay unknown
label.zh: 不想——有些东西就该留在未知里

label.en: You couldn't — they don't know it all themselves
label.zh: 做不到——他们自己也不全知道

title.en: If the Smartest Person in the Country Doesn't Want to Be President, Should We Make Them?
title.zh: 如果全国最聪明的人不想当总统，我们该逼他上任吗？

why.en: Some of the people best suited to lead want nothing to do with it, and the people who want it most are not always the ones you would pick. Should a society be able to draft its best minds into office — or is the right to say no part of what makes them free?
why.zh: 最适合领导的人里，有些人对此毫无兴趣；而最想当领导的人，又未必是你会选的人。一个社会能不能把最优秀的头脑征召上任？还是说，说「不」的权利本身就是自由的一部分？

label.en: Yes — the best should be made to serve
label.zh: 应该——最合适的人有义务出来

label.en: No — no one should be forced into office
label.zh: 不应该——谁都不该被逼上任

label.en: Only if the country deserves them
label.zh: 要看这个国家值不值得他出来

title.en: If Everyone in Your Industry Cuts Corners, Are You a Fool for Not Doing It?
title.zh: 如果你所在的行业人人都走捷径，你不这么做是不是傻？

why.en: In some industries cutting corners is so normal that refusing looks naïve: you lose bids, promotions or customers to people who don't. If everyone does it, are you principled, or just losing?
why.zh: 在某些行业里，走捷径如此普遍，拒绝反而显得天真：你会把投标、升职或客户输给那些不在乎的人。如果人人都这么做，你是有原则，还是只是在输？

label.en: No — it costs you, and it's still right
label.zh: 不——会吃亏，但仍然是对的

label.en: No — it isn't really a loss
label.zh: 不——这其实算不上损失

label.en: Not a fool — but the fix is a referee, not a lone holdout
label.zh: 不傻——但该补的是裁判，不是靠你一个人硬撑

title.en: Is It Betrayal to Spy on Your Own Country to Save It?
title.zh: 为了拯救自己的国家而暗中对它下手，算不算背叛？

why.en: History has people who spied on, leaked from or worked against their own government because they believed it was heading for disaster. Were they traitors, or the most loyal people in the room?
why.zh: 历史上有人因为相信自己的政府正走向灾难，而对它刺探、泄密或暗中反对。他们是叛徒，还是在场最忠诚的人？

label.en: No — saving the country outranks every rule
label.zh: 不是——救国高于一切规则

label.en: Yes — a private person must obey, not judge
label.zh: 是——个人只能服从，不能替国家评判

label.en: Yes — dissent must be open, never secret
label.zh: 是——反对只能公开，不能暗中

title.en: Is Wanting Power the Thing That Should Disqualify You From Having It?
title.zh: 想要权力，是否正是你不该拥有它的理由？

why.en: We distrust people who chase power, yet almost no one gets power without chasing it. Should ambition for office count against the person who has it?
why.zh: 我们不信任追逐权力的人，可几乎没有人不追逐就能得到权力。对公职的野心，应该成为扣分项吗？

label.en: Yes — wanting it is the warning sign
label.zh: 是——想要本身就是危险信号

label.en: No — what matters is what they want it for
label.zh: 不——要看他们想用它做什么

label.en: No — watch the holding, not the wanting
label.zh: 不——该防的是掌权，不是想要

title.en: Do the Most Successful Companies Win by Being Better, or by Being Ruthless?
title.zh: 最成功的公司，是靠更好赢的，还是靠更狠赢的？

why.en: We like to think the market rewards the best product. But the history of business also includes price-fixing, crushed rivals and borrowed ideas. When a company comes out on top, what usually got it there?
why.zh: 我们愿意相信市场奖励最好的产品。但商业史里也有操纵价格、碾压对手和借用他人创意。当一家公司登上顶峰，通常是什么把它送到那里的？

label.en: Better — while competition stays open
label.zh: 靠更好——只要竞争保持开放

label.en: Ruthless — competition rewards it
label.zh: 靠狠——竞争奖励的就是狠

label.en: Neither — the ones that last cooperate
label.zh: 都不是——长久的赢家靠合作

title.en: Is Lying for Your Country Different From Lying for Yourself?
title.zh: 为国家说谎，和为自己说谎有区别吗？

why.en: Diplomats, spies and officials sometimes lie as part of the job, and we often call it duty. The same lie told for personal gain we call wrong. Does the reason change what the lie is?
why.zh: 外交官、间谍和官员有时把说谎当作工作的一部分，我们常称之为职责。同样的谎话若是为了私利，我们就说它错了。理由会改变谎言的性质吗？

label.en: Yes — the state's reasons change what the lie is
label.zh: 是——为国的理由改变了谎言的性质

label.en: It may be needed — but it still stains
label.zh: 也许必要——但仍会留下污点

label.en: No — a lie is a lie
label.zh: 不——谎言就是谎言

title.en: Should a Leader Be Like You, or Better Than You?
title.zh: 领导者应该像你，还是比你更好？

why.en: Some voters want a leader who talks, lives and thinks like them. Others want someone wiser, more expert or more disciplined than they are. Which makes a better leader — and a better democracy?
why.zh: 有些选民希望领导者说话、生活、思考都和自己一样；另一些人想要一个比自己更有智慧、更专业、更自律的人。哪一种会是更好的领导者——又会成就更好的民主？

label.en: Better than you — leading takes expertise
label.zh: 比你更强——领导需要专长

label.en: Like you — someone who shares ordinary life
label.zh: 像你——和普通人过一样的日子

label.en: Neither — what matters is that they answer to you
label.zh: 都不是——关键在于他们向你负责

title.en: When a Product Wins the Market, Does That Prove It's the Best One?
title.zh: 一个产品赢得了市场，就证明它是最好的吗？

why.en: The product everyone uses is not always the one experts rate highest. Network effects, timing and marketing all play a part. Is winning the market the best test of quality we have, or a measure of something else?
why.zh: 人人都在用的产品，未必是专家评价最高的那个。网络效应、时机和营销都在起作用。赢得市场是我们衡量质量的最好方法，还是在衡量别的东西？

label.en: Yes — buyers are the judges
label.zh: 是——买家就是裁判

label.en: Only if informed buyers keep choosing it
label.zh: 只有懂行的买家长期选择它才算

label.en: No — the market measures price, not worth
label.zh: 不是——市场衡量价格，而非价值

title.en: If AI Can Do Your Job Better Than You, What Was All That Effort For?
title.zh: 如果 AI 比你更会做你的工作，那这些年的努力是为了什么？

why.en: You may have spent twenty years getting unusually good at writing, coding or design — and now a machine does part of it in seconds. If technology takes away a skill's economic value, does it take away the value of having mastered it?
why.zh: 你也许花了二十年，才在写作、编程或设计上变得格外出色——如今机器几秒钟就能完成其中一部分。如果技术拿走了一项技能的经济价值，它是否也拿走了掌握它的价值？

label.en: For who it made me — nothing was wasted
label.zh: 为了它把我塑造成的样子，什么都没白费

label.en: Losing the work is not the loss it looks
label.zh: 失去这份工作，并不是看上去那样的损失

label.en: Something real is being lost
label.zh: 确实有真实的东西正在失去

title.en: If a GLP-1 Changes Your Personality, Which Version Is the Real You?
title.zh: 如果 GLP-1 改变了你的性格，哪个才是真正的你？

why.en: GLP-1 drugs were made to change appetite, but early research suggests they can reach craving and impulse too. If a pill makes you calmer and less driven, is that your real self emerging — or a sign there was never one fixed self to find?
why.zh: GLP-1 药物原本用来改变食欲，但早期研究显示，它们也可能影响渴望与冲动。如果一种药让你更平静、更少被欲望驱使，那是真正的你浮现了——还是说明从来就没有一个固定的“真正的我”？

label.en: The real me is what I choose, not what I crave
label.zh: 真正的我是我的选择，而不是我的渴望

label.en: Whichever self I can affirm — judge it by the life it makes
label.zh: 我能认同的那个自己，看它造就怎样的生活

label.en: Neither — there is no fixed real me
label.zh: 都不是，没有一个固定不变的真正的我

title.en: Should people be allowed to sell their eggs or sperm?
title.zh: 人应该可以合法买卖自己的卵子或精子吗？

why.en: Many places already let donors be paid. But once eggs and sperm have a price, it is not only about your body: money shapes who takes the medical risk, and a future person never agreed to the deal. Where should freedom over your own body end?
why.zh: 许多地方已经允许捐赠者获得报酬。但一旦卵子和精子有了价格，问题就不只关乎你的身体：金钱会影响谁去承担医疗风险，而未来的那个人从未同意这笔交易。你对自己身体的自由，边界在哪里？

label.en: Yes — they are yours to sell
label.zh: 可以，它们是你的，你有权出售

label.en: Yes, but regulate prices and protect donors
label.zh: 可以，但价格和捐赠者保护必须受到监管

label.en: No — donate if you like, but not for sale
label.zh: 不可以，可以捐赠，但不应买卖

title.en: Nobody Is Going to Remember You. So Why Are You Trying So Hard?
title.zh: 几代以后，可能根本没人会记得你。那你现在为什么还这么努力？

why.en: Most of us will eventually disappear from collective memory. If achievement, status, and recognition are temporary, what makes the effort we put into our lives worthwhile?
why.zh: 我们中的绝大多数人最终都会从集体记忆中消失。如果成就、地位和认可都是暂时的，我们现在投入这么多精力生活，到底是为了什么？

label.en: It never needed to last — living it is enough
label.zh: 它本来就不需要被记住，活过就够了

label.en: What I do for other people
label.zh: 为别人所做的事

label.en: What I start keeps going without my name
label.zh: 我开始的事情会在没有我名字的情况下继续

title.en: What If Most of What You Believe Was Chosen for You?
title.zh: 如果你相信的大多数东西，其实都是别人替你选的呢？

why.en: You didn't choose your birthplace, family, language, culture, or earliest values. Now algorithms also influence which ideas you encounter. If another environment could have produced a very different you, how much of your worldview can you really call your own?
why.zh: 你没有选择自己的出生地、家庭、语言、文化和最早接受的价值观，现在算法也在影响你会接触哪些思想。如果换一个环境就可能产生完全不同的你，你的世界观到底有多少真正属于自己？

label.en: Much — I can test a belief on its merits, wherever it came from
label.zh: 很多，无论信念从哪里来，我都能凭它本身检验它

label.en: Less than I think — it takes deliberate work against the grain
label.zh: 比我以为的少，需要刻意逆着惯性去思考

label.en: None of it fully — no worldview stands outside its making
label.zh: 没有一样完全属于我，没有世界观能脱离塑造它的环境

title.en: Maybe Nothing Happens for a Reason. Why Do We Keep Looking for One?
title.zh: 也许什么事情都不是「命中注定」。那我们为什么一直想找到一个原因？

why.en: A coincidence changes your career. You meet someone at exactly the right moment. Something terrible eventually leads somewhere unexpected. Are we discovering meaning in these events — or creating a story because randomness is difficult to accept?
why.zh: 一个巧合改变了你的职业，你恰好在某个时间遇见一个重要的人，一件糟糕的事情最后却带来了意外的结果。我们是在这些事情里发现了意义，还是因为很难接受随机，所以后来创造了一个故事？

label.en: Yes — some events are meant
label.zh: 是的，有些事情确实有其意义

label.en: No — the meaning is one we make afterwards
label.zh: 没有，意义是我们事后赋予的

label.en: There is pattern, but no one behind it
label.zh: 有规律，但背后没有安排者

title.en: If the Belief That Changed Your Life Wasn't Literally True, Would It Matter?
title.zh: 如果一个改变了你人生的信念并不是真的，它还重要吗？

why.en: Religious teachings, spiritual practices, philosophical ideas, rituals, and even fictional stories can fundamentally change how someone lives. Does an idea need to describe reality literally to contain something true or valuable?
why.zh: 宗教教义、精神实践、哲学思想、仪式，甚至虚构故事，都可能深刻改变一个人的生活方式。一个思想是否必须在字面上准确描述现实，才可以包含某种真实或价值？

label.en: Yes — truth matters more than usefulness
label.zh: 会，真假比有用更重要

label.en: Not always — where evidence cannot decide, what it does for a life counts
label.zh: 不一定，在证据无法裁决的地方，它对人生的作用也算数

label.en: Wrong test — its truth was never meant literally
label.zh: 问错了，它的真实本来就不是字面上的

title.en: Maybe You Don't Want Unlimited Freedom. Maybe Nobody Does.
title.zh: 也许你并不想拥有无限的自由。可能根本没人想。

why.en: Having more choices sounds desirable, yet people repeatedly create rules, traditions, routines, communities, and institutions that restrict those choices. How much freedom does a person actually need to live well?
why.zh: 更多选择听起来总是更好，但人类又不断创造规则、传统、习惯、群体和制度来限制自己的选择。一个人到底需要多少自由，才能过自己想要的人生？

label.en: As much as possible — the danger is giving it up
label.zh: 越多越好，危险在于把它交出去

label.en: Freedom needs a shape to be worth having
label.zh: 自由需要形状才有价值

label.en: Less than we think — belonging matters more
label.zh: 比我们以为的少，归属更重要

title.en: What If Your Personality Is Partly Something You've Learned to Perform?
title.zh: 如果你的「性格」，有一部分只是你慢慢学会扮演出来的呢？

why.en: Personality tests, attachment styles, family roles, cultural expectations, diagnoses, and algorithms give us increasingly detailed descriptions of ourselves. When a description feels perfectly accurate, is it discovering you — or influencing who you become?
why.zh: 人格测试、依恋类型、家庭角色、文化期待、诊断和算法越来越详细地告诉我们「你是什么样的人」。当一个描述准确得惊人时，它是在发现你，还是也在影响你最后成为谁？

label.en: Performed or not, it becomes really you
label.zh: 无论是不是表演，它最终都成了真正的你

label.en: The labels are making you more than finding you
label.zh: 标签与其说在发现你，不如说在塑造你

label.en: There is no fixed self underneath for them to find
label.zh: 底下根本没有一个固定的自我可供发现

title.en: If You Were Born 500 Years Ago, Would You Still Be “You”?
title.zh: 如果你出生在 500 年前，你还是现在这个「你」吗？

why.en: Change your language, family, gender expectations, religion, technology, education, and everything society considers normal. If almost all of your beliefs and possibilities changed with them, what part of you would actually remain?
why.zh: 换掉你的语言、家庭、性别规范、宗教环境、技术、教育，以及社会对「正常」的全部定义。如果你的信念和人生可能性几乎全部改变，还有什么东西会保持不变？

label.en: Yes — something at the root would still be me
label.zh: 会，根本上的某些东西仍然是我

label.en: There is no clear answer — it is a matter of degree
label.zh: 没有明确答案，这是程度问题

label.en: No — a different world would make a different person
label.zh: 不会，不同的世界会造就另一个人

title.en: If Everyone Around You Thinks You're Wrong, When Should You Start Believing Them?
title.zh: 如果你身边所有人都觉得你错了，你什么时候应该开始相信他们？

why.en: Independent thinking sounds admirable until everyone you trust disagrees with you. At what point does resisting the group stop being courage and become refusing to consider evidence?
why.zh: 独立思考听起来很值得坚持，直到所有你信任的人都不同意你。什么时候坚持自己是勇气，什么时候又只是拒绝面对证据？

label.en: Not because they are many — only for evidence
label.zh: 不因为人多，只因为证据

label.en: Only when they know the subject better than I do
label.zh: 只有当他们比我更懂这件事时

label.en: When each reached it on their own, expert or not
label.zh: 当他们各自独立得出这个结论时，无论是否内行

title.en: If We Could Remove Every Painful Emotion, Should We?
title.zh: 如果我们可以消除所有痛苦的情绪，我们应该这么做吗？

why.en: Fear, grief, jealousy, shame, and anxiety can make life miserable, but they also influence relationships, morality, survival, creativity, and identity. If technology could safely remove them, would a happier human necessarily be a better one?
why.zh: 恐惧、悲伤、嫉妒、羞耻和焦虑会让生活非常痛苦，但它们也影响关系、道德、生存、创造力和身份。如果技术可以安全地消除它们，一个更快乐的人就一定是一个更完整的人吗？

label.en: Yes — remove it wherever we can
label.zh: 应该，能消除就消除

label.en: Only the excess — keep the pain that fits what happened
label.zh: 只去掉过度的部分，保留与事情相称的痛苦

label.en: No — that pain is part of a human life
label.zh: 不应该，这种痛苦本就是人生的一部分

title.en: If Humanity Solved Every Survival Problem, What Would We Do With Ourselves?
title.zh: 如果人类解决了所有生存问题，我们接下来到底要干什么？

why.en: Imagine food, housing, healthcare, and material security becoming abundant while machines handle most necessary labor. Would humans finally become free to live — or would we simply invent new competitions, hierarchies, and problems?
why.zh: 想象食物、住房、医疗和基本物质生活都变得充足，而机器完成大部分必要劳动。人类会终于开始真正自由地生活，还是只是创造新的竞争、等级和问题？

label.en: We would finally turn to love, making and exploring
label.zh: 我们终于会转向关系、创造和探索

label.en: We would invent new contests for work and status
label.zh: 我们会发明新的工作和地位竞争

label.en: Abundance alone changes little — it depends how work and life are organised
label.zh: 光有富足改变不了什么，关键在于工作和生活如何组织

claim.en: I held that art is independent of morality. Judging a work as art is one act; judging the artist as a man who acts in the world is another, and the first has nothing to do with the second.
claim.zh: 我认为艺术独立于道德。把一部作品当作艺术来评判是一回事；把艺术家当作一个在世上行动的人来评判是另一回事，前者与后者毫不相干。

detail.en: In the Aesthetic, Croce separated contemplation from practical life, and in the same passage insisted that the artist still answers to the tribunal of moral conscience: he never excused the person. Applying this to a reader's or listener's love of a work is our step. The strongest objection is that some works are not sealed off from their making — when the wrong was done in making the work, or to the people in it, the two judgments are no longer separate.
detail.zh: 在《美学》中，克罗齐把审美观照与实践生活分开，并在同一段里坚持艺术家仍要接受道德良知的审判：他从未替这个人开脱。把这一点用在读者或听者对作品的喜爱上，是我们的推论。最有力的反驳是：有些作品并没有与它的制作过程隔绝——如果恶行正是在创作中、或是对作品里的人犯下的，这两种评判就不再能分开。

quote.en: The aesthetic judgment on the work of art has nothing to do with the morality of the artist, in so far as he is a practical man, nor with the precautions to be taken that art may not be employed for evil purposes alien to its essence, which is pure theoretic contemplation.
quote.zh: The aesthetic judgment on the work of art has nothing to do with the morality of the artist, in so far as he is a practical man, nor with the precautions to be taken that art may not be employed for evil purposes alien to its essence, which is pure theoretic contemplation.

label.en: Benedetto Croce, Aesthetic as Science of Expression and General Linguistic, trans. Douglas Ainslie
label.zh: 克罗齐《作为表现的科学和一般语言学的美学》，安斯利 英译

claim.en: I wrote that poetry has its own standard of correctness, which is not the standard of politics. A poem is to be faulted for failing as a poem, not for failing at something else.
claim.zh: 我写过，诗有它自己的正误标准，不同于政治的标准。一首诗该因作为诗失败而受指责，而不是因为在别的事情上失败。

detail.en: Aristotle was separating the rules of an art from the rules of civic life, judging a tragedy by its craft rather than its politics. He said nothing about a poet's private conduct; carrying the point from the work's content to its maker's life is our step. The objection: the Poetics itself wants the characters of tragedy to be good, so Aristotle never made art wholly independent of ethics.
detail.zh: 亚里士多德是在把一门艺术的规则与城邦生活的规则分开，按技艺而非政治来评判悲剧。他没有谈过诗人的私人品行；把这一点从作品内容延伸到作者的生平，是我们的推论。反驳是：《诗学》本身就要求悲剧人物品格良好，所以亚里士多德从未让艺术完全独立于伦理。

quote.en: Add to this, that the standard of correctness is not the same in poetry and politics, any more than in poetry and any other art.
quote.zh: Add to this, that the standard of correctness is not the same in poetry and politics, any more than in poetry and any other art.

label.en: Aristotle, Poetics, ch. 25, trans. S. H. Butcher
label.zh: 亚里士多德《诗学》第二十五章，布彻 英译

claim.en: I observed that artists often misread their own work: Wagner misunderstood the philosophy hidden in the very characters he created. The art can hold something its maker does not grasp.
claim.zh: 我注意到，艺术家常常误读自己的作品：瓦格纳就误解了他亲手创造的人物中暗藏的哲学。艺术里可以有作者自己都没有领会的东西。

detail.en: Nietzsche's point concerned an artist's ideas, not his conduct: Wagner's heroes, he thought, contradicted the theories Wagner professed. Applying it to what an artist did is our step. The objection is that it cuts both ways — if the maker is no authority on the work, the argument offers no defence when a work really does carry its maker's worst views.
detail.zh: 尼采说的是艺术家的观念，而不是他的行为：他认为瓦格纳笔下的英雄与瓦格纳本人宣扬的理论相互矛盾。把它用在艺术家的所作所为上，是我们的推论。反驳是：这个论证是双刃的——如果作者对作品没有权威，那么当一部作品确实承载了作者最坏的观点时，它也提供不了任何辩护。

quote.en: It has happened to him as it has already happened to many an artist: he made a mistake in the interpretation of the characters he created, and misunderstood the unexpressed philosophy of the art peculiarly his own.
quote.zh: It has happened to him as it has already happened to many an artist: he made a mistake in the interpretation of the characters he created, and misunderstood the unexpressed philosophy of the art peculiarly his own.

label.en: Friedrich Nietzsche, The Joyful Wisdom, §99, trans. Thomas Common
label.zh: 尼采《快乐的科学》第 99 节，托马斯·康芒 英译

claim.en: I noticed that we can admire a thing and wish it destroyed at the same time: the walls of an enemy city strike us as beautiful for their strength, even while we hope they fall. The two feelings differ in kind, so they can be contrary without cancelling each other.
claim.zh: 我注意到，我们可以同时欣赏一样东西、又希望它被毁掉：敌城的城墙因坚固而显得美，尽管我们盼着它倒塌。这两种感受性质不同，所以可以彼此相反而不相互抵消。

detail.en: Hume was explaining how approval arises when we view things in general rather than through our own interest. That an admirer can hold delight and condemnation together, neither erasing the other, is our application. The objection is that Hume describes what minds can do, not what they should: holding both feelings may simply be a comfortable way of never acting on the second.
detail.zh: 休谟是在解释，当我们从一般的角度、而不是从自身利益出发看待事物时，赞许是如何产生的。一个欣赏者可以同时怀着喜爱与谴责、两者都不抹去对方，这是我们的引申。反驳是：休谟描述的是心灵能做到什么，而不是应当怎样——同时怀着两种感受，也可能只是一种永远不必按第二种感受行事的舒服办法。

quote.en: Nay, these emotions are so different in their feeling, that they may often be contrary, without destroying each other; as when the fortifications of a city belonging to an enemy are esteemed beautiful upon account of their strength, though we could wish that they were entirely destroyed.
quote.zh: Nay, these emotions are so different in their feeling, that they may often be contrary, without destroying each other; as when the fortifications of a city belonging to an enemy are esteemed beautiful upon account of their strength, though we could wish that they were entirely destroyed.

label.en: David Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, Book III, Part III, Sect. I
label.zh: 休谟《人性论》第三卷第三部分第一节

claim.en: I held that it is dangerous to show a person their greatness without their baseness, or their baseness without their greatness, and more dangerous still to see neither. The advantage lies in seeing both.
claim.zh: 我认为，只让人看到自己的伟大而看不到卑劣，或只看到卑劣而看不到伟大，都很危险；两者都看不见则更危险。好处在于把两者都看见。

detail.en: Pascal was writing about human nature before God, not about artists. Applying his double vision, greatness and vileness held in one view, to a gifted person who did harm is our step. The objection: seeing both is easy to claim and hard to sustain, and in practice the greatness on the page or screen tends to win.
detail.zh: 帕斯卡写的是人在上帝面前的本性，而不是艺术家。把他这种双重目光——把伟大与卑劣放在同一视野里——用在一个有才华却伤害过人的人身上，是我们的推论。反驳是：说自己两者都看见很容易，真正做到却很难；实际上，纸面或银幕上的伟大往往会胜出。

quote.en: it is also dangerous to show him his greatness too clearly apart from his vileness. It is still more dangerous to leave him in ignorance of both. But it is of great advantage to show him both.
quote.zh: it is also dangerous to show him his greatness too clearly apart from his vileness. It is still more dangerous to leave him in ignorance of both. But it is of great advantage to show him both.

label.en: Blaise Pascal, Thoughts (Pensées), trans. C. Kegan Paul
label.zh: 帕斯卡《思想录》，凯根·保罗 英译

claim.en: Through Socrates I argued that style follows the soul: grace and harmony are kin to goodness and virtue, and ugliness and discord are close allies of an ill nature.
claim.zh: 我借苏格拉底之口论证，风格随灵魂而来：优雅与和谐是善与德的姊妹，丑陋与不谐则与恶劣的本性为伍。

detail.en: In the Republic the speaker is Socrates, the subject is the education of a city's young guardians, and this passage leads straight to censoring the poets. Reading it as a claim that a bad person's work must carry their badness is our step. The objection is history itself: many people who did terrible things made works of real grace, which the theory says should not happen.
detail.zh: 《理想国》中的说话人是苏格拉底，话题是城邦年轻护卫者的教育，而这段话直接引向了对诗人的审查。把它读成坏人的作品必然带着他的坏，是我们的推论。反驳来自历史本身：许多做过可怕之事的人，都创作出了真正优雅的作品，而按这个理论，这本不该发生。

quote.en: And ugliness and discord and inharmonious motion are nearly allied to ill words and ill nature, as grace and harmony are the twin sisters of goodness and virtue and bear their likeness.
quote.zh: And ugliness and discord and inharmonious motion are nearly allied to ill words and ill nature, as grace and harmony are the twin sisters of goodness and virtue and bear their likeness.

label.en: Plato, The Republic, Book III, trans. Benjamin Jowett
label.zh: 柏拉图《理想国》第三卷，乔伊特 英译

claim.en: I argued that moral concerns do more than outrank beauty: when they fill the mind, a form pleasing in itself can become disagreeable and stop being beautiful to us at all.
claim.zh: 我认为，道德关切不只是比美更重要：当它们占据心灵时，一个本身令人愉悦的形式也会变得令人不快，对我们来说根本不再美。

detail.en: Santayana's examples were occasions, such as too much eloquence in a prayer or a diplomatic letter, and he held that nothing is ugly in itself. That knowing what a maker did can drain a work of its beauty for the one who knows is our application. The objection is that this makes the taint depend on the viewer: for someone who does not know, or whose mind is elsewhere, the work stays as beautiful as before.
detail.zh: 桑塔亚那举的例子是场合，比如祈祷文或外交信函里过多的辞藻，而且他认为没有什么东西本身是丑的。知道作者做过什么，会让作品在知情者眼中失去美，这是我们的引申。反驳是：这样一来，玷污取决于观看的人——对不知情或心思不在此的人来说，作品依然和从前一样美。

quote.en: Forms in themselves pleasing may become disagreeable when the practical interests then uppermost in the mind cannot, without violence, yield a place to them.
quote.zh: Forms in themselves pleasing may become disagreeable when the practical interests then uppermost in the mind cannot, without violence, yield a place to them.

label.en: George Santayana, The Sense of Beauty, §55
label.zh: 桑塔亚那《美感》第 55 节

claim.en: I taught that duties are measured by relations. A father is owed care and patience because he is your father, not because he is a good one: what he does is his affair, what you do is yours.
claim.zh: 我教导说，义务由关系来衡量。父亲应得照顾与忍让，是因为他是你的父亲，而不是因为他是个好父亲：他怎么做是他的事，你怎么做才是你的事。

detail.en: This comes from the Enchiridion, the Stoic handbook in which every relation is a role to be played well whatever the other person does. Applying it to the care of an ageing parent is our step. The strongest objection is in the passage itself: it asks the child to submit even to blows, and a duty that survives abuse can trap the very person Stoicism meant to set free.
detail.zh: 这段话出自《手册》，这部斯多葛派的小书把每一种关系都看作一个角色，无论对方怎样做，都要把它演好。把它用到照顾年迈父母这件事上，是我们的推论。最有力的反驳就在这段话里：它要求孩子连挨打也要顺从，而一种在虐待之下依然有效的义务，可能会困住斯多葛派本想让其获得自由的那个人。

quote.en: Is a man a father? The precept is to take care of him, to yield to him in all things, to submit when he is reproachful, when he inflicts blows. But suppose that he is a bad father. Were you then by nature made akin to a good father? No; but to a father.
quote.zh: Is a man a father? The precept is to take care of him, to yield to him in all things, to submit when he is reproachful, when he inflicts blows. But suppose that he is a bad father. Were you then by nature made akin to a good father? No; but to a father.

origin.zh: 尼科波利斯，约公元 125 年

label.en: Epictetus, Enchiridion 30, trans. George Long
label.zh: 爱比克泰德《手册》第 30 章，朗 英译

claim.en: I held that a son can never repay what his father first gave him, so he remains a debtor all his life. That is why I judged that a son may never disown his father, though a father may disown a son.
claim.zh: 我认为，儿子永远无法偿还父亲最初给予他的一切，所以他一生都是债务人。正因如此，我断定儿子永远不可以与父亲断绝关系，而父亲却可以与儿子断绝关系。

detail.en: Aristotle was ranking the claims of different friendships, and the debt rests on benefits received: existence first, then nurture and education. Carrying it into modern elder care is our step. The objection is that a debt nobody chose to take on is an odd kind of debt, and Aristotle lets a father cast off a depraved son while giving the child of a depraved father no matching way out.
detail.zh: 亚里士多德是在为各种友爱的要求排序，这笔债建立在所受的恩惠之上：首先是生命，然后是养育和教育。把它用到现代的养老问题上，是我们的推论。反驳是：一笔谁也没有选择承担的债，是一种奇怪的债；而且亚里士多德允许父亲抛弃堕落的儿子，却没有给堕落父亲的孩子留下相应的出路。

quote.en: a son can never, by anything he has done, fully requite the benefits first conferred on him by his father, and so is always a debtor.
quote.zh: a son can never, by anything he has done, fully requite the benefits first conferred on him by his father, and so is always a debtor.

label.en: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics, Book VIII, ch. 14, trans. D. P. Chase
label.zh: 亚里士多德《尼各马可伦理学》第八卷第十四章，蔡斯 英译

claim.en: I argued that a child's obligation arises from being kept alive and brought up, not from being begotten. A mother who abandons her infant voids that obligation, and the child then owes everything to whoever raised it.
claim.zh: 我认为，孩子的义务来自被养活、被抚养长大，而不是来自被生下来。抛弃婴儿的母亲使这份义务归于无效，孩子从此对抚养他的人负有一切。

detail.en: Hobbes was writing about dominion in the state of nature, about who has the right to command a child, not about tending the old. Reading it as a rule for elder care is our step. The objection: he turns the family into a ledger of preservation and obedience, so a parent who fed a child but was cruel in every other way would still, on his account, keep the whole claim.
detail.zh: 霍布斯写的是自然状态下的支配权，即谁有权命令一个孩子，而不是照顾老人。把它读作养老的准则，是我们的推论。反驳是：他把家庭变成了一本关于保全与服从的账，按他的说法，一个把孩子喂大、却在其他方面处处残忍的父母，依然保有全部的要求。

quote.en: Wherefore the obligation also which arose from the benefit of life, is by this exposition made void.
quote.zh: Wherefore the obligation also which arose from the benefit of life, is by this exposition made void.

label.en: Thomas Hobbes, Philosophical Rudiments concerning Government and Society (De Cive), ch. IX, §4
label.zh: 霍布斯《论公民》第九章第 4 节

claim.en: I argued that ill-will or indifference is not a crime in itself. It becomes the crime of ingratitude only when it is turned on someone who first showed us good-will and did us good.
claim.zh: 我认为，恶意或冷漠本身并不是罪过。只有当它指向一个先前对我们表示过善意、为我们做过好事的人时，它才成为忘恩负义之罪。

detail.en: Hume was arguing that moral blame comes from sentiment rather than reason, and used ingratitude as his example; applying it to grown children and ageing parents is our step. In the Treatise he names ingratitude toward parents as the most unnatural of crimes, so he was no enemy of filial duty. The objection is that his test needs a record of good-will shown, and few families keep a ledger anyone would agree on.
detail.zh: 休谟论证的是道德上的责备出自情感而非理性，忘恩负义只是他举的例子；把它用到成年子女与年迈父母身上，是我们的推论。在《人性论》里，他把对父母忘恩负义称为最违背天性的罪行，所以他并不反对孝道。反驳是：他的标准需要一份关于善意的记录，而很少有家庭的这本账是各方都认可的。

quote.en: No, they are only crimes when directed towards persons who have before expressed and displayed good-will towards us.
quote.zh: No, they are only crimes when directed towards persons who have before expressed and displayed good-will towards us.

label.en: David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals, Appendix I
label.zh: 休谟《道德原则研究》附录一

claim.en: I wrote that a right always includes a duty. Parents who demand a child's obedience without doing the work of forming the child's mind forfeit the right they claim.
claim.zh: 我写道，权利总是包含着义务。要求孩子服从、自己却不肯花力气塑造孩子心智的父母，丧失了他们所主张的权利。

detail.en: Her chapter on duty to parents attacks parents who insist on blind obedience while neglecting their children's minds; the right at issue is parental authority, and extending it to care in old age is our step. She also says a parent who does that work earns the rights of the closest friendship for life. The objection: someone has to judge whether the duty was fulfilled, and a grown child is hardly an impartial judge of their own upbringing.
detail.zh: 她论对父母之义务的那一章，抨击的是一边坚持要孩子盲从、一边忽视孩子心智的父母；这里说的权利是父母的权威，把它延伸到年老时的照顾，是我们的推论。她也说，尽到这份责任的父母，会终身享有最深厚友谊的权利。反驳是：总得有人来判断这份义务是否尽到，而成年子女很难公正地评判自己的成长。

quote.en: a right always includes a duty, and I think it may, likewise fairly be inferred, that they forfeit the right, who do not fulfil the duty.
quote.zh: a right always includes a duty, and I think it may, likewise fairly be inferred, that they forfeit the right, who do not fulfil the duty.

label.en: Mary Wollstonecraft, A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, ch. XI
label.zh: 沃斯通克拉夫特《女权辩护》第十一章

claim.en: I denied that gratitude has any place in justice. A father who supported his child deserves esteem for the good he did, exactly as if he had done it for a stranger, and when he took on those cares he was not thinking of the particular child who would come.
claim.zh: 我否认感恩在正义中有任何位置。一个抚养孩子的父亲，因他所行的善而值得尊重，但这份尊重与他把同样的善行施于陌生人时完全一样；而且他承担这些操劳时，想的并不是将来会出生的那个具体的孩子。

detail.en: Godwin was arguing that justice must be impartial, so a benefactor's claim rests on his virtue, not on the fact that you were the one he helped. He did not say care is optional: he said a parent has no special claim to it. Applying this to ageing parents is our step, and the objection is the one most of his readers raised, that a morality giving your own mother no more claim on you than a worthy stranger asks for feelings almost no one has.
detail.zh: 葛德文论证正义必须不偏不倚，所以施恩者的要求取决于他的德性，而不取决于受益的恰好是你。他并没有说照顾可有可无，他说的是父母对照顾没有特殊的要求。把它用到年迈父母身上，是我们的推论；反驳则是他的大多数读者都提过的：一种让亲生母亲对你的要求不多于一位可敬陌生人的道德，要求的是几乎没有人具备的情感。

quote.en: When he first subjected himself to the necessity of these cares, he was probably influenced by no particular motives of benevolence to his future offspring.
quote.zh: When he first subjected himself to the necessity of these cares, he was probably influenced by no particular motives of benevolence to his future offspring.

label.en: William Godwin, An Enquiry Concerning Political Justice, Book II, ch. II
label.zh: 葛德文《政治正义论》第二卷第二章

claim.en: I wrote that the child does not owe the parent: parental duty is a gift, not a loan. A parent who has won a child's love will find the child wants to care for them in illness and old age, but that is love answering love, not a debt being collected.
claim.zh: 我写道，孩子并不亏欠父母：父母的责任是一份馈赠，而不是一笔借款。赢得了孩子爱戴的父母，会发现孩子愿意在他们生病和年老时照顾他们，但那是爱对爱的回应，而不是讨债。

detail.en: Gilman was writing against parents who claimed a grown daughter's life as repayment for having raised her; applying it to elder care today is our step. The objection: if care follows only from love that was won, a parent who did their best and still was not loved, or who needs care no one feels moved to give, is left with no claim at all.
detail.zh: 吉尔曼反对的是那些把成年女儿的一生当作养育回报来索取的父母；把它用到今天的养老问题上，是我们的推论。反驳是：如果照顾只来自被赢得的爱，那么一个尽了力却没有被爱的父母，或者需要照顾却没有人愿意付出的父母，就什么要求也没有了。

quote.en: The child does not owe the parent. Parental duty is not a loan.
quote.zh: The child does not owe the parent. Parental duty is not a loan.

label.en: Charlotte Perkins Gilman, Concerning Children
label.zh: 吉尔曼《关于孩子》

claim.en: I argued that society may not protect an adult from himself, but I said plainly that this was never meant for children. Below the age the law fixes, the young must be guarded against their own actions as well as against harm from outside.
claim.zh: 我主张社会无权替成年人防着他自己，但我说得很清楚：这条原则从来不适用于孩子。在法律规定的年龄之前，年轻人既要防外来的伤害，也要防他们自己的行为。

detail.en: This is the exception Mill wrote into the first chapter of On Liberty, before the famous principle could be misread. Reading it as support for an age line on phones is our step, not his. The strongest objection comes from the same book: Mill argued that judgement grows only by being used in real choices, so a child shielded from every choice until sixteen may arrive there unpractised.
detail.zh: 这是密尔在《论自由》第一章里预先写下的例外，免得那条著名原则被误读。把它读成支持手机年龄线，是我们的推演，不是他的。最有力的反驳来自同一本书：密尔认为判断力只有在真实的选择中使用才会长成，一个直到十六岁都被挡在一切选择之外的孩子，到那天可能毫无练习。

quote.en: We are not speaking of children, or of young persons below the age which the law may fix as that of manhood or womanhood. Those who are still in a state to require being taken care of by others, must be protected against their own actions as well as against external injury.
quote.zh: We are not speaking of children, or of young persons below the age which the law may fix as that of manhood or womanhood. Those who are still in a state to require being taken care of by others, must be protected against their own actions as well as against external injury.

label.en: John Stuart Mill, On Liberty, Chapter I
label.zh: 约翰·斯图亚特·密尔《论自由》第一章

claim.en: I argued that ideas joined together often in a child's mind can stay joined for life. A maid who ties goblins to the dark may leave a child who can never again bear the dark.
claim.zh: 我认为，在孩子心里被反复连在一起的观念，可能一辈子都分不开。一个把妖怪和黑暗绑在一起讲的女仆，可能让孩子从此再也受不了黑暗。

detail.en: Locke's chapter on the association of ideas is about how early, repeated pairings outlast reason; it says nothing about devices, and drawing a wait-until-sixteen rule from it is our step. The objection is in his own example: the harm came from what an adult kept putting into the child's mind, not from the dark itself, which argues for watching the content more than for keeping the child out.
detail.zh: 洛克论观念联合的这一章讲的是：早年反复的配对，比理性更持久；它没有谈任何器物，从中推出等到十六岁的规则，是我们的推演。反驳就在他自己的例子里：伤害来自一个大人反复往孩子心里灌的东西，而不是黑暗本身——这更支持看住内容，而不是把孩子挡在外面。

quote.en: The ideas of goblins and sprites have really no more to do with darkness than light: yet let but a foolish maid inculcate these often on the mind of a child, and raise them there together, possibly he shall never be able to separate them again so long as he lives
quote.zh: The ideas of goblins and sprites have really no more to do with darkness than light: yet let but a foolish maid inculcate these often on the mind of a child, and raise them there together, possibly he shall never be able to separate them again so long as he lives

label.en: Locke, An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, II.33.10
label.zh: 洛克《人类理解论》第二卷第 33 章第 10 节

claim.en: I held that the beginning matters most with anything young and tender, because that is when character is formed and impressions take. So the stories children hear should be chosen for them, and most of the ones in circulation set aside.
claim.zh: 我认为，对一切幼嫩的东西，开头最要紧，因为品格正是在那时成形、印记最容易留下。所以孩子听的故事应当由人替他们挑选，流行的那些大多要放下。

detail.en: Socrates speaks these lines in the Republic, as Plato's spokesman, while designing the education of a city's guardians. Treating it as a case for adult-set limits on a phone is our step. Its weakness is who does the choosing: Plato's limits are a censorship run by the state, and the same argument that protects a child from bad stories hands someone the power to decide which stories are bad.
detail.zh: 这是《理想国》里苏格拉底作为柏拉图的代言人，在设计城邦护卫者的教育时说的。把它当作大人给手机设限的理由，是我们的推演。它的弱点在于由谁来挑：柏拉图的限制是由国家执行的审查，同一个保护孩子不听坏故事的论证，也把决定什么是坏故事的权力交到了某人手里。

quote.en: the beginning is the most important part of any work, especially in the case of a young and tender thing; for that is the time at which the character is being formed and the desired impression is more readily taken.
quote.zh: the beginning is the most important part of any work, especially in the case of a young and tender thing; for that is the time at which the character is being formed and the desired impression is more readily taken.

label.en: Plato, Republic, Book II (377a-b), trans. Benjamin Jowett
label.zh: 柏拉图《理想国》第二卷（377a-b），乔伊特 英译

claim.en: I argued that the first job of a school is to give the young a simplified environment, and the second is to weed out the unworthy features of the world around them. A society is full of the trivial and the perverse, and a child should not meet all of it at once.
claim.zh: 我认为，学校的第一件事是给年轻人一个简化的环境，第二件事是剔除周围世界中不值得的部分。一个社会里满是琐碎和反常的东西，孩子不该一下子全部撞上。

detail.en: Dewey is remembered for learning by doing, so it surprises people that he also asked adults to select and purify what the young encounter. He wrote this about schools in 1916; applying it to phones is our step. The objection is his own: he wanted that selected world to connect with life outside, and a filtered environment that never meets the real one can leave a child unready for it.
detail.zh: 人们记得杜威主张从做中学，所以会意外地发现，他也要求大人替年轻人挑选、净化他们接触的东西。他是在 1916 年就学校写下这些的；把它用到手机上，是我们的推演。反驳来自他自己：他要求那个被挑选过的世界与外面的生活相连，一个从不与真实世界相遇的过滤环境，可能让孩子对真实世界毫无准备。

quote.en: it is the business of the school environment to eliminate, so far as possible, the unworthy features of the existing environment from influence upon mental habitudes. It establishes a purified medium of action.
quote.zh: it is the business of the school environment to eliminate, so far as possible, the unworthy features of the existing environment from influence upon mental habitudes. It establishes a purified medium of action.

label.en: John Dewey, Democracy and Education, Chapter 2
label.zh: 杜威《民主与教育》第二章

claim.en: I agreed that a child should not be brought up in his mother's lap. Love too tender to let him meet hardships and hazards will not make him good for anything as a man.
claim.zh: 我同意，孩子不该在母亲膝上长大。温柔到不让他碰任何艰苦与危险的爱，不会把他养成一个有用的男人。

detail.en: Montaigne was writing about the education of a young nobleman, and the hazards he had in mind were cold drinks, unruly horses and fencing. Carrying that to phones is our step. The objection is that his boy was not left free: he was hardened under a tutor's close governance, which is exposure chosen by an adult, not a child's own unsupervised use.
detail.zh: 蒙田写的是一个年轻贵族的教育，他想到的危险是冷饮、烈马和击剑。把它搬到手机上，是我们的推演。反驳在于：他笔下的孩子并没有被放任，而是在导师的严密管教下被磨炼——那是大人选定的历练，而不是孩子自己无人看管的使用。

quote.en: Mothers are too tender, and their natural affection is apt to make the most discreet of them all so overfond, that they can neither find in their hearts to give them due correction for the faults they may commit, nor suffer them to be inured to hardships and hazards, as they ought to be.
quote.zh: Mothers are too tender, and their natural affection is apt to make the most discreet of them all so overfond, that they can neither find in their hearts to give them due correction for the faults they may commit, nor suffer them to be inured to hardships and hazards, as they ought to be.

label.en: Montaigne, Essays I, Of the Education of Children, trans. Charles Cotton
label.zh: 蒙田《随笔集》第一卷〈论儿童的教育〉，科顿 英译

claim.en: I argued that obedience teaches a child nothing. What matters is that the child builds a connected scheme of life for himself, his young faculties improving as he uses them, so that his conduct is his own and not forced on him from outside.
claim.zh: 我认为服从教不会孩子任何东西。要紧的是孩子自己建起一套连贯的生活方式，他幼小的能力在使用中变强，让他的行为是他自己的，而不是外力强加的。

detail.en: Concerning Children is an attack on training children by command; Gilman wanted them to reason their way to their own conduct. Applying that to phones is our step. The objection is that her method is far from hands-off: she has parents and trained educators arranging the causes and letting the child feel only the pleasant or not too painful effects, which is closer to adult-set limits than to free use.
detail.zh: 《关于孩子》是对以命令训练孩子的抨击；吉尔曼希望孩子靠推理走到自己的行为上。把它用到手机上，是我们的推演。反驳在于：她的方法远非放手不管——她让父母和受过训练的教育者安排好原因，只让孩子感受愉快或不太痛的后果，这更接近由大人设限，而不是自由使用。

quote.en: What is important is that the child shall gradually establish a rational and connected scheme of life and method of action, his young faculties improving as he uses them, life growing easier and plainer to him from year to year.
quote.zh: What is important is that the child shall gradually establish a rational and connected scheme of life and method of action, his young faculties improving as he uses them, life growing easier and plainer to him from year to year.

label.en: Charlotte Perkins Gilman, Concerning Children
label.zh: 吉尔曼《关于孩子》

claim.en: I argued that young children should spend their early years in harmless play, without minute direction or a nurse's constant watch. Looking after themselves is the first exercise of their understanding, and a child never left to its own direction, a girl above all, is made dependent.
claim.zh: 我认为幼小的孩子应当在无害的嬉戏中度过早年，不需要事事指点，也不需要保姆时时盯着。照料自己是他们理解力的第一次练习；一个从不被允许自己做主的孩子，尤其是女孩，就这样被养成了依赖。

detail.en: Wollstonecraft was arguing in 1792 that girls were kept weak by over-supervision passed off as tenderness. Extending that to screens is our step. The objection is that her case is about bodily play in the open, where the risks are scraped knees; a device that carries strangers and markets into a child's room is a different kind of hazard, and she wrote nothing about that.
detail.zh: 沃斯通克拉夫特在 1792 年论证：女孩被冒充温柔的过度看管弄得软弱。把这一点延伸到屏幕上，是我们的推演。反驳在于：她说的是户外的身体游戏，风险是擦破膝盖；一台把陌生人和市场带进孩子房间的设备，是另一种危险，她对此什么也没写。

quote.en: the infancy of children, conformable to this intimation, should be passed in harmless gambols, that exercise the feet and hands, without requiring very minute direction from the head, or the constant attention of a nurse.
quote.zh: the infancy of children, conformable to this intimation, should be passed in harmless gambols, that exercise the feet and hands, without requiring very minute direction from the head, or the constant attention of a nurse.

label.en: Mary Wollstonecraft, A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
label.zh: 沃斯通克拉夫特《女权辩护》

claim.en: I argued that marriage was corrupted by a wife's economic dependence on her husband. Once women earn their own living, money and comfort drop out of the choice, and men and women can meet on love alone.
claim.zh: 我认为，婚姻被妻子在经济上对丈夫的依附败坏了。一旦女性能自己谋生，金钱和安逸就会从选择中退出，男女便可以只凭爱情相会。

detail.en: Women and Economics is a critique of the 1890s household, written partly as a prediction; reading it as a verdict on marrying for love today is our step. The strongest objection is that love freed from every practical tie may also find it easier to leave, so purer motives need not mean longer marriages.
detail.zh: 《妇女与经济》是对 1890 年代家庭的批判，部分写成了预言；把它读作对今天为爱结婚的判断，是我们自己迈出的一步。最有力的反驳是：摆脱了一切现实纽带的爱，也可能更容易离开，动机更纯并不等于婚姻更久。

quote.en: In reality, we may hope that the most valuable effect of this change in the basis of living will be the cleansing of love and marriage from this base admixture of pecuniary interest and creature comfort
quote.zh: In reality, we may hope that the most valuable effect of this change in the basis of living will be the cleansing of love and marriage from this base admixture of pecuniary interest and creature comfort

label.en: Charlotte Perkins Gilman, Women and Economics
label.zh: 吉尔曼《妇女与经济》

claim.en: I wrote against the prudence that presides at weddings with one eye on the cellar. Love, the enchantment of one person for another, is what founds a marriage, and teaching girls that marriage means only thrift withers the best hope in them.
claim.zh: 我批评那种在婚礼上一只眼睛还盯着地窖的精明算计。爱情，即一个人对另一个人的倾心，才是婚姻的根基；教导女孩说婚姻不过是持家节俭，会让她们心中最好的希望枯萎。

detail.en: The essay Love treats romance as the first step of the soul toward a larger, less personal love; using it to vote on the modern question is our step. Its weakness is that Emerson himself says the charms that first drew a couple together are deciduous, so love as he describes it cannot be what keeps a marriage standing.
detail.zh: 《爱》这篇随笔把浪漫之爱看作灵魂走向一种更大、更不私人的爱的第一步；用它来为这个现代问题投票，是我们自己的一步。它的弱点是：爱默生自己也说，最初吸引两人的魅力会像落叶一样凋谢，所以他所描述的爱情，撑不起一桩婚姻的长久。

quote.en: Worst, when this sensualism intrudes into the education of young women, and withers the hope and affection of human nature by teaching that marriage signifies nothing but a housewife’s thrift, and that woman’s life has no other aim.
quote.zh: Worst, when this sensualism intrudes into the education of young women, and withers the hope and affection of human nature by teaching that marriage signifies nothing but a housewife’s thrift, and that woman’s life has no other aim.

origin.zh: 马萨诸塞州康科德，1841 年

label.en: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Essays: First Series, Love
label.zh: 爱默生《随笔集·第一辑》〈爱〉

claim.en: I held that a good marriage, if there is one, keeps away from the conditions of love and imitates friendship instead: constancy, trust and a great many solid services owed to each other.
claim.zh: 我认为，一桩好的婚姻——如果真有的话——会避开爱情的条件，转而效仿友谊：恒久、信任，以及彼此承担的许多切实的照应。

detail.en: He wrote as a sixteenth-century nobleman in an arranged marriage, in an essay that is mostly about desire; applying his line to choosing a spouse today is our step. The strongest objection is that a marriage built to exclude passion may simply send passion elsewhere, which his own essay half admits.
detail.zh: 他写这些时是一位婚姻由家族安排的十六世纪贵族，而那篇随笔大半在谈欲望；把这句话用到今天的择偶上，是我们自己的一步。最有力的反驳是：一桩刻意排除激情的婚姻，可能只是把激情推到了别处，而他自己的文章也半承认了这一点。

quote.en: A good marriage, if there be any such, rejects the company and conditions of love, and tries to represent those of friendship.
quote.zh: A good marriage, if there be any such, rejects the company and conditions of love, and tries to represent those of friendship.

label.en: Michel de Montaigne, Essays, Book III, ch. 5, Upon Some Verses of Virgil, trans. Charles Cotton
label.zh: 蒙田《随笔集》第三卷第五章〈论维吉尔的几句诗〉，科顿 英译

claim.en: I argued that even for two good young people it might be a blessing if something cooled their passion when they married, so the match rested on esteem. Then they would plan a friendship for the whole of life instead of living for the moment.
claim.zh: 我认为，即便是两个品行端正的年轻人结婚，若有什么事让他们的激情稍稍冷却，使这桩婚事建立在敬重之上，或许反倒是幸事。那样他们会为一生规划一段友谊，而不是只活在眼前。

detail.en: The Vindication is mainly an argument that women be educated as rational beings, and this passage attacks the advice that wives should keep a husband's passion alive by art; carrying it to a modern choice of partner is our step. The objection is pointed: she later fell passionately in love herself, and a marriage that starts by hoping passion is checked may never find out what it was worth.
detail.zh: 《女权辩护》主要论证女性应当作为有理性的人受教育，这段话针对的是那种教妻子用手段维持丈夫激情的劝告；把它搬到今天的择偶上，是我们自己的一步。反驳很尖锐：她自己后来也曾热烈地坠入爱河，而一桩一开始就希望激情被抑制的婚姻，也许永远不会知道那份激情本来值多少。

quote.en: Personal attachment is a very happy foundation for friendship; yet, when even two virtuous young people marry, it would, perhaps, be happy if some circumstance checked their passion
quote.zh: Personal attachment is a very happy foundation for friendship; yet, when even two virtuous young people marry, it would, perhaps, be happy if some circumstance checked their passion

label.en: Mary Wollstonecraft, A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
label.zh: 沃斯通克拉夫特《女权辩护》

claim.en: I held that marriage agrees with reason when desire does not come from bodily beauty alone, but also from wanting to raise children wisely, and when each loves the other for freedom of mind and not looks only. Love caused by anything else, I said, easily turns into hatred.
claim.zh: 我认为，婚姻若要合乎理性，欲望就不能只出自身体的美貌，还要出自好好养育孩子的愿望；双方相爱也不能只因容貌，还要因对方心灵的自由。出于别的原因的爱，我说过，很容易转为恨。

detail.en: These are short rules in the appendix to Part IV of the Ethics, a book about living by reason; reading them as advice on whom to marry today is our step. The objection is that Spinoza never married, and his test of freedom of soul is one almost nobody can apply to another person before living with them.
detail.zh: 这些是《伦理学》第四部分附录中的简短条目，这本书讲的是依理性而生活；把它们读作今天择偶的建议，是我们自己的一步。反驳在于：斯宾诺莎终身未婚，而他所说的心灵自由这一标准，几乎没有人能在共同生活之前用来衡量另一个人。

quote.en: As concerning marriage, it is certain that this is in harmony with reason, if the desire for physical union be not engendered solely by bodily beauty, but also by the desire to beget children and to train them up wisely;
quote.zh: As concerning marriage, it is certain that this is in harmony with reason, if the desire for physical union be not engendered solely by bodily beauty, but also by the desire to beget children and to train them up wisely;

label.en: Baruch Spinoza, Ethics, Part IV, Appendix XX, trans. R. H. M. Elwes
label.zh: 斯宾诺莎《伦理学》第四部分附录第二十条，埃尔维斯 英译

claim.en: I argued that marriage as the law fixes it is a fraud and a form of property in another person, and that abolishing it would bring no evil. Two people should stay together exactly as long as both still choose to.
claim.zh: 我认为，法律所规定的婚姻是一种欺骗，是把另一个人当作财产，废除它不会带来任何恶果。两个人应当只在双方都仍愿意的时候在一起。

detail.en: Godwin attacked the indissoluble marriage of his day, not companionship itself, and expected free and lasting partnerships to replace it; matching this to the modern option is our step. The strongest objection came from his own life: a few years later he married Mary Wollstonecraft so that their child would not be born outside the law.
detail.zh: 葛德文攻击的是他那个时代不可解除的婚姻，而不是伴侣关系本身，他预期自由而持久的结合会取而代之；把它对应到这个现代选项，是我们自己的一步。最有力的反驳来自他本人：几年后，他为了不让孩子生在法律之外，与玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特结了婚。

quote.en: Add to this that marriage, as now understood, is a monopoly, and the worst of monopolies.
quote.zh: Add to this that marriage, as now understood, is a monopoly, and the worst of monopolies.

label.en: William Godwin, An Enquiry Concerning Political Justice
label.zh: 葛德文《政治正义论》

claim.en: I observed that a man with a wife and children has given hostages to fortune, and that the greatest public works have come from the unmarried and childless, who gave their affection and their means to the public instead.
claim.zh: 我观察到，有妻有子的人等于把人质交给了命运；最伟大、最有益于公众的事业，往往出自未婚或无子的人，他们把感情和财力都献给了公众。

detail.en: The essay weighs both sides: Bacon also says single men are often harder-hearted and that wives are companions for middle age, and he himself married. Treating it as a case against marrying at all is our step, and its weakness is plain, since it judges a life only by its public works.
detail.zh: 这篇随笔是两面权衡的：培根也说单身者往往心肠更硬，妻子是中年的伴侣，而他本人也结了婚。把它当作根本不该结婚的理由，是我们自己的一步；它的弱点也很明显，因为它只按公共功业来衡量一个人的一生。

quote.en: Certainly the best works, and of greatest merit for the public, have proceeded from the unmarried or childless men; which both in affection and means, have married and endowed the public.
quote.zh: Certainly the best works, and of greatest merit for the public, have proceeded from the unmarried or childless men; which both in affection and means, have married and endowed the public.

label.en: Francis Bacon, Essays, Of Marriage and Single Life
label.zh: 培根《随笔集》〈论婚姻与独身〉

claim.en: I served as mayor of Bordeaux and kept the office at arm's length: the mayor and I were two. A man should lend himself to his work and give himself only to himself.
claim.zh: 我做过波尔多市长，却始终和这个职位保持距离：市长是市长，我是我。人可以把自己借给差事，但只应把自己交给自己。

detail.en: In this essay Montaigne argues that a man should lend himself to others and give himself only to himself. He meant public office, not a wage, and carrying it to a job taken for money is our step. The objection is that the separation takes a sturdy self to keep: most people slowly become what they spend their days doing, and Montaigne was rich enough that no office could own him.
detail.zh: 蒙田在这篇随笔里主张：人可以把自己借给别人，却只应把自己交给自己。他说的是公职，不是工资；把它用到为钱而接的工作上，是我们的引申。最有力的反驳是：这种分离需要一个很结实的自我才守得住。大多数人会慢慢变成自己每天在做的事，而蒙田本人足够富有，没有哪个职位能真正占有他。

quote.en: The Mayor of Bordeaux and Montaigne have ever been two by very manifest separation.
quote.zh: The Mayor of Bordeaux and Montaigne have ever been two by very manifest separation.

label.en: Montaigne, Essays, Book III, ch. 10, Of Managing the Will, trans. Charles Cotton
label.zh: 蒙田《随笔集》第三卷第十章〈论管理意志〉，科顿 英译

claim.en: I thought a philosopher who must earn his bread does better at some humble trade, polishing lenses or minding the door of a quiet museum, than at a post that claims his thinking. Work that asks little of the mind leaves the mind free.
claim.zh: 我认为，一个必须谋生的哲学家，与其去做占据他思想的职位，不如做些卑微的营生：磨镜片，或在冷清的博物馆门口收雨伞。对头脑要求不多的工作，反而让头脑自由。

detail.en: Santayana was writing about Harvard and the risk of turning philosophy into a profession; extending it to anyone with a dull, well-paid job is our step, and he says nothing about double pay. His humble trades are quiet and light. The objection is that most meaningless jobs are neither: work that drains the day can take the free mind with it. He left teaching himself only after an inheritance made it possible.
detail.zh: 桑塔亚那写的是哈佛，以及把哲学变成职业的危险；把它推到任何一份乏味而高薪的工作上，是我们的引申，他也完全没谈薪水翻倍。他举的那些卑微营生安静而轻松。反驳在于：大多数无意义的工作两样都不是，耗尽一整天的工作，也会把自由的头脑一并耗掉。而他本人也是在一笔遗产让他有了余裕之后，才辞去教职的。

quote.en: If philosophers must earn their living and not beg (which some of them have thought more consonant with their vocation), it would be safer for them to polish lenses like Spinoza, or to sit in a black skull‐cap and white beard at the door of some unfrequented museum, selling the catalogues and taking in the umbrellas
quote.zh: If philosophers must earn their living and not beg (which some of them have thought more consonant with their vocation), it would be safer for them to polish lenses like Spinoza, or to sit in a black skull‐cap and white beard at the door of some unfrequented museum, selling the catalogues and taking in the umbrellas

label.en: George Santayana, Character and Opinion in the United States, ch. 1
label.zh: 乔治·桑塔亚那《美国的性格与见解》第一章

claim.en: I described the poor man's son who labours night and day for a future ease, and gives up for it a real tranquillity that was always in his power. In old age he finds that wealth and greatness are trinkets of frivolous utility.
claim.zh: 我描写过一个穷人家的儿子：他日夜操劳，为的是将来的安逸，却为此牺牲了一份始终握在自己手里的真正的宁静。到了晚年，他才发现财富与显赫不过是些用处轻微的小玩意。

detail.en: This is from Smith's book on moral feeling, not The Wealth of Nations, and it is about ambition; reading it against a well-paid job is our step. The strongest objection is Smith's own. Later in the same chapter, in the passage where his invisible hand appears, he argues that this very deception is what keeps the industry of mankind in motion: bad for the man, good for the world.
detail.zh: 这段出自斯密谈道德情感的书，而不是《国富论》，谈的是野心；拿它来衡量一份高薪工作，是我们的引申。最有力的反驳来自斯密自己：就在同一章稍后，在看不见的手出现的那段里，他论证正是这种自我欺骗，推动着人类的勤劳。对个人是坏事，对世界却是好事。

quote.en: Through the whole of his life he pursues the idea of a certain artificial and elegant repose which he may never arrive at, for which he sacrifices a real tranquillity that is at all times in his power
quote.zh: Through the whole of his life he pursues the idea of a certain artificial and elegant repose which he may never arrive at, for which he sacrifices a real tranquillity that is at all times in his power

label.en: Adam Smith, The Theory of Moral Sentiments, Part IV, ch. 1
label.zh: 亚当·斯密《道德情操论》第四卷第一章

claim.en: I held that spending the best part of life earning money, to enjoy a doubtful liberty in the least valuable part of it, is a bad bargain. The man who means to be a poet later should climb to his garret now.
claim.zh: 我认为，用一生中最好的时光去挣钱，好在最不值钱的那段时光里享受一点可疑的自由，是笔糟糕的买卖。打算以后当诗人的人，现在就该爬上阁楼。

detail.en: Walden opens with this accounting of what a life costs; Thoreau was addressing his Concord neighbours, and applying it to a modern salary is our step. The objection is that his experiment was cheap because it was short and cushioned: he built on land Emerson owned, walked into the village often, stayed two years, and had no one depending on his income.
detail.zh: 《瓦尔登湖》开篇就是这样一笔人生的账；梭罗是对康科德的邻居们说的，把它用到今天的薪水上，是我们的引申。反驳在于：他的实验之所以便宜，是因为短暂而有依靠。他在爱默生的地上盖房，常常走回镇上，只住了两年，也没有任何人靠他的收入生活。

quote.en: This spending of the best part of one’s life earning money in order to enjoy a questionable liberty during the least valuable part of it, reminds me of the Englishman who went to India to make a fortune first, in order that he might return to England and live the life of a poet.
quote.zh: This spending of the best part of one’s life earning money in order to enjoy a questionable liberty during the least valuable part of it, reminds me of the Englishman who went to India to make a fortune first, in order that he might return to England and live the life of a poet.

origin.zh: 马萨诸塞州康科德，1854 年

label.en: Henry David Thoreau, Walden, ch. 1, Economy
label.zh: 梭罗《瓦尔登湖》第一章〈经济〉

claim.en: I argued that manufacture breaks a craft into detail tasks and fixes each worker to one of them. It makes him a crippled monstrosity: one narrow knack forced at the expense of all his other powers.
claim.zh: 我论证过：工场手工业把一门手艺拆成零碎的局部操作，把每个工人钉死在其中一项上，把他变成畸形的怪物：一项狭窄的熟练被强行发展，代价是他其余的一切能力。

detail.en: Capital describes the workshop division of labour of Marx's time, and for him the fault lay in the system, not in a worker's choice; treating it as advice about which job to take is our step. The objection is that his remedy was collective, not personal: on his own account, refusing one meaningless post changes nothing, and the worker who refuses must still sell his hours to someone.
detail.zh: 《资本论》描写的是马克思那个时代工场里的分工，在他看来，错在制度，不在工人的选择；把它当成择业建议，是我们的引申。反驳在于：他的出路是集体的，不是个人的。按他自己的分析，拒绝一份无意义的工作什么也改变不了，拒绝的人仍然得把自己的时间卖给某个人。

quote.en: It converts the labourer into a crippled monstrosity, by forcing his detail dexterity at the expense of a world of productive capabilities and instincts
quote.zh: It converts the labourer into a crippled monstrosity, by forcing his detail dexterity at the expense of a world of productive capabilities and instincts

label.en: Karl Marx, Capital, Volume I, ch. 14, trans. Samuel Moore and Edward Aveling
label.zh: 卡尔·马克思《资本论》第一卷第十四章，穆尔、艾威林 英译

claim.en: I called riches the baggage of virtue: they cannot be left behind, but they hinder the march. Great riches have no real use except in their distribution; the rest is vanity.
claim.zh: 我把财富称作美德的辎重：丢不下，却拖慢行军。巨额财富除了分出去，没有真正的用处；其余都是虚荣。

detail.en: Of Riches is advice to men of means, and it ends by urging riches gotten justly and distributed cheerfully; reading it as a case for taking a job in order to give is our step. The objection sits in Bacon's own life: as Lord Chancellor he was convicted in 1621 of taking bribes, and he died in debt. The distribution he praised was easier to write than to practise.
detail.zh: 〈论财富〉是写给有产者的劝告，结尾劝人取之有道、乐于散财；把它读成为了捐赠而接一份工作的理由，是我们的引申。反驳就在培根自己身上：他身为大法官，1621 年被判受贿，死时负债累累。他称赞的散财，写起来比做起来容易。

quote.en: Of great riches there is no real use, except it be in the distribution; the rest is but conceit.
quote.zh: Of great riches there is no real use, except it be in the distribution; the rest is but conceit.

label.en: Francis Bacon, Essays, Of Riches
label.zh: 培根《随笔集》〈论财富〉

claim.en: I argued that the good things of the world are a common stock. What a man holds beyond his need belongs in justice to whoever it would benefit most, and handing it over is paying a debt, not being generous.
claim.zh: 我论证过：世上的好东西是一份共同的储备。一个人超出所需的部分，按正义属于最能从中受益的人；把它交出去是还债，不是慷慨。

detail.en: Political Justice argues for property held according to need, and complains that religion taught the rich to treat giving as bounty rather than debt. Applying it to a pay rise is our step. The objection his critics pressed from the start: if the surplus is never yours, the motive to earn it may go, and Godwin's answer, that people would work from reason and benevolence, remains a hope rather than a finding.
detail.zh: 《政治正义论》主张财产应按需要归属，并批评宗教让富人把施与当作恩赐，而不是债务。把它用到一次加薪上，是我们的引申。他的批评者从一开始就提出的反驳是：如果多出来的钱从来不属于你，挣它的动力可能就没了；葛德文的回答是人会出于理性与仁爱而劳动，但这至今仍是一个希望，而不是一个结论。

quote.en: Hence it follows, upon the principles of equal and impartial justice, that the good things of the world are a common stock, upon which one man has as valid a title as another to draw for what he wants.
quote.zh: Hence it follows, upon the principles of equal and impartial justice, that the good things of the world are a common stock, upon which one man has as valid a title as another to draw for what he wants.

label.en: William Godwin, An Enquiry Concerning Political Justice, Book VIII
label.zh: 葛德文《政治正义论》第八卷

claim.en: I argued that a person reaches back as far as his consciousness of his past acts reaches: whatever he can remember doing, he is the same self that did it. On that sameness rests all the justice of reward and punishment.
claim.zh: 我论证过：一个人的意识能回溯到多远，这个人就延伸到多远；凡是他能记起是自己做过的事，他就是做那件事的同一个自我。奖赏与惩罚的全部正当性，就建立在这种同一上。

detail.en: Locke's chapter on identity was added to the second edition of the Essay to settle who answers for past acts; bringing it to old posts is our step. It cuts more ways than option A wants: on Locke's account, what someone has truly forgotten is not theirs. And Thomas Reid objected that memory makes a broken chain: an old general may remember his days as an officer, and the officer a flogging as a boy, while the general has forgotten the boy.
detail.zh: 洛克这一章是在《人类理解论》第二版中补入的，为的是厘清谁要为过去的行为负责；把它用到旧帖子上，是我们的引申。它的锋芒不只指向一边：按洛克的说法，一个人真正遗忘了的事，就不再属于他。托马斯·里德还提出过反驳：记忆是一条会断的链。老将军记得自己当军官的日子，军官记得小时候挨过的鞭打，可将军早已忘了那个孩子。

quote.en: In this personal identity is founded all the right and justice of reward and punishment
quote.zh: In this personal identity is founded all the right and justice of reward and punishment

label.en: John Locke, An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, Book II, ch. 27
label.zh: 洛克《人类理解论》第二卷第二十七章

claim.en: I wrote that every smallest act of virtue or vice leaves its scar. The drunkard may tell himself this one will not count, but down among his nerve-cells it is being counted, and nothing we do is ever wiped out.
claim.zh: 我写过：每一个微小的善行或恶行都会留下疤痕。酒鬼可以对自己说这一次不算，但在他的神经细胞里，这一次正被记下；我们做过的事，没有一件会被抹去。

detail.en: The passage comes from James's chapter on habit, a claim about how character is built from repeated acts, not about blame; using it to say an old act still belongs to someone is our step. And it cuts both ways, as James says in the next sentence: the same counting that makes a drunkard by separate drinks makes a saint by separate good acts, so ten years of different conduct are counted too.
detail.zh: 这段出自詹姆斯论习惯的一章，讲的是性格如何由反复的行为塑成，而不是讲责备；用它来说旧行为仍属于某人，是我们的引申。而且它两头都切，詹姆斯在下一句就说了：同样的累积，让人一杯一杯地成了酒鬼，也让人一件一件善行地成了圣徒。十年来不同的作为，同样被记了下来。

quote.en: Nothing we ever do is, in strict scientific literalness, wiped out.
quote.zh: Nothing we ever do is, in strict scientific literalness, wiped out.

label.en: William James, The Principles of Psychology, Volume 1, ch. 4, Habit
label.zh: 威廉·詹姆斯《心理学原理》第一卷第四章〈习惯〉

claim.en: I argued that actions make a person blameworthy only as signs of a lasting character. That is why repentance wipes off a crime, above all when a visible reform of life follows it.
claim.zh: 我论证过：行为之所以使人应受责备，只因为它们是某种持久品格的证据。所以悔过能洗去罪行，尤其是伴随着明显的生活改变时。

detail.en: Hume uses repentance in his discussion of liberty and necessity, to show that blame attaches to settled character rather than to bare acts; applying it to old posts is our step. His reasoning sits close to option C: what counts is the present character, and repentance is evidence of it. The objection is evidential: repentance is easy to perform and hard to check, and Hume asks for an evident reform, which an apology alone does not show.
detail.zh: 休谟是在讨论自由与必然时谈到悔过的，用来说明责备针对的是稳定的品格，而不是孤立的行为；把它用到旧帖子上，是我们的引申。他的推理其实很接近选项 C：要紧的是现在的品格，悔过只是它的证据。反驳在于证据：悔过容易表演、难以核实，而休谟要求的是明显的改变，一份道歉本身证明不了这一点。

quote.en: Again, repentance wipes off every crime, especially if attended with an evident reformation of life and manners.
quote.zh: Again, repentance wipes off every crime, especially if attended with an evident reformation of life and manners.

label.en: David Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, Book II, Part III, Section II
label.zh: 大卫·休谟《人性论》第二卷第三部分第二节

claim.en: I wrote out my past sins for others to read, because the good rejoice to hear of evils a person has been freed from: not because they were evils, but because they were, and are no more.
claim.zh: 我把过去的罪写出来给人看，因为善良的人乐于听到一个人已经摆脱的恶：不是因为那是恶，而是因为它们曾经存在，如今已不在了。

detail.en: The Confessions is a book-length owning of a past; in Book X Augustine asks why he publishes it, and this is part of his answer. Carrying it to old posts is our step. The objection is that for Augustine the freeing is God's forgiveness, not the readers' verdict, and he concedes in the same chapter that readers cannot see into his heart, so they cannot check that the change is real.
detail.zh: 《忏悔录》整本书就是对过去的认领；在第十卷里，奥古斯丁自问为什么要把它公之于众，这是他回答的一部分。把它用到旧帖子上，是我们的引申。反驳在于：对奥古斯丁来说，使人摆脱罪的是上帝的宽恕，不是读者的裁决；他在同一章里也承认，读者看不进他的心，因而无从核实这种改变是否真实。

quote.en: And the good delight to hear of the past evils of such as are now freed from them, not because they are evils, but because they have been and are not.
quote.zh: And the good delight to hear of the past evils of such as are now freed from them, not because they are evils, but because they have been and are not.

label.en: Augustine, Confessions, Book X, ch. 3, trans. E. B. Pusey
label.zh: 奥古斯丁《忏悔录》第十卷第三章，普西 英译

claim.en: I distrusted those who profess great remorse and show no amendment. If repentance does not cure the life it is no cure at all; real repentance, laid on the scale, would outweigh the sin.
claim.zh: 我不相信那些自称深深懊悔、却看不出任何改正的人。悔恨若治不好生活，就根本不算治疗；真正的悔恨放上天平，会比罪更重。

detail.en: In Of Repentance Montaigne is hard on penitents who profess grief and change nothing, and he says that disliking what one is by nature is not repentance at all, only regret. Reading it as a test for owning an old post is our step. The objection is that his standard, a repentance that must sting through and through, is so strict that almost no one could show they have met it, which leaves option B close to A in practice.
detail.zh: 在〈论悔恨〉里，蒙田对那些口称悲痛、却毫无改变的忏悔者毫不客气；他还说，不喜欢自己天生的样子并不是悔恨，只是遗憾。把它读成认领旧帖子的标准，是我们的引申。反驳在于：他的标准太严，悔恨必须刺透全身，几乎没有人能证明自己做到了，这让选项 B 在实际上和 A 相差无几。

quote.en: It cannot be a cure if the malady be not wholly discharged; if repentance were laid upon the scale of the balance, it would weigh down sin.
quote.zh: It cannot be a cure if the malady be not wholly discharged; if repentance were laid upon the scale of the balance, it would weigh down sin.

label.en: Montaigne, Essays, Book III, ch. 2, Of Repentance, trans. Charles Cotton
label.zh: 蒙田《随笔集》第三卷第二章〈论悔恨〉，科顿 英译

claim.en: I wrote that an opinion we once loved and now call an error was as necessary to us then, when we were another person, as our present truths are now. We are always another person; our new life, not our reason, kills the old opinion.
claim.zh: 我写过：一个我们曾经珍爱、如今称为错误的看法，对那时的我们来说，就像现在的真理对现在的我们一样必要。那时我们是另一个人，而我们永远是另一个人；杀死旧看法的，是新的生活，不是理性。

detail.en: Section 307 is about one's own past beliefs and the vanity of thinking reason defeated them; it says nothing about judging others, and that step is ours. The objection is that if each of us is always another person, no one is answerable for anything, including the self who wrote yesterday's apology. Nietzsche is describing how opinions die, not laying down a rule of forgiveness.
detail.zh: 第 307 节谈的是一个人自己过去的信念，以及以为是理性战胜了它们的虚妄；它完全没有谈如何评判别人，这一步是我们走的。反驳在于：如果每个人永远是另一个人，那就没有人需要为任何事负责，包括昨天写下道歉的那个自己。尼采描述的是看法如何死去，并不是在立一条宽恕的规矩。

quote.en: But perhaps that error was then, when thou wast still another person—thou art always another person,—just as necessary to thee as all thy present "truths," like a skin, as it were, which concealed and veiled from thee much which thou still mayst not see.
quote.zh: But perhaps that error was then, when thou wast still another person—thou art always another person,—just as necessary to thee as all thy present "truths," like a skin, as it were, which concealed and veiled from thee much which thou still mayst not see.

label.en: Friedrich Nietzsche, The Joyful Wisdom, §307, trans. Thomas Common
label.zh: 弗里德里希·尼采《快乐的科学》第 307 节，康芒 英译

claim.en: I set it down as a law of nature that in revenge men look not at the greatness of the evil past but at the good to follow. Punishment for any purpose other than correcting the offender or guiding others is forbidden.
claim.zh: 我把它列为一条自然法：报复时，人们不应看过去的恶有多大，而应看将来的善有多大。除了矫正犯错者、警示他人，任何其他目的的惩罚都是被禁止的。

detail.en: These are the sixth and seventh laws of nature in Leviathan: pardon those who repent and give assurance for the future, and punish only for what punishment can still do. Applying them to old posts is our step. The objection is that the rule still allows punishment as a lesson to others, which is exactly what making an example of an old post claims to be; and Hobbes meant the sovereign, not a crowd, to do the judging.
detail.zh: 这是《利维坦》中的第六和第七条自然法：宽恕那些悔改并对将来作出保证的人；惩罚只为惩罚还能起的作用。把它们用到旧帖子上，是我们的引申。反驳在于：这条规则仍然允许以儆效尤的惩罚，而拿一条旧帖子开刀，声称的恰恰就是这个；况且霍布斯设想的裁判者是主权者，不是人群。

quote.en: Whereby we are forbidden to inflict punishment with any other design, than for correction of the offender, or direction of others.
quote.zh: Whereby we are forbidden to inflict punishment with any other design, than for correction of the offender, or direction of others.

label.en: Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan, ch. XV, in The English Works, vol. III, ed. William Molesworth
label.zh: 霍布斯《利维坦》第十五章，收于莫尔斯沃思编《霍布斯英文著作集》第三卷

claim.en: In the Laws my Athenian lawgiver urges every citizen to cling to immortality by leaving children's children to serve the gods in his place, and fines any man still unmarried at thirty-five.
claim.zh: 在《法篇》里，我笔下的雅典立法者劝告每个公民，要通过留下子孙、让他们代替自己侍奉神明来把握不朽，并对三十五岁仍未结婚的男子处以罚款。

detail.en: The speaker is the unnamed Athenian Stranger, Plato's spokesman in his last dialogue, drafting laws for an imagined colony; the duty is owed to the gods and the city, not to humanity at large. Applying it to people deciding today is our step. The objection: the duty is enforced by the state, with fines and public dishonour, and few who call childlessness selfish would accept that machinery.
detail.zh: 说话的是那位无名的雅典客人，他是柏拉图在最后一部对话中的代言人，正为一个设想中的殖民城邦起草法律；这份义务是对神明和城邦的，不是对全人类的。把它用到今天做决定的人身上，是我们的推论。反驳是：这份义务由城邦用罚款和公开的羞辱来强制执行，而说不要孩子是自私的人，很少会接受这套机制。

quote.en: a man should cling to immortality, and leave behind him children's children to be the servants of God in his place for ever.
quote.zh: a man should cling to immortality, and leave behind him children's children to be the servants of God in his place for ever.

label.en: Plato, Laws, Book VI, trans. Benjamin Jowett
label.zh: 柏拉图《法篇》第六卷，乔伊特 英译

claim.en: I told my students that philosophy is an inn to pass through, not to stay in. Their purpose was to go home, do the duties of a citizen, marry, beget children and hold the usual offices.
claim.zh: 我告诉学生，哲学是一家用来路过、而不是用来久住的客栈。他们的目的是回到家乡，尽公民的义务，结婚，生儿育女，担任通常的公职。
