detail.en: The passage warns students not to linger in clever argument, and marriage and children appear as ordinary duties of a citizen's life rather than as its subject. Treating them as an answer about choosing not to have children is our step. The objection: Epictetus also held that a true Cynic, serving everyone, might rightly stay unmarried, so even he did not think the duty bound every life.
detail.zh: 这段话告诫学生不要沉溺于巧妙的论辩，婚姻和子女是作为公民生活中寻常的义务出现的，而不是这段话的主题。把它当作关于选择不要孩子的回答，是我们的推论。反驳是：爱比克泰德也认为，一位服务所有人的真正犬儒者可以正当地不结婚，所以就连他也不认为这份义务约束每一种人生。

quote.en: But your purpose is this, to return to your country, to relieve your kinsmen of anxiety, to discharge the duties of a citizen, to marry, to beget children, to fill the usual magistracies.
quote.zh: But your purpose is this, to return to your country, to relieve your kinsmen of anxiety, to discharge the duties of a citizen, to marry, to beget children, to fill the usual magistracies.

origin.zh: 尼科波利斯，约公元 125 年

label.en: Epictetus, Discourses, trans. George Long
label.zh: 爱比克泰德《论说集》，朗 英译

claim.en: I observed that the noblest works and foundations have come from childless men, who expressed the images of their minds where those of their bodies failed, so that care for posterity runs highest in those who have none. In the same essay I wrote that children sweeten labours.
claim.zh: 我注意到，最高贵的作品和事业，往往出自没有子女的人，他们在身体的形象无以延续之处，表达了心灵的形象；所以最关心后世的，恰恰是没有后代的人。在同一篇随笔里，我也写道，孩子让劳苦变得甜美。

detail.en: His essay on parents and children weighs both sides: children sweeten labour and soften the thought of death, and they make misfortune more bitter. Using it to answer the charge of selfishness is our step. The objection: a handful of founders of colleges and states does not show that the ordinary childless life is more public-spirited, and in another essay Bacon grants that many choose a single life for their own liberty.
detail.zh: 他谈父母与子女的随笔是在权衡两方面：孩子让劳苦变甜、让人对死亡的念头变得柔和，也让不幸变得更苦。用它来回应自私的指责，是我们的推论。反驳是：少数学院和国家的创立者，并不能证明寻常的无子女生活更有公心；而且培根在另一篇随笔里也承认，许多人选择独身是为了自己的自由。

quote.en: And surely a man shall see the noblest works and foundations have proceeded from childless men; which have sought to express the images of their minds, where those of their bodies have failed.
quote.zh: And surely a man shall see the noblest works and foundations have proceeded from childless men; which have sought to express the images of their minds, where those of their bodies have failed.

label.en: Francis Bacon, Essays, Of Parents and Children
label.zh: 培根《随笔集》〈论父母与子女〉

claim.en: I was a father myself, and still I held that what we engender by the soul, our understanding, courage and abilities, comes from nobler parts than the body and is more truly our own. In that generation we are both father and mother.
claim.zh: 我自己也是父亲，但我仍然认为，我们用心灵孕育的东西，即我们的理解、勇气和才能，出自比身体更高贵的部分，也更真正属于我们自己。在这种生育里，我们既是父亲，也是母亲。

detail.en: The point comes in his essay on the affection of fathers, as a reason to love one's books and works no less than one's children; he never says anyone should forgo children. Using it against the charge of selfishness is our step. The objection: books are not dependants, and calling them children borrows the dignity of parenthood without any of its obligations.
detail.zh: 这一点出现在他谈父亲之爱的随笔里，用来说明人应当像爱孩子一样爱自己的书和作品；他从没有说谁应该不要孩子。用它来反驳自私的指责，是我们的推论。反驳是：书不需要人抚养，把它们称作孩子，是借用了为人父母的尊严，却不承担任何责任。

quote.en: that which we engender by the soul, the issue of our understanding, courage, and abilities, springs from nobler parts than those of the body, and that are much more our own: we are both father and mother in this generation.
quote.zh: that which we engender by the soul, the issue of our understanding, courage, and abilities, springs from nobler parts than those of the body, and that are much more our own: we are both father and mother in this generation.

label.en: Michel de Montaigne, Essays, Book II, ch. 8, trans. Charles Cotton
label.zh: 蒙田《随笔集》第二卷第八章，科顿 英译

claim.en: I argued that causing a human being to exist is one of the most responsible acts in life, and that doing it without a fair prospect of a desirable existence for the child is a crime against that child.
claim.zh: 我认为，使一个人来到世上，是人生中责任最重大的行为之一；如果孩子没有过上像样生活的合理前景，这样做就是对那个孩子的犯罪。

detail.en: Mill was arguing in On Liberty that misplaced ideas of freedom stop people from recognising what parents owe, and he defended laws forbidding marriage to those without means to support a family. Applying it to the charge of selfishness is our step. The objection: his test is about prospects and means, so it condemns careless parenthood, not parenthood itself, and a parent who can provide passes it easily.
detail.zh: 密尔在《论自由》中论证，错置的自由观念让人们看不到父母所负的义务，他还为禁止无力养家者结婚的法律辩护。把它用到自私的指责上，是我们的推论。反驳是：他的标准关乎前景和能力，因此它谴责的是草率地为人父母，而不是为人父母本身；一个养得起孩子的父母可以轻松通过这个标准。

quote.en: The fact itself, of causing the existence of a human being, is one of the most responsible actions in the range of human life.
quote.zh: The fact itself, of causing the existence of a human being, is one of the most responsible actions in the range of human life.

label.en: John Stuart Mill, On Liberty, ch. V
label.zh: 密尔《论自由》第五章

claim.en: I wrote that women take on direct responsibility for the life or death of the human race with no study, no experience and no guarantee of capability, trusting that maternal instinct will see them through.
claim.zh: 我写道，女人担起了关乎整个人类生死的直接责任，却没有学习，没有经验，也没有任何能力上的保证，只指望所谓母性本能能让她们应付过去。

detail.en: Gilman was arguing for trained, shared child care, not against motherhood: she thought the work too important to leave to instinct. Reading it as a reason that the choice to have children needs justifying is our step. The objection: she wanted better parents, not fewer, and her argument bears on how children are raised far more than on whether they are born.
detail.zh: 吉尔曼主张的是受过训练、由社会分担的育儿，而不是反对做母亲：她认为这份工作太重要，不能交给本能。把它读作生孩子需要理由的依据，是我们的推论。反驳是：她想要的是更好的父母，而不是更少的父母，她的论证关乎孩子怎样被养大，远多于孩子该不该出生。

quote.en: Women enter a position which gives into their hands direct responsibility for the life or death of the whole human race with neither study nor experience, with no shadow of preparation or guarantee of capability.
quote.zh: Women enter a position which gives into their hands direct responsibility for the life or death of the whole human race with neither study nor experience, with no shadow of preparation or guarantee of capability.

label.en: Charlotte Perkins Gilman, Women and Economics
label.zh: 吉尔曼《妇女与经济》

claim.en: I held that merely existing is so sweet that even the wretched do not want to perish: what they wish gone is their misery, not themselves.
claim.zh: 我认为，单单存在本身就如此甜美，连悲惨的人也不愿灭亡：他们希望消失的是自己的痛苦，而不是自己。

detail.en: In the City of God this is an argument about nature's love of being, and it leads toward God: Augustine believed the life truly worth having is eternal life with God, not endless years on earth. Using it for a healthy earthly forever is our step. The objection is that not wanting to die today is not the same as wanting never to die: fearing the end and wanting no end are different things.
detail.zh: 在《上帝之城》中，这是一个关于自然热爱存在的论证，并且指向上帝：奥古斯丁相信，真正值得拥有的是与上帝同在的永生，而不是在世上无尽的岁月。把它用在健康的尘世永生上，是我们的推论。反驳是：今天不想死，并不等于永远不想死——害怕终点与不要终点是两回事。

quote.en: And truly the very fact of existing is by some natural spell so pleasant, that even the wretched are, for no other reason, unwilling to perish; and, when they feel that they are wretched, wish not that they themselves be annihilated, but that their misery be so.
quote.zh: And truly the very fact of existing is by some natural spell so pleasant, that even the wretched are, for no other reason, unwilling to perish; and, when they feel that they are wretched, wish not that they themselves be annihilated, but that their misery be so.

label.en: Augustine, The City of God, Book XI, ch. 27, trans. Marcus Dods
label.zh: 奥古斯丁《上帝之城》第十一卷第二十七章，多兹 英译

claim.en: I argued that every thing strives to persist in its own being, and that this striving involves no fixed term: nothing in a thing's own nature sets a date for its end.
claim.zh: 我论证过，每一事物都努力保持自身的存在，而这种努力不包含任何限定的时间：事物自身的本性中，没有什么规定了它终结的日期。

detail.en: Spinoza was giving an account of all things, not recommending long life, and he also wrote that a free man thinks of nothing less than of death. Reading the wish for endless healthy life as this striving become conscious of itself is our step. The objection: a striving is not a verdict, and that something pushes to go on does not show that going on forever would be good.
detail.zh: 斯宾诺莎是在解释万物，而不是在提倡长寿；他还写过，自由的人最少想到死亡。把对无尽健康生命的愿望读作这种努力的自觉，是我们的推论。反驳是：努力不等于判断——某物竭力延续下去，并不证明永远延续下去是好的。

quote.en: The endeavour, whereby a thing endeavours to persist in its own being, involves no finite time, but an indefinite time.
quote.zh: The endeavour, whereby a thing endeavours to persist in its own being, involves no finite time, but an indefinite time.

label.en: Baruch Spinoza, Ethics, Part III, Prop. VIII, trans. R. H. M. Elwes
label.zh: 斯宾诺莎《伦理学》第三部分命题八，埃尔维斯 英译

claim.en: I taught that endless time holds no more pleasure than limited time, once reason has measured what pleasure is. A complete life has no need to go on forever.
claim.zh: 我教导说，一旦用理性量清了快乐的界限，无限的时间并不比有限的时间包含更多快乐。一个完整的人生，不需要永远延续。

detail.en: Epicurus held that pleasure, rightly understood, peaks as the absence of pain and does not grow by adding time, so death takes nothing from a complete life. Applying this to an offer of endless health is our step. The objection: his measure of pleasure is deliberately narrow, and people who love their work, other people or discovery may find that more time does bring more of what they value.
detail.zh: 伊壁鸠鲁认为，正确理解的快乐在痛苦消除时便达到顶点，不会因时间延长而增加，所以死亡并没有从一个完整的人生中拿走什么。把它用在无尽健康的提议上，是我们的推论。反驳是：他对快乐的衡量刻意狭窄；热爱工作、热爱他人或热爱探索的人，可能会发现更多时间确实带来更多他们珍视的东西。

quote.en: Infinite and finite time both have equal pleasure, if any one measures its limits by reason.
quote.zh: Infinite and finite time both have equal pleasure, if any one measures its limits by reason.

label.en: Epicurus, Principal Doctrines 19, in Diogenes Laertius, Lives, Book X, trans. C. D. Yonge
label.zh: 伊壁鸠鲁《主要原理》第 19 条，见第欧根尼·拉尔修《名哲言行录》第十卷，扬格 英译

claim.en: I told myself that it comes to the same whether a man watches the world for forty years or for ten thousand: the same things return, and there is nothing more to see.
claim.zh: 我对自己说，一个人看这世界四十年也好，一万年也好，都是一样的：同样的事物反复出现，再没有更多可看。

detail.en: Marcus wrote this to steady himself toward death, in a notebook not meant for others. Treating it as a reason to refuse endless life is our step. The objection is that his world changed slowly; someone who lived long enough to watch societies, sciences and arts transformed might see a great deal more.
detail.zh: 马可·奥勒留写下这些，是为了让自己平静地面对死亡，写在一本不打算给别人看的笔记里。把它当作拒绝永生的理由，是我们的推论。反驳是：他的世界变化缓慢；一个活得足够久、亲眼看着社会、科学与艺术发生巨变的人，也许会看到多得多的东西。

quote.en: It comes all to one therefore, whether a man be a spectator of the things of this life but forty years, or whether he see them ten thousand years together: for what shall he see more?
quote.zh: It comes all to one therefore, whether a man be a spectator of the things of this life but forty years, or whether he see them ten thousand years together: for what shall he see more?

label.en: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations, trans. Meric Casaubon
label.zh: 马可·奥勒留《沉思录》，卡索邦 英译

claim.en: I argued that death does not come to the living only from outside. Life, as life, carries the germ of its own death; to be finite is to hold one's ending within.
claim.zh: 我论证过，死亡并非只是从外部降临到生者身上。生命作为生命，本身就带着死亡的种子；有限，就是在自身之中包含着终结。

detail.en: Hegel's point is logical: a finite thing is defined by a limit it contains, not one imposed on it from outside. Reading this as saying that an endless human life would no longer be a human life is our step. The objection is that logic cannot settle biology: if medicine could hold the end off indefinitely, Hegel's argument would tell us what finitude means, not whether to accept it.
detail.zh: 黑格尔的论点是逻辑上的：有限之物由它内含的界限所规定，而不是由外部强加的界限。把它读成无尽的人生将不再是人的一生，是我们的推论。反驳是：逻辑解决不了生物学的问题——如果医学能无限期推迟终点，黑格尔的论证告诉我们的只是有限意味着什么，而不是我们是否应当接受它。

quote.en: But the true view of the matter is that life, as life, involves the germ of death, and that the finite, being radically self-contradictory, involves its own self-suppression.
quote.zh: But the true view of the matter is that life, as life, involves the germ of death, and that the finite, being radically self-contradictory, involves its own self-suppression.

label.en: G. W. F. Hegel, The Logic of Hegel (Encyclopaedia of the Philosophical Sciences, Part I), trans. William Wallace
label.zh: 黑格尔《哲学全书·逻辑学》（小逻辑），华莱士 英译

claim.en: I taught that the door ought to stand open for every occasion. Knowing that we may leave is what lets us stay without being troubled.
claim.zh: 我教导说，门应当为一切情形敞开。知道自己可以离开，正是让我们能够留下而不受困扰的原因。

detail.en: The open door is Epictetus's figure for leaving life when it becomes intolerable, and he also taught that one should not leave without good reason. Applying it to an endless life, acceptable only with the exit kept open, is our step. The objection: in Stoic thought the exit is bearable partly because death comes anyway; an endless life with an optional exit would put the whole weight of ending on a single choice, renewed every day.
detail.zh: 敞开的门，是爱比克泰德对生活变得无法忍受时离开人世的比喻；他同时也教导，没有正当理由不应离开。把它用在一个只有保留出口才可以接受的无尽人生上，是我们的推论。反驳是：在斯多葛思想中，出口之所以可以承受，部分在于死亡终究会来；一个出口可选的无尽人生，会把结束的全部重量压在一个每天都要重新面对的选择上。

quote.en: For the door ought to be open for all occasions; and so we have no trouble.
quote.zh: For the door ought to be open for all occasions; and so we have no trouble.

origin.zh: 尼科波利斯，约公元 108 年

label.en: Epictetus, Discourses, Book II, ch. 1, trans. George Long
label.zh: 爱比克泰德《论说集》第二卷第一章，朗 英译

claim.en: I wrote that to think on death beforehand is to think on liberty: whoever has learned to die has unlearned how to serve.
claim.zh: 我写过，预先思考死亡，就是预先思考自由：学会了死的人，也就忘掉了如何做奴仆。

detail.en: The line comes from Montaigne's essay that to philosophise is to learn to die, and it echoes Seneca; his point is that a person unafraid of the end cannot be cowed. Taking it to mean that an endless life stays free only if ending remains possible is our step. The objection: Montaigne's freedom comes from accepting a death that will certainly come, not from keeping an option in reserve.
detail.zh: 这句话出自蒙田那篇谈哲学即学习死亡的随笔，并呼应了塞涅卡；他的意思是，不惧怕终点的人无法被威吓。把它理解为无尽的人生只有在仍可结束时才是自由的，是我们的推论。反驳是：蒙田的自由来自接受一个必然到来的死亡，而不是保留一个备用的选项。

quote.en: The premeditation of death is the premeditation of liberty; he who has learned to die has unlearned to serve.
quote.zh: The premeditation of death is the premeditation of liberty; he who has learned to die has unlearned to serve.

label.en: Michel de Montaigne, Essays, Book I, ch. 19, trans. Charles Cotton
label.zh: 蒙田《随笔集》第一卷第十九章，科顿 英译

claim.en: I taught that what nature needs is easy to get and what is useless is hard to get. Those who can best do without luxury enjoy it most.
claim.zh: 我教导说，自然所需的东西容易得到，无用的东西才难以得到。最能不靠奢侈过日子的人，最能享受奢侈。

detail.en: The Letter to Menoeceus is advice on living pleasantly by needing little; it says nothing about wages or working weeks, and turning it into a case for trading pay for time is our step. The strongest objection: the advice assumes you already have the natural necessities. For someone whose fifth day pays the rent, giving it up is not a matter of trimming desires.
detail.zh: 《致美诺寇的信》是关于靠少欲而活得愉快的劝告；它没有谈工资或工作周，把它变成以工资换时间的理由，是我们的推演。最有力的反驳：这个劝告预设你已经拥有自然所需。对一个靠第五天的工资付房租的人来说，放弃那一天不是删减欲望的问题。

quote.en: those men enjoy luxury most completely who are the best able to do without it
quote.zh: those men enjoy luxury most completely who are the best able to do without it

label.en: Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus, in Diogenes Laertius, Lives X, trans. C. D. Yonge
label.zh: 伊壁鸠鲁《致美诺寇的信》，见第欧根尼·拉尔修《名哲言行录》第十卷，永格 英译

claim.en: I argued that a weekly day of rest is a good custom that no one can keep alone, because those who go on working impose the same necessity on everyone else. So the law may rightly guarantee it for all by suspending the greater operations of industry.
claim.zh: 我认为，每周休息一天是好习俗，却没有人能独自守住，因为继续工作的人会把同样的压力加到其他所有人身上。所以法律可以正当地暂停主要的工商活动，为所有人保障这一天。

detail.en: Surprisingly for the author of On Liberty, this is an argument against leaving rest to each person's choice. Mill made it about the Sabbath, and stretching it to a third free day is our step. The limit is his own: in the same passage he refused to let the law say how anyone spends that day, and his reasoning covers a common day off, not a cut in pay.
detail.zh: 出自《论自由》的作者，这竟是一个反对把休息交给个人选择的论证。密尔是就安息日说的，把它延伸到每周第三个休息日，是我们的推演。限度出自他自己：在同一段里，他拒绝让法律规定任何人如何度过那一天；而他的推理涵盖的是共同的休息日，不是减薪。

quote.en: in so far as some persons by working may impose the same necessity on others, it may be allowable and right that the law should guarantee to each, the observance by others of the custom, by suspending the greater operations of industry on a particular day.
quote.zh: in so far as some persons by working may impose the same necessity on others, it may be allowable and right that the law should guarantee to each, the observance by others of the custom, by suspending the greater operations of industry on a particular day.

label.en: John Stuart Mill, On Liberty, Chapter IV
label.zh: 约翰·斯图亚特·密尔《论自由》第四章

claim.en: I argued that a man in comfortable circumstances may not let his talents rest and give his life to idleness and enjoyment. As a rational being he must will that his faculties be developed, since they were given him for all sorts of purposes.
claim.zh: 我认为，一个境况安逸的人不可以让自己的才能闲置，把一生交给懒散和享乐。作为理性存在者，他必然意愿自己的能力得到发展，因为这些能力是为各种可能的目的而赋予他的。

detail.en: This is one of Kant's four examples in the Groundwork, a duty to cultivate one's gifts rather than live for pleasure. Treating it as a case for keeping the fifth working day is our step, and the weakest one here: Kant's duty is to develop faculties, not to sell hours, and a free day spent learning or making something may meet it better than one more day of routine.
detail.zh: 这是康德在《奠基》中的四个例子之一：培养自身禀赋、而不是为享乐而活的义务。把它当作保留第五个工作日的理由，是我们的推演，也是这里最弱的一步：康德的义务是发展能力，不是出卖工时；一个用来学习或创造的休息日，可能比多一天例行工作更能履行它。

quote.en: For, as a rational being, he necessarily wills that his faculties be developed, since they serve him and have been given him, for all sorts of possible purposes.
quote.zh: For, as a rational being, he necessarily wills that his faculties be developed, since they serve him and have been given him, for all sorts of possible purposes.

label.en: Immanuel Kant, Groundwork of the Metaphysic of Morals, Second Section, trans. T. K. Abbott
label.zh: 康德《道德形而上学奠基》第二章，阿博特 英译

claim.en: I argued that most of us habitually use only a small part of the powers we have. We stop at the first layer of fatigue, and beyond it, if something presses us on, lie reserves we never touch.
claim.zh: 我认为，我们大多数人习惯上只用了自己能力中的一小部分。我们在第一层疲劳处就停下了；若有什么推着我们继续，越过它，就是我们从未动用过的储备。

detail.en: In The Energies of Men James was describing untapped mental and physical power, released by crisis, ideas and effort of will. Using it against a shorter week is our step. The objection is in the same essay: he says these deeper reserves repair themselves by rest, and nothing in it suggests that one more day of ordinary work is what wakes them.
detail.zh: 在〈人的能量〉中，詹姆斯描述的是未被开发的身心力量，由危机、观念和意志的努力所唤起。用它来反对缩短工作周，是我们的推演。反驳就在同一篇文章里：他说这些更深的储备也靠休息来恢复，文中也没有任何地方暗示，多上一天平常的班就能唤醒它们。

quote.en: Compared with what we ought to be, we are only half awake. Our fires are damped, our drafts are checked. We are making use of only a small part of our possible mental and physical resources.
quote.zh: Compared with what we ought to be, we are only half awake. Our fires are damped, our drafts are checked. We are making use of only a small part of our possible mental and physical resources.

label.en: William James, The Energies of Men, in Memories and Studies
label.zh: 威廉·詹姆斯〈人的能量〉，收入《回忆与研究》

claim.en: I found that by working with my hands about six weeks a year I could meet all my expenses, and kept the rest of the year free for study. But I wanted no one to copy my way of living; I wanted each person to find and pursue his own.
claim.zh: 我发现，一年只靠双手干大约六个星期的活，就足以支付全部开销，其余时间都留给了学习。但我不希望任何人照搬我的生活方式；我希望每个人找到并走自己的路。

detail.en: Walden opens with this accounting of what things cost in life rather than money. Placing it under choose-your-own-hours is our step; Thoreau could as easily stand under time over money. The objection is that his freedom was unusually cheap: a single man, borrowed land, no dependants, and a town close by. Most people's hours are set by employers and households, not by the cost of beans.
detail.zh: 《瓦尔登湖》开篇就是这笔账：东西的代价，按生命而不是按钱来算。把它放在自己选工时之下，是我们的推演；梭罗同样可以站在时间比钱更值那一边。反驳在于他的自由异常便宜：单身、借来的土地、无人需要供养、镇子就在附近。多数人的工时是由雇主和家庭决定的，而不是由豆子的价钱。

quote.en: For more than five years I maintained myself thus solely by the labor of my hands, and I found, that by working about six weeks in a year, I could meet all the expenses of living.
quote.zh: For more than five years I maintained myself thus solely by the labor of my hands, and I found, that by working about six weeks in a year, I could meet all the expenses of living.

origin.zh: 马萨诸塞州康科德，1854 年

label.en: Henry David Thoreau, Walden, Economy
label.zh: 梭罗《瓦尔登湖》〈经济篇〉

claim.en: I held that the property every man has in his own labour is the most sacred of all. The patrimony of a poor man is the strength and skill of his hands, and to stop him using them as he thinks proper, without injuring his neighbour, violates it.
claim.zh: 我认为，每个人对自己劳动的所有权，是一切所有权中最神圣的。穷人的全部家当就是他双手的力气与技巧；只要不伤害邻人，阻止他按自己认为合适的方式使用它们，就是侵犯这份所有权。

detail.en: Smith wrote this against the apprenticeship laws that kept workmen out of trades, not about hours; reading it as a case for choosing one's own week is our step. The surprise is in the same book: he also warned that men paid by the piece overwork themselves, and that the man who works moderately enough to work constantly does the most in a year. And Mill's reply names the weak point: one person's freely chosen long hours can set the terms for everyone else.
detail.zh: 斯密写这段话，针对的是把工人挡在行业之外的学徒法，而不是工时；把它读成自己选择工作周的理由，是我们的推演。意外之处在同一本书里：他也警告说，计件拿钱的人会过度劳累，而干得适度、能长久干下去的人，一年里干得最多。密尔在这个问题上的回应点出了弱点：一个人自愿的长工时，可能为所有人定下条件。

quote.en: The patrimony of a poor man lies in the strength and dexterity of his hands; and to hinder him from employing this strength and dexterity in what manner he thinks proper, without injury to his neighbour, is a plain violation of this most sacred property.
quote.zh: The patrimony of a poor man lies in the strength and dexterity of his hands; and to hinder him from employing this strength and dexterity in what manner he thinks proper, without injury to his neighbour, is a plain violation of this most sacred property.

label.en: Adam Smith, The Wealth of Nations, Book I, Chapter 10
label.zh: 亚当·斯密《国富论》第一卷第十章

claim.en: I held that the best medicine for keeping the mind healthy is the faithful admonition of a friend. Judging yourself is too corrosive and books are too flat; a friend's counsel is drier and purer light than your own.
claim.zh: 我认为，保持心智健康最好的良药，是朋友忠实的规劝。自我审判太过刺激，读书又太过平淡；朋友的忠告，比你自己的判断更清澈、更纯净。

detail.en: Of Friendship lists counsel as one of friendship's chief fruits, and Bacon was writing with courtiers and great men in mind; extending it to an unasked-for truth between equals is our step. The objection is that he praises counsel a man receives, and says little about how often it is refused or resented when it was not sought.
detail.zh: 《论友谊》把忠告列为友谊的主要果实之一，培根写作时心里想的是朝臣和权贵；把它推到平辈之间没人要求的真话上，是我们自己的一步。反驳在于：他赞美的是一个人接受的忠告，却很少谈到不请自来的忠告有多常被拒绝或怨恨。

quote.en: It is a strange thing to behold, what gross errors and extreme absurdities many (especially of the greater sort) do commit, for want of a friend to tell them of them; to the great damage both of their fame and fortune
quote.zh: It is a strange thing to behold, what gross errors and extreme absurdities many (especially of the greater sort) do commit, for want of a friend to tell them of them; to the great damage both of their fame and fortune

label.en: Francis Bacon, Essays, Of Friendship
label.zh: 培根《随笔集》〈论友谊〉

claim.en: I wrote that a friend who only agrees with me is worthless to me. Where I hoped for support or at least resistance, I hate to find a mush of concession; better to sting a friend than to echo him.
claim.zh: 我写过，一个只会附和我的朋友对我毫无用处。我期待的是支持，至少是抵抗，却只看到一团退让，这让我厌恶；宁可做朋友身边的荨麻，也不要做他的回声。

detail.en: The essay Friendship describes an ideal between two strong, independent people and admits such friendships are rare; applying it to everyday candour is our step. Its weakness is that Emerson's ideal friend can do without the friendship, and most real friends cannot, so a sting may end what an echo would have kept.
detail.zh: 《友谊》这篇随笔描述的是两个强大而独立的人之间的理想，也承认这样的友谊很少见；把它用到日常的坦率上，是我们自己的一步。它的弱点是：爱默生理想中的朋友可以不需要这段友谊，而大多数真实的朋友做不到，于是一下刺痛可能终结一段原本靠附和就能维持的关系。

quote.en: I hate, where I looked for a manly furtherance, or at least a manly resistance, to find a mush of concession. Better be a nettle in the side of your friend than his echo.
quote.zh: I hate, where I looked for a manly furtherance, or at least a manly resistance, to find a mush of concession. Better be a nettle in the side of your friend than his echo.

origin.zh: 马萨诸塞州康科德，1841 年

label.en: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Essays: First Series, Friendship
label.zh: 爱默生《随笔集·第一辑》〈友谊〉

claim.en: I argued that society may not compel a person for his own good, but that it may, and should, tell him plainly where it thinks he is wrong. I wished people could point out one another's faults far more freely than politeness allows.
claim.zh: 我认为，社会不能为了一个人自己的好处而强迫他，但可以、也应当坦白告诉他，它认为他哪里错了。我希望人们能比礼貌所允许的更自由地指出彼此的过失。

detail.en: This comes from the chapter of On Liberty that draws the line between persuasion and compulsion: telling someone is allowed precisely because forcing them is not. Applying it to a friend is our step; the objection is that Mill was defending a right to speak, and a right says nothing about whether speaking is wise in a given case.
detail.zh: 这段出自《论自由》中划分劝说与强制界限的那一章：可以告诉一个人，恰恰因为不能强迫他。把它用到朋友身上，是我们自己的一步；反驳在于：密尔辩护的是说话的权利，而权利本身并不说明在具体情形下说出来是否明智。

quote.en: It would be well, indeed, if this good office were much more freely rendered than the common notions of politeness at present permit, and if one person could honestly point out to another that he thinks him in fault, without being considered unmannerly or presuming.
quote.zh: It would be well, indeed, if this good office were much more freely rendered than the common notions of politeness at present permit, and if one person could honestly point out to another that he thinks him in fault, without being considered unmannerly or presuming.

label.en: John Stuart Mill, On Liberty, ch. IV
label.zh: 约翰·斯图亚特·密尔《论自由》第四章

claim.en: I told myself to correct those who go wrong if I am able, and if I am not, to bear with them patiently. Showing a man his error is worth doing only where it can cure him; otherwise mildness is the duty.
claim.zh: 我告诫自己：对犯错的人，能教就教；教不了，就耐心地包容他们。指出一个人的错，只有在能治好他时才值得做；否则，温和才是本分。

detail.en: The Meditations are private notes on how an emperor should treat difficult people, not advice about friends; carrying the rule to a friend's hard truth is our step. Its weakness is that you rarely know beforehand whether a truth will cure, so the condition can become an excuse for never trying.
detail.zh: 《沉思录》是一位皇帝写给自己的笔记，讲的是如何对待难相处的人，并非关于朋友的建议；把这条规则用到对朋友说难听的真话上，是我们自己的一步。它的弱点在于：你很少能事先知道一句真话能不能治好人，于是这个条件可能变成永远不去尝试的借口。

quote.en: Either teach them better if it be in thy power; or if it be not, remember that for this use, to bear with them patiently, was mildness and goodness granted unto thee.
quote.zh: Either teach them better if it be in thy power; or if it be not, remember that for this use, to bear with them patiently, was mildness and goodness granted unto thee.

label.en: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations, trans. Meric Casaubon
label.zh: 马可·奥勒留《沉思录》，卡索邦 英译

claim.en: I held that it takes no small strength of character to take each person as he is. Those who are better at railing at vice than at building virtue, who break people rather than strengthen them, harm themselves and everyone else.
claim.zh: 我认为，接受每个人本来的样子，需要不小的品格力量。那些更擅长痛斥恶习而非培养德性、把人压垮而不是使人坚强的人，既伤害自己，也伤害别人。

detail.en: This is a rule in the appendix to Part IV of the Ethics on how to live among people who mostly do not live by reason; turning it into a test for one conversation is our step. The objection is that almost anyone who speaks a hard truth believes they are strengthening, so the test is hard to apply to oneself.
detail.zh: 这是《伦理学》第四部分附录中的一条规则，讲的是如何与大多不依理性生活的人相处；把它变成一次谈话的检验标准，是我们自己的一步。反驳在于：几乎每个说难听真话的人都相信自己是在使对方坚强，所以这个标准很难用来检验自己。

quote.en: But those who carp at mankind, and are more skilled in railing at vice than in instilling virtue, and who break rather than strengthen men's dispositions, are hurtful both to themselves and others.
quote.zh: But those who carp at mankind, and are more skilled in railing at vice than in instilling virtue, and who break rather than strengthen men's dispositions, are hurtful both to themselves and others.

label.en: Baruch Spinoza, Ethics, Part IV, Appendix XIII, trans. R. H. M. Elwes
label.zh: 斯宾诺莎《伦理学》第四部分附录第十三条，埃尔维斯 英译

claim.en: I taught that one should not lecture the uninstructed about how to live, but simply live that way. At a feast, do not tell others how to eat; eat properly, and let your conduct be the only instruction.
claim.zh: 我教导说，不要对未受教的人讲该怎样生活，只要自己那样生活就好。宴席上，不要告诉别人该怎么吃；自己吃得得体，让行为成为唯一的教导。

detail.en: The Enchiridion is advice to a student of philosophy about not showing off his principles, and its target is vanity, not friendship; reading it as a rule for friends is our step. The strongest objection is that a good example works slowly, and some mistakes a friend is making will be past repair before any example is noticed.
detail.zh: 《手册》是给哲学学生的建议，叫他不要炫耀自己的原则，它针对的是虚荣，而不是友谊；把它读作朋友之间的规则，是我们自己的一步。最有力的反驳是：好榜样起作用很慢，而朋友正在犯的有些错误，等他注意到榜样时早已无法挽回。

quote.en: For example, at a banquet do not say how a man ought to eat, but eat as you ought to eat.
quote.zh: For example, at a banquet do not say how a man ought to eat, but eat as you ought to eat.

origin.zh: 尼科波利斯，约公元 125 年

label.en: Epictetus, Enchiridion §46, trans. George Long
label.zh: 爱比克泰德《手册》第 46 节，朗 英译

claim.en: I argued that the rules of good manners were invented because pride collides with pride in company. Deference shown, contempt disguised and authority hidden are virtues in their own right, because they are immediately agreeable to others.
claim.zh: 我认为，礼貌的规则之所以产生，是因为在交往中骄傲总会撞上骄傲。表现尊重、掩饰轻视、隐藏权威，本身就是美德，因为它们直接让他人感到愉快。

detail.en: Hume is describing politeness in company, among acquaintances, as one kind of merit among several; extending it to a close friend's mistake is our step. The objection comes from Hume's own system, which also prizes what is useful, and a friend kept comfortable in an error has been pleased, not served.
detail.zh: 休谟描述的是社交场合、熟人之间的礼貌，把它看作多种美德中的一种；把它推到好朋友犯的错误上，是我们自己的一步。反驳来自休谟自己的体系：他同样看重有用的品质，而一个被安稳地留在错误里的朋友，只是被取悦了，并没有被帮到。

quote.en: Among well-bred people, a mutual deference is affected; contempt of others disguised; authority concealed; attention given to each in his turn; and an easy stream of conversation maintained, without vehemence, without interruption, without eagerness for victory, and without any airs of superiority.
quote.zh: Among well-bred people, a mutual deference is affected; contempt of others disguised; authority concealed; attention given to each in his turn; and an easy stream of conversation maintained, without vehemence, without interruption, without eagerness for victory, and without any airs of superiority.

label.en: David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals, Section VIII
label.zh: 大卫·休谟《道德原则研究》第八章

claim.en: Bentham's Panopticon was built on the feeling of being watched, and he proposed it for prisons, schools, hospitals and workhouses alike. On this view, visibility improves conduct, and the well-behaved lose nothing.
claim.zh: 边沁的圆形监狱建立在「被注视感」之上，他把它推荐给监狱、学校、医院和济贫院。照此看法，可见性会改善行为，而守规矩的人什么也不会失去。

detail.en: That is the strongest version of the 'nothing to hide' case. The cost is that Bentham's own design works through constant self-monitoring, which is exactly the change in the innocent that critics fear.
detail.zh: 这是「没什么可藏」论证最有力的版本。代价是：边沁自己的设计正是通过持续的自我监控来运作的，而这恰恰是批评者担心的、发生在无辜者身上的改变。

quote.en: the persons to be inspected should always feel themselves as if under inspection, at least as standing a great chance of being so
quote.zh: the persons to be inspected should always feel themselves as if under inspection, at least as standing a great chance of being so

label.en: Jeremy Bentham, Panopticon; or, The Inspection-House (1791)
label.zh: 边沁《圆形监狱》（1791）

claim.en: Rousseau traced a loss in social life: people come to live in others' eyes rather than their own. Being watched more closely deepens that shift whether or not you have anything to hide.
claim.zh: 卢梭追溯了社会生活中的一种丧失：人们开始活在他人的眼光里，而不是自己的感受里。被更紧密地注视，会加深这种转变——无论你有没有东西要藏。

detail.en: On this reading the harm of watching is not exposure but performance: you start living for the viewer. The cost is that Rousseau's 'savage' is an idealised figure, and the argument tells you what is lost without saying how much watching is too much.
detail.zh: 照这个读法，被注视的伤害不在于暴露，而在于表演：你开始为观看者而活。代价是：卢梭的「野蛮人」是一个理想化的形象，这个论证告诉你失去了什么，却没说多少注视才算太多。

quote.en: the savage lives within himself, whereas the citizen, constantly beside himself, knows only how to live in the opinion of others
quote.zh: the savage lives within himself, whereas the citizen, constantly beside himself, knows only how to live in the opinion of others

label.en: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Discourse on the Origin of Inequality, Part II
label.zh: 卢梭《论人类不平等的起源和基础》第二部分

claim.en: Mill described a society where everyone lives as if under a hostile censor, so people stop asking what they prefer and ask what is expected. He meant public opinion, not cameras, but the mechanism is the same.
claim.zh: 密尔描述了一个人人都像生活在敌意审查者眼皮底下的社会，于是人们不再问自己喜欢什么，而是问别人期待什么。他说的是舆论而非摄像头，但机制相同。

detail.en: By this argument the innocent lose something real: the habit of choosing for themselves. The cost is that Mill also accepted that society may watch and punish harm to others, so the line between protection and censorship is still to be drawn.
detail.zh: 照这个论证，无辜者失去了真实的东西：为自己做选择的习惯。代价是：密尔也承认社会可以监督并惩罚对他人的伤害，因此保护与审查之间的界线仍有待划定。

quote.en: In our times, from the highest class of society down to the lowest, every one lives as under the eye of a hostile and dreaded censorship. Not only in what concerns others, but in what concerns only themselves, the individual, or the family, do not ask themselves--what do I prefer?
quote.zh: In our times, from the highest class of society down to the lowest, every one lives as under the eye of a hostile and dreaded censorship. Not only in what concerns others, but in what concerns only themselves, the individual, or the family, do not ask themselves--what do I prefer?

label.en: John Stuart Mill, On Liberty, ch. III
label.zh: 约翰·斯图亚特·密尔《论自由》第三章

claim.en: Thoreau describes government as a device for letting people alone. On his terms, a government that watches the innocent has reversed its purpose — whether or not they have anything to hide.
claim.zh: 梭罗把政府描述为一种让人们彼此不受打扰的手段。按他的说法，一个监视无辜者的政府已经背离了自己的目的——无论他们有没有东西要藏。

detail.en: This puts the burden on the watcher, not the watched. The cost is that Thoreau's ideal of minimal government offers little guidance on threats that really do require looking, such as violence planned in private.
detail.zh: 这把举证责任放在了监视者身上，而不是被监视者。代价是：梭罗的最小政府理想，对于那些确实需要察看的威胁——比如私下策划的暴力——几乎没有指导。

quote.en: For government is an expedient, by which men would fain succeed in letting one another alone; and, as has been said, when it is most expedient, the governed are most let alone by it.
quote.zh: For government is an expedient, by which men would fain succeed in letting one another alone; and, as has been said, when it is most expedient, the governed are most let alone by it.

origin.zh: 马萨诸塞州康科德，1849 年

label.en: Henry David Thoreau, "Civil Disobedience" (1849)
label.zh: 梭罗〈论公民的不服从〉（1849）

claim.en: Godwin hoped small communities could do without much law, because neighbours watching one another's conduct would restrain vice more surely than punishment. Being seen, for him, was the better kind of discipline.
claim.zh: 葛德文希望小型社群可以不太需要法律，因为邻里彼此注视对方的行为，会比刑罚更有效地约束恶行。在他看来，被人看见是一种更好的约束。

detail.en: Godwin meant the free judgement of neighbours, not cameras or a state's records, and he said it worked only when 'unstained with caprice'; moving it to data collection is ours. His position is contested, and the cost is plain in his own words: a censorship that cannot be resisted is also one an innocent oddity cannot escape.
detail.zh: 葛德文说的是邻里自由的判断，不是摄像头或国家的档案，而且他说只有在不受任性玷污时才有效；把它搬到数据收集上是我们的推论。他的立场颇有争议，代价就在他自己的话里：一种无法抗拒的审查，也是一个无害的怪人无法逃脱的审查。

quote.en: the inspection of every man over the conduct of his neighbours, when unstained with caprice, would constitute a censorship of the most irresistible nature.
quote.zh: the inspection of every man over the conduct of his neighbours, when unstained with caprice, would constitute a censorship of the most irresistible nature.

label.en: William Godwin, An Enquiry Concerning Political Justice
label.zh: 葛德文《政治正义论》

claim.en: William James held that a person has as many social selves as there are groups whose opinion he cares about, and shows each a different side. Who is watching shapes which self appears.
claim.zh: 威廉·詹姆斯认为，一个人在意多少群体的看法，就有多少个社会自我，并向每个群体展示不同的一面。谁在看，决定了哪个自我出现。

detail.en: James treats this as normal and often harmless, a division of labour as much as a mask; the worry that constant watching collapses those selves into one performance is our extension. The weakness is that, on his account, there is no unperformed self for privacy to protect, only selves suited to different audiences.
detail.zh: 詹姆斯把这看作正常的、往往无害的事，与其说是面具，不如说是一种分工；担心无处不在的注视会把这些自我压缩成一场表演，是我们的延伸。弱点是：按他的说法，并不存在一个未经表演、需要隐私来保护的自我，只有适合不同观众的各个自我。

quote.en: He generally shows a different side of himself to each of these different groups.
quote.zh: He generally shows a different side of himself to each of these different groups.

label.en: William James, The Principles of Psychology, vol. 1, ch. X
label.zh: 威廉·詹姆斯《心理学原理》第一卷第十章

claim.en: Smith held that a sovereign should be freed from superintending private people's work, because no human wisdom or knowledge could ever be enough to do it well. Leaving people alone was not a gap in government but part of its proper shape.
claim.zh: 斯密认为，君主应当卸下监管私人劳动的职责，因为任何人的智慧或知识都不足以把这件事做好。让人们自行其是，不是政府的缺位，而是政府应有的样子。

detail.en: Smith was writing about trade and industry, not about watching citizens; reading his limit on what a sovereign can know as a limit on surveillance is ours. The cost is that his argument rests on the state not being able to know enough, and modern data collection is precisely an attempt to close that gap.
detail.zh: 斯密写的是贸易与产业，不是监视公民；把他对君主所能知之限度的论述，读成对监控的限制，是我们的推论。代价是：他的论证建立在国家无法知道足够多这一点上，而现代的数据收集恰恰是在试图填补这个空缺。

quote.en: The sovereign is completely discharged from a duty, in the attempting to perform which he must always be exposed to innumerable delusions, and for the proper performance of which, no human wisdom or knowledge could ever be sufficient; the duty of superintending the industry of private people, and of directing it towards the employments most suitable to the interests of the society.
quote.zh: The sovereign is completely discharged from a duty, in the attempting to perform which he must always be exposed to innumerable delusions, and for the proper performance of which, no human wisdom or knowledge could ever be sufficient; the duty of superintending the industry of private people, and of directing it towards the employments most suitable to the interests of the society.

label.en: Adam Smith, The Wealth of Nations, Book IV, ch. IX
label.zh: 亚当·斯密《国富论》第四卷第九章

claim.en: The Analects picture a ruler whose virtue does the work: people orient themselves around a good character the way stars turn around the pole star.
claim.zh: 《论语》描绘的统治者，是靠德行本身发挥作用：人们围绕一个好品格而定向，就像众星环绕北极星。

detail.en: On this view goodness is not a constraint on effectiveness; it is the mechanism. The cost is that the Analects assume a society that already shares ideas of propriety — in a divided country, a leader's virtue may attract half the sky and repel the other half.
detail.zh: 按这种看法，德行不是对效率的限制，而是效率的来源。代价是：《论语》预设了一个共享礼义观念的社会——在一个分裂的国家，领导者的德行可能吸引一半的星空，同时推开另一半。

quote.en: He who exercises government by means of his virtue may be compared to the north polar star, which keeps its place and all the stars turn towards it.
quote.zh: 爲政以德，譬如北辰，居其所，而眾星共之。

label.en: Confucius, Analects 2.1, trans. James Legge
label.zh: 《论语·为政》2.1，理雅各 英译

claim.en: The Prince argues that a ruler who acts only as a good person ought to will be destroyed among people who do not — so the leader you need must know how to do wrong.
claim.zh: 《君主论》认为，一个只按好人标准行事的统治者，在不守规矩的人中间必然毁灭——所以你需要的领导者，必须懂得如何作恶。

detail.en: Machiavelli was describing princes holding fragile Italian states, not elected officials. The cost of carrying his argument over is that it licenses any wrong a leader can call necessary, and gives the people no way to tell necessity from convenience.
detail.zh: 马基雅维利描述的是守着脆弱意大利城邦的君主，而不是民选官员。把他的论证照搬过来的代价是：领导者只要声称「必要」，就可以做任何坏事，而人民没有办法分辨那是必要还是方便。

quote.en: how one lives is so far distant from how one ought to live, that he who neglects what is done for what ought to be done, sooner effects his ruin than his preservation; for a man who wishes to act entirely up to his professions of virtue soon meets with what destroys him among so much that is evil.
quote.zh: how one lives is so far distant from how one ought to live, that he who neglects what is done for what ought to be done, sooner effects his ruin than his preservation; for a man who wishes to act entirely up to his professions of virtue soon meets with what destroys him among so much that is evil.

label.en: Niccolò Machiavelli, The Prince, ch. XV, trans. W. K. Marriott
label.zh: 马基雅维利《君主论》第十五章，马里奥特 英译

claim.en: Hobbes sets one test for whoever holds power: the safety of the people — which he says includes life's other contentments too, not bare survival. Private virtue is beside the point.
claim.zh: 霍布斯给掌权者设了唯一的标准：人民的安全——他说这还包括生活中的其他满足，而不只是活着。私人品德无关紧要。

detail.en: By this standard the 'good versus effective' question dissolves: you judge a leader by outcomes for the governed. The cost is that Hobbes makes the sovereign answerable to God alone, so the people get a standard to judge by but no way to enforce it.
detail.zh: 按这个标准，「好人还是能人」的问题就消失了：你根据被统治者的结果来评价领导者。代价是：霍布斯让主权者只对上帝负责，于是人民有了评判标准，却没有执行它的手段。

quote.en: The OFFICE of the Soveraign, (be it a Monarch, or an Assembly,) consisteth in the end, for which he was trusted with the Soveraign Power, namely the procuration of the Safety Of The People
quote.zh: The OFFICE of the Soveraign, (be it a Monarch, or an Assembly,) consisteth in the end, for which he was trusted with the Soveraign Power, namely the procuration of the Safety Of The People

label.en: Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan, ch. XXX
label.zh: 霍布斯《利维坦》第三十章

claim.en: Aristotle's name for what a good leader has is practical wisdom, and his example is a working statesman: someone who can see what is good and also how to bring it about.
claim.zh: 亚里士多德把好领导所具有的东西称为实践智慧，他举的例子正是一位实干的政治家：既能看清什么是好的，也知道如何把它实现。

detail.en: On this account, goodness without the skill to act is not yet the virtue, and skill aimed at the wrong ends is mere cleverness — so the trade-off is false. The cost is that real leaders are rarely both, and the theory says little about which to prefer when you must choose.
detail.zh: 照这个说法，不会行动的善还不是德性，而用错地方的本事只是机巧——所以这个取舍是假的。代价是：现实中的领导者很少两者兼备，而这个理论对「非选不可时该选哪个」几乎没有回答。

quote.en: For this reason we think Pericles and men of that stamp to be Practically Wise, because they can see what is good for themselves and for men in general
quote.zh: For this reason we think Pericles and men of that stamp to be Practically Wise, because they can see what is good for themselves and for men in general

label.en: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics, Book VI, ch. 5, trans. D. P. Chase
label.zh: 亚里士多德《尼各马可伦理学》第六卷第五章，蔡斯 英译

claim.en: An emperor's own notebook: do what the moment requires, don't wait for an ideal state, and count small improvements as real ones.
claim.zh: 一位皇帝写给自己的笔记：做此刻该做的事，不要等待理想国，把微小的进步也当作真正的进步。

detail.en: Read as advice to leaders, it joins the two halves: goodness is shown in getting ordinary, imperfect things done. The cost is that Marcus' modest gradualism was written by a man with absolute power; patience with small progress is easier for the one who sets the pace.
detail.zh: 把它当作给领导者的建议来读，它把两半连在了一起：善体现在把平凡而不完美的事情办成。代价是：马可·奥勒留这种温和的渐进主义，出自一个握有绝对权力的人；对小进步保持耐心，对掌控节奏的人来说更容易。

quote.en: Do what thy nature doth now require. Resolve upon it, if thou mayest: and take no thought, whether anybody shall know it or no. Yea, but sayest thou, I must not expect a Plato's commonwealth. If they profit though never so little, I must be content; and think much even of that little progress.
quote.zh: Do what thy nature doth now require. Resolve upon it, if thou mayest: and take no thought, whether anybody shall know it or no. Yea, but sayest thou, I must not expect a Plato's commonwealth. If they profit though never so little, I must be content; and think much even of that little progress.

label.en: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations, Book IX, 29, trans. Meric Casaubon
label.zh: 马可·奥勒留《沉思录》第九卷第 29 节，卡索邦 英译

claim.en: Kant held that talent, resolve and nerve are good only in the hands of a good will; without one, the same gifts become dangerous. On his view ability is no substitute for character, because character decides what ability is used for.
claim.zh: 康德认为，才智、决心和胆识，只有掌握在善良意志手中才是好的；没有善良意志，同样的天赋会变得危险。在他看来，能力不能代替品格，因为品格决定能力被用来做什么。

detail.en: Kant was writing about the moral worth of persons, not about choosing rulers; reading it as a test for leaders is our application. Its strength is the warning that competence magnifies whatever will directs it. Its cost is that Kant says little about how to judge a will from outside, which is all a voter ever sees.
detail.zh: 康德写的是人的道德价值，而不是如何挑选统治者；把它当作衡量领导者的标准，是我们的引申。它的力量在于提醒：能力会放大驱使它的任何意志。代价是：一个人的意志如何从外部判断，康德几乎没说，而选民能看到的恰恰只有外部。

quote.en: Intelligence, wit, judgement, and the other talents of the mind, however they may be named, or courage, resolution, perseverance, as qualities of temperament, are undoubtedly good and desirable in many respects; but these gifts of nature may also become extremely bad and mischievous if the will which is to make use of them, and which, therefore, constitutes what is called character, is not good.
quote.zh: Intelligence, wit, judgement, and the other talents of the mind, however they may be named, or courage, resolution, perseverance, as qualities of temperament, are undoubtedly good and desirable in many respects; but these gifts of nature may also become extremely bad and mischievous if the will which is to make use of them, and which, therefore, constitutes what is called character, is not good.

label.en: Immanuel Kant, Groundwork of the Metaphysic of Morals, First Section, trans. T. K. Abbott
label.zh: 康德《道德形而上学奠基》第一章，阿博特 英译

claim.en: Croce held that strength of will is a real excellence of its own, one we admire even in Machiavelli's prince or in Iago, and that the moral person is the one who joins that same force to good will. On his terms the good leader is not the gentle one but the one who has both.
claim.zh: 克罗齐认为，意志的力量本身就是一种真正的优点，连马基雅维利笔下的君主或伊阿古身上的这种力量，我们也会钦佩；而有德之人，就是把同样的力量与善良意志结合起来的人。照他的说法，好的领导者不是温和的人，而是两者兼备的人。

detail.en: Croce was writing a treatise on aesthetics and the theory of the will, not advice on choosing leaders; applying it here is ours. The cost is that he names the union without saying what to do when the strong-willed candidate and the good one are different people, which is the choice the question actually poses.
detail.zh: 克罗齐写的是一部关于美学和意志理论的著作，不是挑选领导者的建议；把它用在这里是我们的引申。代价是：他指出了两者的结合，却没有说当意志坚强的人选和善良的人选是两个人时该怎么办，而这恰恰是这个问题真正要人做的选择。

quote.en: The moral man unites with the pertinacity and fearlessness of a Caesar Borgia, of an Iago, or of a ser Ciappelletto, the good will of the saint or of the hero.
quote.zh: The moral man unites with the pertinacity and fearlessness of a Caesar Borgia, of an Iago, or of a ser Ciappelletto, the good will of the saint or of the hero.

label.en: Benedetto Croce, Aesthetic as Science of Expression and General Linguistic, trans. Douglas Ainslie
label.zh: 克罗齐《作为表现的科学和一般语言学的美学》，安斯利 英译

claim.en: Hume argued that the rules of justice exist because they serve the public good, so in an emergency the safety of the people outranks them. On that view a leader is measured by what the rules are for, not by how faithfully they are kept.
claim.zh: 休谟主张，正义的规则之所以存在，是因为它们服务于公共利益；所以在危急时刻，人民的安全高于这些规则。照这个看法，衡量领导者要看规则是为了什么，而不是看规则被守得多严。

detail.en: Hume's examples are sieges, famines and shipwrecks, where ordinary rules of property give way; extending that to everyday leadership is our application. Unlike Hobbes, he grounds justice itself in public usefulness rather than in the sovereign's office. The weakness is that an emergency is easy to declare, and Hume offers no check on the person who declares it.
detail.zh: 休谟举的例子是围城、饥荒和船难，在这些情形下，平常的财产规则会让步；把它推广到日常的领导，是我们的引申。与霍布斯不同，他把正义本身建立在公共效用上，而不是建立在主权者的职责上。弱点是：紧急状态很容易宣布，而对宣布它的人，休谟没有给出任何约束。

quote.en: The safety of the people is the supreme law: All other particular laws are subordinate to it, and dependent on it: And if, in the COMMON course of things, they be followed and regarded; it is only because the public safety and interest COMMONLY demand so equal and impartial an administration.
quote.zh: The safety of the people is the supreme law: All other particular laws are subordinate to it, and dependent on it: And if, in the COMMON course of things, they be followed and regarded; it is only because the public safety and interest COMMONLY demand so equal and impartial an administration.

label.en: David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals, Section III
label.zh: 大卫·休谟《道德原则研究》第三章

claim.en: Emerson dismisses luck as the explanation shallow people reach for. In his view fortunes are fruits: what happens to a person grows out of what they think and do.
claim.zh: 爱默生把运气斥为浅薄之人的解释。在他看来，财富是果实：一个人遭遇的事，从他的所思所为中生长出来。

detail.en: It is a bracing view and a flattering one for the successful. The cost is that it has no room for the lottery of birth, timing or health, and it quietly implies the unlucky are shallow.
detail.zh: 这是一种令人振奋的看法，也很讨成功者欢心。代价是：它没有给出身、时机或健康的偶然性留下位置，还暗含着不走运的人就是浅薄的。

quote.en: Shallow men believe in luck, believe in circumstances: It was somebody's name, or he happened to be there at the time, or, it was so then, and another day it would have been otherwise. Strong men believe in cause and effect.
quote.zh: Shallow men believe in luck, believe in circumstances: It was somebody's name, or he happened to be there at the time, or, it was so then, and another day it would have been otherwise. Strong men believe in cause and effect.

origin.zh: 马萨诸塞州康科德，1860 年

label.en: Ralph Waldo Emerson, The Conduct of Life, "Worship"
label.zh: 爱默生《生活的准则》〈崇拜〉

claim.en: Spencer's formula for justice is that each person should receive the good and bad results of their own nature and conduct. A great fortune, on this view, is what justice looks like when the conduct was effective.
claim.zh: 斯宾塞的正义公式是：每个人都应承受自己天性和行为所带来的好与坏的结果。照此看法，巨额财富正是行为卓有成效时正义的样子。

detail.en: Spencer's view grew out of the biology that gave us 'survival of the fittest', a phrase he coined, and it was widely used to defend inequality. The cost: 'his own nature' includes inheritance he did nothing to earn, which the formula counts as his anyway.
detail.zh: 斯宾塞的观点源自催生「适者生存」一词的生物学——这个说法正是他创造的——并被广泛用来为不平等辩护。代价是：「他自己的天性」包括他毫无功劳的遗传，而公式照样把这些算作他的。

quote.en: ethically considered, this law implies that each individual ought to receive the benefits and the evils of his own nature and consequent conduct
quote.zh: ethically considered, this law implies that each individual ought to receive the benefits and the evils of his own nature and consequent conduct

label.en: Herbert Spencer, The Principles of Ethics, vol. II, Part IV "Justice", ch. III
label.zh: 斯宾塞《伦理学原理》第二卷第四部分〈正义〉第三章

claim.en: Smith noticed that we defer to the rich not because we expect anything from them but because we admire their situation. That admiration comes first; the story of their merit comes after.
claim.zh: 斯密注意到，我们顺从富人，并不是因为指望从他们那里得到什么，而是因为仰慕他们的处境。仰慕在先，关于他们才德的故事在后。

detail.en: If he is right, the question 'earned or luck?' is one we are badly placed to answer, because our judgement is tilted before we look. The cost is that this explains our bias without settling the case either way.
detail.zh: 如果他是对的，「挣来的还是运气」就是一个我们很难回答的问题，因为在我们审视之前，判断已经倾斜了。代价是：这解释了我们的偏见，却没有对问题本身作出裁决。

quote.en: Our obsequiousness to our superiors more frequently arises from our admiration for the advantages of their situation, than from any private expectations of benefit from their good-will.
quote.zh: Our obsequiousness to our superiors more frequently arises from our admiration for the advantages of their situation, than from any private expectations of benefit from their good-will.

label.en: Adam Smith, The Theory of Moral Sentiments, Part I, sect. III, ch. 2
label.zh: 亚当·斯密《道德情操论》第一卷第三篇第二章

claim.en: Kropotkin argued that no invention is anyone's alone: each rests on the work of millions, known and unknown, past and present. A single fortune claims a shared inheritance.
claim.zh: 克鲁泡特金认为，没有哪项发明完全属于某一个人：每一项都建立在千百万已知与未知、过去与现在的人的劳动之上。一笔个人财富，占有的是一份共同遗产。

detail.en: This sidesteps both 'earned' and 'luck': the fortune may reflect real skill, but the ground it stands on belongs to everyone. The cost is that it gives no account of why some people combine that inheritance far better than others.
detail.zh: 这绕开了「挣来」与「运气」两种答案：财富也许反映了真实的才能，但它所立足的土地属于所有人。代价是：它无法解释为什么有些人能把这份遗产组合得比别人好得多。

quote.en: There is not even a thought, or an invention, which is not common property, born of the past and the present.
quote.zh: There is not even a thought, or an invention, which is not common property, born of the past and the present.

label.en: Peter Kropotkin, The Conquest of Bread, ch. I
label.zh: 克鲁泡特金《面包与自由》第一章

claim.en: Marx's answer is neither merit nor chance: capital grows by drawing on the labour of others. A fortune is, on this account, mostly other people's work in stored form.
claim.zh: 马克思的回答既不是才德也不是运气：资本靠汲取他人的劳动而增长。照此说法，一笔财富大体上是以储存形式存在的他人劳动。

detail.en: This is the most contested answer here, resting on the labour theory of value that most economists reject. The cost is that it leaves no space for value created by organising, risking or inventing, which many would say is exactly what founders do.
detail.zh: 这是这里最具争议的回答，它建立在大多数经济学家都不接受的劳动价值论之上。代价是：它没有给组织、冒险或发明所创造的价值留下空间，而许多人会说，创始人做的恰恰是这些。

quote.en: Capital is dead labour, that vampire-like, only lives by sucking living labour, and lives the more, the more labour it sucks.
quote.zh: Capital is dead labour, that vampire-like, only lives by sucking living labour, and lives the more, the more labour it sucks.

label.en: Karl Marx, Capital, vol. I, ch. X, trans. Samuel Moore and Edward Aveling
label.zh: 马克思《资本论》第一卷第十章，穆尔与艾威林 英译

claim.en: Machiavelli observed that a ruler who wins and holds power will have his means judged honest and be praised by everyone, because most people judge by appearances and outcomes. Success writes its own character reference.
claim.zh: 马基雅维利观察到，一个夺得并守住权力的君主，他的手段总会被认为是正当的，人人都会称赞他，因为多数人只凭表象和结果来判断。成功会替自己写好品行证明。

detail.en: He was writing about princes, not fortunes, and the step to how we judge the rich is ours. Where Smith traces our deference to the pleasures of wealth, Machiavelli traces it to the result: whoever won is assumed to have deserved it. The cost is that this explains the praise without telling us whether it is ever earned, and The Prince's own tone is contested; some have read it as satire.
detail.zh: 他写的是君主而不是财富，把它推到我们如何看待富人，是我们的引申。斯密把我们对富人的顺从归于财富带来的愉悦，马基雅维利则归于结果：赢了的人，就被认定是配得上赢的。代价是：这解释了赞誉从何而来，却说不出赞誉是否属实；而且《君主论》本身的语气有争议，有人把它读作讽刺。

quote.en: let a prince have the credit of conquering and holding his state, the means will always be considered honest, and he will be praised by everybody; because the vulgar are always taken by what a thing seems to be and by what comes of it
quote.zh: let a prince have the credit of conquering and holding his state, the means will always be considered honest, and he will be praised by everybody; because the vulgar are always taken by what a thing seems to be and by what comes of it

label.en: Niccolò Machiavelli, The Prince, ch. XVIII, trans. W. K. Marriott
label.zh: 马基雅维利《君主论》第十八章，马里奥特 英译

claim.en: Gilman held that the power to make things belongs to society as a whole, and that individuals are its parts. Wealth, on her view, is social wealth before it is anyone's fortune.
claim.zh: 吉尔曼认为，制造东西的能力属于整个社会，个人只是社会的组成部分。照她的看法，财富首先是社会的财富，然后才是某个人的家产。

detail.en: She did not deny that individuals work hard; she denied that their output can be separated from the society that trained, fed and equipped them. Applying this to a single modern fortune is our step. Her social theory is heavily disputed, and treating society as one organism can leave the individual with no claim to anything.
detail.zh: 她并不否认个人勤奋；她否认的是，个人的产出能与培养、供养和装备他的社会分开。把这用在某一笔现代巨富上，是我们的引申。她的社会理论争议很大，而把社会当成一个有机体，可能让个人对任何东西都失去正当的主张。

quote.en: Society is a unit, we are but parts. Social life develops the power to make things—the things which are essential to social life. Increase in these things is increase in social wealth and social power—a ceaseless line of development.
quote.zh: Society is a unit, we are but parts. Social life develops the power to make things—the things which are essential to social life. Increase in these things is increase in social wealth and social power—a ceaseless line of development.

label.en: Charlotte Perkins Gilman, Human Work
label.zh: 吉尔曼《人类的工作》

claim.en: Godwin held that almost all wealth is produced by the daily labour of people now living, and that an inherited title is only a licence to collect what others have made.
claim.zh: 葛德文认为，几乎所有财富都是由当下活着的人日复一日的劳动生产出来的，而继承来的产权只是一张收取他人劳动成果的执照。

detail.en: Godwin was writing about inherited estates in 1790s England, and extending him to self-made fortunes is ours; it would need the founder's own work to count for little. Unlike Marx, he wanted no seizure: he argued that equalising property by force would fail, and that only a change of opinion could fix it. The cost is that his remedy is slow and may never come.
detail.zh: 葛德文写的是 18 世纪 90 年代英国的继承财产，把他推到白手起家的巨富身上是我们的引申；那样就得认定创始人自己的劳动无足轻重。与马克思不同，他不主张剥夺：他论证说用强力拉平财产会失败，只有观念的改变才能纠正。代价是：他的药方见效极慢，也许永远不会到来。

quote.en: The property is produced by the daily labour of men who are now in existence. All that their ancestors bequeathed to them was a mouldy patent, which they show, as a title to extort from their neighbours what the labour of those neighbours has produced.
quote.zh: The property is produced by the daily labour of men who are now in existence. All that their ancestors bequeathed to them was a mouldy patent, which they show, as a title to extort from their neighbours what the labour of those neighbours has produced.

label.en: William Godwin, An Enquiry Concerning Political Justice, Book VIII
label.zh: 葛德文《政治正义论》第八卷

claim.en: Spinoza held that a feeling that rules us loses its grip once we understand it clearly. On this view, suspicion feeds on half-knowledge, and clearer knowledge would free you from it.
claim.zh: 斯宾诺莎认为，一种支配我们的情感，一旦被我们清楚地理解，就会失去控制力。照此看法，猜疑以一知半解为食，更清楚的认识会让你摆脱它。

detail.en: Spinoza meant understanding the causes of your own emotion, not reading someone's messages; the inference is ours. The cost is that some facts, once known, produce new passions instead of dissolving old ones.
detail.zh: 斯宾诺莎说的是理解自身情感的成因，而不是查看别人的消息；推论是我们的。代价是：有些事实一旦知道，产生的是新的激情，而不是消解旧的。

quote.en: An emotion, which is a passion, ceases to be a passion, as soon as we form a clear and distinct idea thereof.
quote.zh: An emotion, which is a passion, ceases to be a passion, as soon as we form a clear and distinct idea thereof.

label.en: Baruch Spinoza, Ethics, Part V, Prop. III, trans. R. H. M. Elwes
label.zh: 斯宾诺莎《伦理学》第五部分命题三，埃尔维斯 英译

claim.en: Pascal thought that if everyone knew what everyone else said about them, friendship would barely survive. Some not-knowing is part of what holds people together.
claim.zh: 帕斯卡认为，如果每个人都知道别人在背后怎么说自己，友谊就几乎无法存活。某种程度的不知道，正是把人们维系在一起的东西。

detail.en: He wrote about friends, not partners; the extension is ours. The cost is that this can excuse real deception, and it leaves the person kept in the dark with no say in the bargain.
detail.zh: 他写的是朋友，不是伴侣；延伸是我们的推论。代价是：这可能为真正的欺骗开脱，而且被蒙在鼓里的人在这笔交易中毫无发言权。

quote.en: I put it down as a fact that if all men knew what each said of the other, there would not be four friends in the world.
quote.zh: I put it down as a fact that if all men knew what each said of the other, there would not be four friends in the world.

label.en: Blaise Pascal, Thoughts (Pensées), trans. C. Kegan Paul
label.zh: 帕斯卡《思想录》，凯根·保罗 英译

claim.en: Montaigne, who loved his family, still kept a back room of the mind entirely his own — free, private, closed to everyone, spouse included.
claim.zh: 蒙田爱他的家人，却依然为自己保留一间完全属于自己的心灵后屋——自由、私密，对所有人关闭，包括配偶。

detail.en: On this view a partner's privacy is not a threat to love but a condition of a self worth loving. The cost is that Montaigne doesn't say where a private room ends and a hidden life begins.
detail.zh: 照此看法，伴侣的隐私不是对爱的威胁，而是一个值得被爱的自我得以存在的条件。代价是：蒙田没有说明，私人空间在哪里结束，隐秘生活又从哪里开始。

quote.en: we must reserve a backshop, wholly our own and entirely free, wherein to settle our true liberty, our principal solitude and retreat.
quote.zh: we must reserve a backshop, wholly our own and entirely free, wherein to settle our true liberty, our principal solitude and retreat.

label.en: Michel de Montaigne, Essays, Book I, ch. 38 "Of Solitude", trans. Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt
label.zh: 蒙田《随笔集》第一卷第三十八章〈论孤独〉，科顿 英译，黑兹利特 编

claim.en: Nietzsche thought depth and concealment go together: what is deepest in a person hides even from likeness. Demanding total transparency would flatten the very thing you love.
claim.zh: 尼采认为深度与掩藏相伴：一个人身上最深的东西，甚至连形象和比喻都躲避。要求完全透明，会把你所爱的东西本身压平。

detail.en: Nietzsche was not writing about couples; the application is ours. The cost is that 'everything profound loves the mask' is also what everyone with something shabby to hide would like to believe.
detail.zh: 尼采写的不是伴侣关系；应用是我们的推论。代价是：「一切深刻的东西都爱面具」，也正是每个藏着见不得人之事的人乐于相信的话。

quote.en: Everything that is profound loves the mask: the profoundest things have a hatred even of figure and likeness.
quote.zh: Everything that is profound loves the mask: the profoundest things have a hatred even of figure and likeness.

label.en: Friedrich Nietzsche, Beyond Good and Evil, §40, trans. Helen Zimmern
label.zh: 尼采《善恶的彼岸》第 40 节，齐默恩 英译

claim.en: Freud's claim is that the self is not master in its own house: much of what drives us is unconscious. A partner cannot show you everything they hide, because they do not know it all themselves.
claim.zh: 弗洛伊德的观点是，自我并不是自己家中的主人：驱动我们的很多东西是无意识的。伴侣无法把隐藏的一切都给你看，因为他们自己也并不全知道。

detail.en: This reframes the question from secrecy to self-knowledge. The cost is that psychoanalysis is contested as science, and 'they don't know themselves' can become a way to dismiss what a partner does say.
detail.zh: 这把问题从保密转向了自我认识。代价是：精神分析作为科学是有争议的，而「他们自己也不知道」可能成为无视伴侣真实表达的说辞。

quote.en: it is not even master in its own home, but is dependent upon the most scanty information concerning all that goes on unconsciously in its psychic life.
quote.zh: it is not even master in its own home, but is dependent upon the most scanty information concerning all that goes on unconsciously in its psychic life.

label.en: Sigmund Freud, A General Introduction to Psychoanalysis, Lecture 18 (1920 English edition)
label.zh: 弗洛伊德《精神分析引论》第十八讲（1920 年英译本）

claim.en: Bacon held that suspicion grows from knowing little, and that the cure is to find out more rather than let suspicion smoulder. Ignorance, not knowledge, is what feeds distrust.
claim.zh: 培根认为，猜疑源于所知太少，补救的办法是去了解更多，而不是让猜疑闷在心里。滋养不信任的是无知，而不是知情。

detail.en: Bacon was advising people on those they 'employ and deal with', and in the same essay he tells them not to expect others to be saints; applying it to a partner's phone is ours. The cost is that he assumes what you learn will settle the suspicion, when some of it will start new ones.
detail.zh: 培根是在劝人看待那些与自己共事往来的人，并在同一篇里提醒不要指望别人是圣人；把它用到伴侣的手机上是我们的推论。代价是：他假定知道的东西会平息猜疑，而有些东西反而会引出新的猜疑。

quote.en: There is nothing makes a man suspect much, more than to know little; and therefore men should remedy suspicion, by procuring to know more, and not to keep their suspicions in smother.
quote.zh: There is nothing makes a man suspect much, more than to know little; and therefore men should remedy suspicion, by procuring to know more, and not to keep their suspicions in smother.

label.en: Francis Bacon, Essays, "Of Suspicion"
label.zh: 培根《随笔集》〈论猜疑〉

claim.en: Emerson held that a friend should stay something of a stranger, revered rather than possessed, because what is finest in a person cannot be seen from too close. Distance is what lets the other remain worth loving.
claim.zh: 爱默生认为，朋友应当始终保留几分陌生，被敬重而不是被占有，因为一个人身上最美好的东西，靠得太近反而看不见。距离让对方始终值得爱。

detail.en: Emerson was writing about friendship, not marriage or romance, so carrying it to partners is ours. The cost is that his ideal is austere: it asks for a distance and a reserve that few couples sharing a home could live by.
detail.zh: 爱默生写的是友谊，不是婚姻或爱情，把它用到伴侣身上是我们的推论。代价是：他的理想很清苦，要求的距离和矜持，同住一个屋檐下的伴侣很少能照此生活。

quote.en: Let him be to thee for ever a sort of beautiful enemy, untamable, devoutly revered, and not a trivial conveniency to be soon outgrown and cast aside. The hues of the opal, the light of the diamond, are not to be seen if the eye is too near.
quote.zh: Let him be to thee for ever a sort of beautiful enemy, untamable, devoutly revered, and not a trivial conveniency to be soon outgrown and cast aside. The hues of the opal, the light of the diamond, are not to be seen if the eye is too near.

origin.zh: 马萨诸塞州康科德，1841 年

label.en: Ralph Waldo Emerson, Essays: First Series, "Friendship"
label.zh: 爱默生《随笔集·第一辑》〈友谊〉

claim.en: Augustine held that there is something in a person that even their own spirit does not know, and that only God knows anyone wholly. No partner could hand over the whole of themselves, because they do not have it.
claim.zh: 奥古斯丁认为，人身上有些东西，连他自己的心灵也不知道，只有上帝完全认识一个人。没有哪个伴侣能把自己的全部交出来，因为他们自己也并不拥有全部。

detail.en: This is a religious teaching: Augustine's point is that full self-knowledge belongs to God, and the application to partners is ours. It reaches the same answer as Freud by another road. The weakness is that it settles what can be known, not whether you should try to know what can.
detail.zh: 这是一种宗教教导：奥古斯丁的意思是，完全的自我认识属于上帝，把它用到伴侣身上是我们的推论。它经由另一条路，得出了与弗洛伊德相同的结论。弱点是：它回答了什么是可知的，却没有回答对于可知的部分，你是否应该去探知。

quote.en: although no man knoweth the things of a man, but the spirit of a man which is in him, yet is there something of man, which neither the spirit of man that is in him, itself knoweth.
quote.zh: although no man knoweth the things of a man, but the spirit of a man which is in him, yet is there something of man, which neither the spirit of man that is in him, itself knoweth.

label.en: Augustine, Confessions, Book X, ch. 5, trans. E. B. Pusey
label.zh: 奥古斯丁《忏悔录》第十卷第五章，璞赛 英译

claim.en: Plato's argument runs the other way from ours: good people will never seek office for money or honour, so they have to be compelled, and the compulsion is simply the prospect of being ruled by someone worse.
claim.zh: 柏拉图的论证与我们的直觉相反：好人不会为了钱或名声去求官，所以必须有所强迫，而这种强迫就是——不上任，就会被更差的人统治。

detail.en: On this reading, reluctance is close to a qualification rather than a disqualification. The cost is that the argument assumes someone can reliably tell who the 'best' are, and Plato's rulers had been trained for decades for the job; a gifted person pressed into office untrained may rule badly and resentfully.
detail.zh: 照这个读法，不情愿几乎是一种资格，而不是失格。代价是：这个论证假定有人能可靠地认出谁是「最好的人」，而柏拉图笔下的统治者为此受过几十年的训练；一个未经训练、被硬推上任的天才，可能治理得既差又心怀怨气。

quote.en: Now the worst part of the punishment is that he who refuses to rule is liable to be ruled by one who is worse than himself.
quote.zh: Now the worst part of the punishment is that he who refuses to rule is liable to be ruled by one who is worse than himself.

label.en: Plato, Republic, Book I (347c), trans. Benjamin Jowett
label.zh: 柏拉图《理想国》第一卷（347c），乔伊特 英译

claim.en: Mill's harm principle, read strictly, leaves no room to conscript someone into office: declining to rule does not harm others in the sense Mill meant, so power over that person has no warrant.
claim.zh: 严格按密尔的「伤害原则」来读，就没有理由把一个人征召上任：拒绝当领导，并不构成密尔所说的对他人的伤害，因此对这个人施加权力就没有正当依据。

detail.en: The inference is ours, not Mill's — he never discussed drafting a president. The cost is real: elsewhere Mill wanted the most capable to carry more weight in public life, and a society that respects every refusal may watch its best people choose private life.
detail.zh: 这是我们的推论，不是密尔的原话——他从未讨论过征召总统。代价也是真实的：密尔在别处希望最有能力的人在公共生活中有更大分量，而一个尊重每一次拒绝的社会，可能眼看着最优秀的人退回私人生活。

quote.en: That the only purpose for which power can be rightfully exercised over any member of a civilised community, against his will, is to prevent harm to others.
quote.zh: That the only purpose for which power can be rightfully exercised over any member of a civilised community, against his will, is to prevent harm to others.

label.en: John Stuart Mill, On Liberty, ch. I
label.zh: 约翰·斯图亚特·密尔《论自由》第一章

claim.en: The Analects treat stepping forward or staying out of sight as a judgement about the state of the country — not a duty owed to it on demand.
claim.zh: 《论语》把出仕还是隐退看作对国家状况的判断，而不是国家一开口就必须履行的义务。

detail.en: Applied to today, a capable person who declines may be passing a verdict on the system they would have to serve; forcing them answers the wrong question. The cost is that anyone can decide the country is badly governed and stay out for good.
detail.zh: 放到今天，一个有能力却拒绝出来的人，可能是在对他将要服务的体制下判断；强迫他上任，回答的是错误的问题。代价是：任何人都可以认定国家治理不善，从而永远置身事外。

quote.en: When right principles of government prevail in the kingdom, he will show himself; when they are prostrated, he will keep concealed.
quote.zh: 天下有道則見，無道則隱。

label.en: Confucius, Analects 8.13, trans. James Legge
label.zh: 《论语·泰伯》8.13，理雅各 英译

claim.en: In Mencius' account even a sage-king could not hand over the empire: he could only put a candidate forward, and Heaven and the people had to accept him. Talent nominates; acceptance decides.
claim.zh: 在孟子的叙述里，即使是圣王也不能私相授受天下：他只能推荐人选，必须由天与民接受。才能只是提名，认可才是决定。

detail.en: Read across 2,300 years, this suggests nobody becomes a rightful ruler by being drafted for their brilliance. The cost is that Mencius reads 'the people accepted him' from signs and conduct, not a count — a claim that is easy for any ruler to make.
detail.zh: 跨越两千三百年来读，这意味着没有人会因为聪明被征召就成为正当的统治者。代价是：孟子说的「民受之」是从迹象和行事中看出来的，不是点票的结果——任何统治者都很容易这样宣称。

quote.en: Anciently Yaou presented Shun to Heaven, and Heaven accepted him; he displayed him to the people, and the people accepted him.
quote.zh: 昔者堯薦舜於天而天受之，暴之於民而民受之。

label.en: Mencius 5A.5, trans. James Legge, The Life and Works of Mencius (1875)
label.zh: 《孟子·万章上》5A.5，理雅各 英译（1875）

claim.en: Augustine held that a person drawn to study and quiet is free to stay there unless the burden of governing is laid on them; then love obliges them to take it up. The call comes from others, not from ambition.
claim.zh: 奥古斯丁认为，一个向往研读与清静的人可以安于其中，除非治理的重担被加在他身上；那时，爱使他不得不承担。召唤来自他人，而不是来自野心。

detail.en: Augustine was writing about Christians called to office, as he himself had been ordained against his will; applying it to a president is ours. Plato compels the good with the threat of being ruled by worse, while Augustine grounds the duty in love of neighbour. What he leaves open is who has the right to lay the burden on someone, which is the whole of this question.
detail.zh: 奥古斯丁写的是被召去担任职务的基督徒，他自己当年就是违背本意被授予圣职的；把它用到总统身上，是我们的引申。柏拉图用被更差的人统治来强迫好人，奥古斯丁则把这份责任建立在对邻人的爱上。他没有回答的是：谁有权把重担加给一个人，而这正是本题的全部所在。

quote.en: And therefore holy leisure is longed for by the love of truth; but it is the necessity of love to undertake requisite business. If no one imposes this burden upon us, we are free to sift and contemplate truth; but if it be laid upon us, we are necessitated for love's sake to undertake it.
quote.zh: And therefore holy leisure is longed for by the love of truth; but it is the necessity of love to undertake requisite business. If no one imposes this burden upon us, we are free to sift and contemplate truth; but if it be laid upon us, we are necessitated for love's sake to undertake it.

label.en: Augustine, The City of God, Book XIX, ch. 19, trans. Marcus Dods
label.zh: 奥古斯丁《上帝之城》第十九卷第十九章，多兹 英译

claim.en: Montaigne held that a person may lend themselves to others but should give themselves only to themselves. Chosen mayor of Bordeaux while abroad, he served, and kept the office at arm's length.
claim.zh: 蒙田认为，人可以把自己借给别人，但只应把自己交给自己。他身在国外时被选为波尔多市长，他接受了，却始终与这个职位保持距离。

detail.en: Montaigne did not refuse: he asked to be excused, was told the king wanted it, and took the post. So his answer is not a simple no; what he denies is that an office can claim the whole person. Applying this to a national draft is ours, and the cost is plain: a leader who serves at arm's length may be what a crisis can least afford.
detail.zh: 蒙田并没有拒绝：他请求免任，被告知国王也有此意，于是就任。所以他的回答不是简单的不；他否认的是职位可以占有整个人。把它用到全国性的征召上，是我们的引申；代价也很明显：一个与职位保持距离的领导者，可能正是危机时期最承受不起的。

quote.en: But against such affections as wholly carry me away from myself and fix me elsewhere, against those, I say, I oppose myself with my utmost power. ‘Tis my opinion that a man should lend himself to others, and only give himself to himself.
quote.zh: But against such affections as wholly carry me away from myself and fix me elsewhere, against those, I say, I oppose myself with my utmost power. ‘Tis my opinion that a man should lend himself to others, and only give himself to himself.

label.en: Michel de Montaigne, Essays, Book III, ch. 10 "Of Managing the Will", trans. Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt
label.zh: 蒙田《随笔集》第三卷第十章〈论意志的掌控〉，科顿 英译，黑兹利特 编

claim.en: Thoreau held that an honest man could not, without disgrace, be associated with a government that upheld slavery. Whether to serve a state depends first on what that state is doing.
claim.zh: 梭罗认为，一个正直的人不能与维护奴隶制的政府为伍而不蒙羞。是否为一个国家效力，首先取决于这个国家在做什么。

detail.en: Thoreau was writing about allegiance and taxes in 1849, not about taking office; applying it to a drafted leader is ours. Unlike the Confucian advice to keep hidden in bad times, his reason is complicity rather than prudence. The weakness is that a country which most needs its best people is usually one in trouble, and his test would keep them away.
detail.zh: 梭罗在 1849 年写的是效忠和纳税，而不是出任公职；把它用到被征召的领导者身上，是我们的引申。与儒家无道则隐的劝告不同，他的理由是不愿同流合污，而不是明哲保身。弱点是：一个国家最需要其最优秀的人时，往往正是它陷入困境之时，而他的标准会让这些人远离。

quote.en: How does it become a man to behave toward the American government today? I answer that he cannot without disgrace be associated with it.
quote.zh: How does it become a man to behave toward the American government today? I answer that he cannot without disgrace be associated with it.

origin.zh: 马萨诸塞州康科德，1849 年

label.en: Henry David Thoreau, "Civil Disobedience" (1849)
label.zh: 梭罗〈论公民的不服从〉（1849）

claim.en: Mencius admits plainly that he wants both things. When they can't be had together, he gives up the lesser for the greater — even life for what is right.
claim.zh: 孟子坦白承认两样他都想要。当二者不可兼得时，他舍弃较轻的，选择较重的——甚至为义舍生。

detail.en: Applied to work, the honest person is not a fool who misread the game but someone who ranked what they wanted. The cost is that the passage is about life and death; most corner-cutting is grey, and Mencius gives little help with small, frequent compromises.
detail.zh: 用在工作上，诚实的人不是看不懂游戏规则的傻子，而是把自己想要的东西排了序。代价是：这段话讲的是生死；大多数走捷径是灰色的，而对于那些小而频繁的妥协，孟子帮不上太多忙。

quote.en: I like fish, and I also like bears' paws. If I cannot get both together, I will let the fish go, and take the bears' paws. So I like life, and I also like righteousness. If I cannot keep the two together, I will let life go, and choose righteousness.
quote.zh: 魚，我所欲也；熊掌，亦我所欲也。二者不可得兼，舍魚而取熊掌者也。生，亦我所欲也；義，亦我所欲也。二者不可得兼，舍生而取義者也。

label.en: Mencius 6A.10, trans. James Legge, The Life and Works of Mencius (1875)
label.zh: 《孟子·告子上》6A.10，理雅各 英译（1875）

claim.en: Kant's test asks whether you could will your rule to be everyone's. 'Everyone cuts corners' is not an excuse under it; it is the test already failed, out in the open.
claim.zh: 康德的检验是：你能否意愿自己的准则成为所有人的法则。在这个检验下，「大家都走捷径」不是借口，而是这个检验已经公开失败的样子。

detail.en: On this view, how many others break the rule has no bearing on whether you should. The cost is that the test is silent about consequences: you may keep your integrity and lose your job, and Kant offers no comfort for that.
detail.zh: 照此看法，有多少人违规，与你该不该违规毫无关系。代价是：这个检验对后果保持沉默——你可能保住了正直却丢了工作，而康德对此不提供任何安慰。

quote.en: I am never to act otherwise than so that I could also will that my maxim should become a universal law.
quote.zh: I am never to act otherwise than so that I could also will that my maxim should become a universal law.

label.en: Immanuel Kant, Groundwork of the Metaphysic of Morals, First Section, trans. T. K. Abbott
label.zh: 康德《道德形而上学奠基》第一章，阿博特 英译

claim.en: Epictetus treats every advantage as having a price. The one who flattered got the dinner; you kept what you would have paid. You did not lose the deal — you declined it.
claim.zh: 爱比克泰德认为每一种好处都有价码。奉承的人得到了晚宴；你保住了本要付出的东西。你不是输了这笔交易，而是拒绝了它。

detail.en: This recasts 'losing' as a trade made with open eyes, not foolishness. The cost is that Stoic accounting can feel thin when the price is your rent; it tells you what you kept, not how to live on it.
detail.zh: 这把「输」重新理解为一次清醒的交换，而不是愚蠢。代价是：当代价是你的房租时，斯多葛式的算账可能显得单薄；它告诉你保住了什么，却没告诉你靠什么生活。

quote.en: If then a man gives up the obolus, and receives the lettuces, and if you do not give up the obolus and do not obtain the lettuces, do not suppose that you receive less than he who has got the lettuces; for as he has the lettuces, so you have the obolus which you did not give.
quote.zh: If then a man gives up the obolus, and receives the lettuces, and if you do not give up the obolus and do not obtain the lettuces, do not suppose that you receive less than he who has got the lettuces; for as he has the lettuces, so you have the obolus which you did not give.

origin.zh: 尼科波利斯，约公元 125 年

label.en: Epictetus, Enchiridion 25, trans. George Long
label.zh: 爱比克泰德《手册》第 25 节，朗 英译

claim.en: Hobbes saw that keeping a bargain alone, where nobody enforces it, only exposes you to those who won't. Where corners are cut everywhere, the real failure is the absence of a power that makes rules binding.
claim.zh: 霍布斯看到，在没有人强制执行的地方，独自守约只会让你暴露在不守约的人面前。在人人都走捷径的地方，真正的失败是缺少一个能让规则生效的权力。

detail.en: On this reading you are not a fool for keeping the rules, but neither are you obliged to be the only one — the fix is enforcement, not heroism. Hobbes also argued elsewhere that breaking covenants is against reason once a common power exists. The cost: waiting for a referee can become an excuse to join in.
detail.zh: 照这个读法，守规矩不是傻，但你也没有义务做唯一守规矩的人——解决办法是执法，而不是英雄主义。霍布斯在别处也论证过，一旦存在共同权力，背约就违背理性。代价是：等待裁判，可能变成随波逐流的借口。

quote.en: For he that performeth first, has no assurance the other will performe after; because the bonds of words are too weak to bridle mens ambition, avarice, anger, and other Passions, without the feare of some coerceive Power
