label.en: Aristotle, Politics, Book II, Chapter III, 1261b, trans. Benjamin Jowett
label.zh: 亚里士多德《政治学》第二卷第三章 1261b，乔伊特 英译

claim.en: Not every decision should begin with the question of profit. Reproduction belongs inside a network of duties and relationships, so turning genetic material into a price competition risks letting gain determine something that should first be judged by what is right.
claim.zh: 不是每件事都应该先问能赚多少钱。生育存在于一整套责任和关系之中，如果把遗传材料变成价格竞争，就可能让利益决定原本应该先由「义」判断的事情。

detail.en: Confucius never discussed gamete donation, so this applies his distinction between yi, what is fitting or right, and li, profit. The cost of this position is that it restricts transactions even when both adults consent, because some relationships are understood to carry obligations that cannot be reduced to individual advantage.
detail.zh: 孔子当然没有讨论过配子捐赠；这里应用的是他对「义」和「利」的区分。这个立场的代价是，即使两个成年人都同意，一些交易仍可能受到限制，因为某些关系包含不能简化为个人利益的责任。

quote.en: The superior man understands what is right; the inferior man understands what is profitable.
quote.zh: 君子喻於義，小人喻於利。

label.en: Confucius, Analects 4.16, trans. based on James Legge
label.zh: 《论语·里仁》4.16，理雅各 英译

claim.en: Calling a sale voluntary does not tell you enough. When people have radically unequal resources, the market can turn economic necessity into a choice that looks free on paper.
claim.zh: 把一笔交易称为「自愿」还远远不够。当人们拥有的经济资源极不平等时，市场可以把经济压力变成一种纸面上看起来完全自由的选择。

detail.en: Applied to egg markets, Marx would push us to ask who is usually paying and who is taking hormones, undergoing procedures and accepting risk for money. The cost of refusing commodification is real too: restricting payment can reduce the supply of donor eggs and limit reproductive choices for people who need them.
detail.zh: 应用到卵子市场，马克思式的问题会是：通常是谁付钱，又是谁为了钱接受激素、医疗操作和身体风险？但拒绝商品化同样有代价：限制报酬可能减少卵子供给，也会限制需要捐赠卵子的人实现生育的机会。

quote.en: It is not the consciousness of men that determines their existence, but their social existence that determines their consciousness.
quote.zh: 不是人们的意识决定人们的存在，相反，是人们的社会存在决定人们的意识。

label.en: Karl Marx, A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy, Preface, trans. S. W. Ryazanskaya
label.zh: 卡尔·马克思《政治经济学批判》序言，梁赞斯卡娅 英译

claim.en: Birth is not merely the transfer of biological material. Every birth introduces a new person into a shared human world, so reproduction cannot be understood only as a private transaction between existing adults.
claim.zh: 出生并不只是生物材料的转移。每一次出生都会让一个全新的人进入共同的人类世界，因此生育不能只被理解为现有成年人之间的一笔私人交易。

detail.en: Arendt's concept of natality treats each birth as the appearance of someone genuinely new, not as the production of an object. Applied here, the future child creates moral interests that a pure property-right model misses; the cost is limiting adults' reproductive freedom for the sake of someone who does not yet exist.
detail.zh: 阿伦特的「诞生性」把每一个出生的人理解为真正的新开始，而不是被生产出来的物品。应用到这里，未来孩子本身带来了纯粹财产权模型无法涵盖的利益；代价则是为了一个尚未存在的人，限制现有成年人的生殖自由。

quote.en: The miracle that saves the world, the realm of human affairs, from its normal, 'natural' ruin is ultimately the fact of natality.
quote.zh: 最终把世界 — 这个人类事务的领域 — 从其正常的、「自然的」毁灭中拯救出来的奇迹，就是诞生这一事实。

label.en: Hannah Arendt, The Human Condition, Chapter V, §34
label.zh: 汉娜·阿伦特《人的境况》第五章第 34 节

claim.en: Being remembered was never the point. Being here, without fear, while you are — that is the whole of it.
claim.zh: 被记住从来不是重点。趁你还在，无所畏惧地在这里 — 这就是全部。

detail.en: Epicurus is making a logical point, not a consoling one: harm requires someone to be harmed, and death removes the subject along with the experience. His whole ethics follows from clearing away fears that cannot be cashed out — of gods, of the afterlife, of oblivion. Applied here, the question loses its sting: if being forgotten is a state you will never occupy, effort does not need posterity to justify it.
detail.zh: 伊壁鸠鲁给出的是逻辑论证而非安慰：伤害需要有一个被伤害者，而死亡在取走经验的同时也取走了主体。他的整个伦理学都建立在清除那些兑现不了的恐惧之上 — 对神、对来世、对湮灭的恐惧。用在这里，问题的刺就没了：如果「被遗忘」是一个你永远不会身处其中的状态，努力就不需要靠后世来证成。

quote.en: Death is nothing to us; for that which is dissolved is without sensation, and that which lacks sensation is nothing to us.
quote.zh: 死亡与我们无关：消散之物没有感觉，而没有感觉之物与我们无关。

label.en: Epicurus, Principal Doctrines II, trans. Robert Drew Hicks
label.zh: 伊壁鸠鲁《主要教义》第二条，希克斯 译

claim.en: The tree nobody wants for timber is the one that lives out its years.
claim.zh: 没人要拿去做木材的树，才能活满它的年岁。

detail.en: The line inverts the usual scale: usefulness is what gets a tree measured, felled and consumed, so uselessness is what lets it stand. Zhuangzi's recurring move is to show that the categories we rank things by are ours, not the world's. Against this question, he refuses the premise — a life assessed by what it produced was already being read on the wrong scale.
detail.zh: 这句话颠倒了通常的尺度：有用才会让一棵树被丈量、砍伐、消耗，所以无用才使它得以存留。庄子反复做的事，就是揭示我们用来排序的范畴属于我们，而非属于世界。面对这个问题，他拒绝其前提 — 一个以产出来评估的人生，本来就被放在错误的尺度上读。

quote.en: All men know the advantage of being useful, but no one knows the advantage of being useless.
quote.zh: 人皆知有用之用，而莫知无用之用也。

origin.zh: 中国，约公元前 4 世纪

label.en: Zhuangzi, Inner Chapters 4, trans. James Legge
label.zh: 《庄子·内篇·人间世》，理雅各 译

claim.en: You are held in place by obligations, not by an audience.
claim.zh: 把你固定在位置上的是义务，不是观众。

detail.en: The sentence reverses the anxiety in the question: the problem worth having is not that you go unrecognised but that you fail to recognise others. Confucius consistently redirects attention from standing to conduct — toward parents, colleagues, the people actually in front of you. On this reading being forgotten is not a loss at all, because the work was never addressed to an audience.
detail.zh: 这句话把问题里的焦虑反转了过来：值得担心的不是你不被了解，而是你不了解别人。孔子一贯把注意力从声名转向行事 — 转向父母、同僚、眼前的人。据此，被遗忘根本不是损失，因为那些工作从来就不是说给观众听的。

quote.en: I will not be afflicted at men's not knowing me; I will be afflicted that I do not know men.
quote.zh: 不患人之不己知，患不知人也。

label.en: Analects 1.16, trans. James Legge
label.zh: 《论语·学而》1.16，理雅各 译

claim.en: Meaning is not a reward collected at the end. It is found inside the situation you were handed.
claim.zh: 意义不是终点领取的奖赏，而是在你被交到手里的处境中被找到的。

detail.en: Frankl is naming what survived when everything measurable had been stripped away — status, work, family, future. What remained was the one thing no circumstance can confiscate: how you meet what is happening. That is why he answers this question from the side of contribution rather than legacy: meaning was never stored in the record, it was made in the encounter.
detail.zh: 弗兰克尔指认的，是当一切可衡量之物 — 地位、工作、家庭、未来 — 都被剥夺后仍然留存的东西：任何处境都无法没收的那一件，即你如何面对正在发生的事。这也是他从「贡献」而非「遗产」的一侧回答这个问题的原因：意义从未储存在记录里，它是在遭遇中生成的。

quote.en: Everything can be taken from a man but one thing: the last of the human freedoms — to choose one's attitude in any given set of circumstances.
quote.zh: 一切都可以从一个人身上被夺走，除了一件事：人类最后的自由 — 在任何既定处境中选择自己态度的自由。

label.en: Frankl, Man's Search for Meaning, part one
label.zh: 弗兰克尔《活出意义来》第一部

claim.en: What outlasts you is not the memory of you. It is what you started.
claim.zh: 比你活得久的不是关于你的记忆，而是你开启的事。

detail.en: Natality is Arendt's counterweight to mortality: the significant fact about a person is not that they end but that they begin things others carry on. She separates labour, consumed as it is produced, from action, which starts a chain no one controls. That reframes the question — what outlasts you is not a memory of you but a consequence, and consequences do not need to be attributed to keep running.
detail.zh: 「诞生性」是阿伦特对「必死性」的配重：关于一个人，重要的不是他会终结，而是他开启了他人得以延续之事。她区分随生产即被消耗的「劳动」，与启动一条无人能控制的链条的「行动」。这重构了问题 — 比你活得久的不是关于你的记忆，而是后果；而后果不需要被署名也照样运行。

quote.en: Men, though they must die, are not born in order to die but in order to begin.
quote.zh: 人虽必死，但生来不是为了死，而是为了开始。

label.en: Arendt, The Human Condition, §24
label.zh: 阿伦特《人的境况》第 24 节

claim.en: Everyone who might remember you is also dying. What is actually yours is this hour, and how you meet it.
claim.zh: 所有可能记得你的人也都在死去。真正属于你的是此刻这一小时，以及你如何面对它。

detail.en: An emperor writes this to himself, which is what gives it force: the person with the best claim to be remembered is talking himself out of wanting it. The reasoning is plain — the rememberers are as short-lived as the remembered, so fame is a loan from people who are themselves leaving. Against this question, he answers by relocating the whole of what is yours into the present hour.
detail.zh: 写下这句话的是一位皇帝 — 这正是它的力量所在：最有资格被记住的人，正在说服自己不要去想被记住。推理很朴素：记忆者与被记忆者同样短暂，所以名声是从同样正在离场的人那里借来的。面对这个问题，他的回答是把「属于你的一切」全部挪回此刻这一小时。

quote.en: Shortly thou wilt forget all things, and shortly all things will forget thee.
quote.zh: 不久你将遗忘万物，不久万物也将遗忘你。

label.en: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations VII.21, trans. George Long
label.zh: 马可·奥勒留《沉思录》7.21，朗 译

claim.en: It matters because you are going to die. The wish to leave something behind is that fear, given a respectable shape.
claim.zh: 它之所以重要，是因为你终将死去。「想留下点什么」正是这份恐惧，被赋予了体面的形状。

detail.en: Becker's opening claim is that mortality is not one anxiety among others but the one the rest are built to cover. Cultures, on his reading, supply respectable ways of not looking at it — and building something to outlast you is the most respectable of all. He does not deny that leaving something behind matters; he explains why it matters so much more than the reasons we give for it.
detail.zh: 贝克尔的开篇主张是：死亡不是众多焦虑中的一种，而是其余焦虑用来遮盖的那一种。在他看来，文化提供了体面的方式让人不去直视它 — 而「建造某种比你活得久的东西」是其中最体面的一种。他并不否认留下什么是重要的；他解释的是为何它的重要程度，远超我们为它给出的理由。

quote.en: The idea of death, the fear of it, haunts the human animal like nothing else.
quote.zh: 死亡的念头、对死亡的恐惧，以任何别的事物都不及的方式纠缠着人这种动物。

label.en: Becker, The Denial of Death, preface
label.zh: 贝克尔《拒斥死亡》序言

claim.en: The forgetting is not a flaw in the arrangement. It is the arrangement.
claim.zh: 被遗忘不是这套安排的缺陷，它就是这套安排本身。

detail.en: The verse states the disappearance of memory twice — backwards and forwards — and then offers nothing to soften it. That refusal is the book's method: it names what is the case and declines the consolations available to it. What it recommends instead is bread, work and company, held without illusion, which is a way of saying the question's premise is true and the effort was never for the record.
detail.zh: 这节经文两次陈述记忆的消失 — 向前与向后 — 然后不提供任何缓和。这种拒绝正是全书的方法：它指出实情，并回绝手边现成的安慰。它转而推荐饮食、劳作与陪伴，且不带幻想地持守 — 这等于说：问题的前提是真的，而努力从来就不是为了留下记录。

quote.en: There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.
quote.zh: 已过的世代，无人记念；将来的世代，后来的人也不记念。

origin.zh: 古以色列，约公元前 3 世纪

label.en: Ecclesiastes 1:11, King James Version
label.zh: 《传道书》1:11，钦定版

claim.en: The world will not supply a reason. Take that as settled and go on anyway.
claim.zh: 世界不会提供理由。就当这事已成定局，然后照样活下去。

detail.en: Sisyphus is condemned to a task with no product, which makes him the exact test case for this question. Camus's claim is that once you stop demanding a reason from a world that has none to give, the pushing itself is available to be lived. He rejects both despair and the leap to faith; what remains he calls revolt, and it needs no audience at the top of the hill.
detail.zh: 西西弗斯被判处一项没有产物的劳作，这使他恰好成为这个问题的检验案例。加缪的主张是：一旦你不再向一个给不出理由的世界索求理由，推石头这件事本身就变得可以被活。他同时拒绝绝望与信仰的跃升；剩下的他称为反抗，而它在山顶不需要观众。

quote.en: The struggle itself towards the heights is enough to fill a man's heart. One must imagine Sisyphus happy.
quote.zh: 仅仅是向着高处挣扎这件事本身，就足以充满一个人的心。必须想象西西弗斯是幸福的。

label.en: Camus, The Myth of Sisyphus, closing lines
label.zh: 加缪《西西弗斯神话》结尾

claim.en: You do not know your own position until you have met the strongest version of the opposite one.
claim.zh: 在你遇到反面立场的最强版本之前，你并不真正知道自己的立场。

detail.en: The line is about competence, not politeness: an opinion you have only ever heard from your own side is one you have not yet examined. Mill's mechanism for escaping inherited belief is not willpower but exposure — you find out what you actually hold by meeting the strongest version of the opposite. That is his answer here: environment sets your starting position, but it does not have to set the final one.
detail.zh: 这句话谈的是能力而非礼貌：一个你只从自己这一方听说过的意见，是你尚未检验过的意见。密尔摆脱继承信念的机制不是意志力，而是接触 — 你要通过遭遇反面立场的最强版本，才知道自己真正持有什么。这就是他在此的回答：环境设定了你的起点，但不必设定终点。

quote.en: He who knows only his own side of the case knows little of that.
quote.zh: 只知道自己这一方说法的人，对这件事所知甚少。

label.en: Mill, On Liberty, chapter 2
label.zh: 密尔《论自由》第二章

claim.en: How you came to believe something and whether it is true are two separate questions.
claim.zh: 你如何得到某个信念，和它是否为真，是两个不同的问题。

detail.en: Russell is separating two things this question keeps fusing: how widely a belief is held and whether it is true. Popularity is a fact about a population, not evidence about the world. Applied here, it cuts both ways — discovering that you absorbed a belief from your upbringing tells you where it came from and nothing at all about whether it is correct.
detail.zh: 罗素把这个问题不断混同的两件事分开：一个信念被持有得多广，与它是否为真。流行是关于人群的事实，而非关于世界的证据。用在这里，它是双向的 — 发现你从成长环境中吸收了某个信念，只告诉你它从哪里来，完全没告诉你它是否正确。

quote.en: The fact that an opinion has been widely held is no evidence whatever that it is not utterly absurd.
quote.zh: 一个意见被广泛持有，丝毫不能证明它不是荒谬透顶的。

label.en: Russell, Marriage and Morals, chapter 5
label.zh: 罗素《婚姻与道德》第五章

claim.en: Ask who a value served before asking whether you agree with it.
claim.zh: 在问你是否同意某个价值之前，先问它曾服务于谁。

detail.en: The claim is not that morality is fake but that it is interpretation all the way down, and interpretations have authors with interests. The Genealogy's method is to ask who a value served before asking whether it is right, which makes the feeling of obviousness itself the thing to be suspicious of. That lands directly on this question: the beliefs that feel least chosen are the ones most worth tracing.
detail.zh: 这一主张不是说道德是假的，而是说它自始至终都是解释 — 而解释有其作者与利益。《谱系》的方法是：先问某个价值曾服务于谁，再问它是否正确；这就使「理所当然」这种感觉本身成为最该被怀疑的东西。这恰好落在本题上：那些最不像被选择的信念，最值得追溯。

quote.en: There are no moral phenomena at all, but only a moral interpretation of phenomena.
quote.zh: 根本没有道德现象，只有对现象的道德解释。

label.en: Nietzsche, Beyond Good and Evil §108, trans. Helen Zimmern
label.zh: 尼采《善恶的彼岸》第 108 节，齐默恩 译

claim.en: Reason is slower and weaker than you think, and usually arrives after the conclusion.
claim.zh: 理性比你以为的更慢、更弱，而且通常在结论之后才到场。

detail.en: Hume is describing the order in which belief actually forms, not recommending it: sentiment and custom move first, and reasoning arrives afterwards to supply the argument. That is a hard limit on the idea of thinking your way out of your environment — not that it is impossible, but that it is not the default motion and takes deliberate work against the grain.
detail.zh: 休谟描述的是信念实际形成的次序，而不是在推荐它：情感与习惯先动，推理随后到场来补上论证。这对「靠思考走出环境」构成了硬性限制 — 不是说不可能，而是说它不是默认动作，需要逆着纹理刻意用力。

quote.en: Reason is, and ought only to be the slave of the passions, and can never pretend to any other office than to serve and obey them.
quote.zh: 理性是、且只应当是激情的奴隶，除了服侍与服从激情之外，绝不能僭称任何别的职能。

label.en: Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, II.3.3
label.zh: 休谟《人性论》第二卷第三章第三节

claim.en: A person is made, not issued. The situation you were placed in did much of the making.
claim.zh: 人是被造就的，不是被发放的。你被放置其中的处境完成了大部分造就工作。

detail.en: The sentence is about production, not biology: a role that feels like nature turns out to have been assembled by a situation. Beauvoir's analysis generalises past its original subject — whatever feels most simply like who you are is where the shaping was most thorough. Against this question, that is the strongest form of the case: independence is not something a worldview can have.
detail.zh: 这句话谈的是生产而非生理：一个感觉像本性的角色，最终被发现是由处境组装起来的。波伏娃的分析可以超出其原初主题 — 那些最单纯地感觉像「你是谁」的东西，恰恰是塑造最彻底之处。面对本题，这是该立场最强的形式：独立性不是一个世界观可能拥有的东西。

quote.en: One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.
quote.zh: 女人不是天生的，而是被造就的。

label.en: Beauvoir, The Second Sex, Book II opening line
label.zh: 波伏娃《第二性》第二卷开篇

claim.en: You learned to watch yourself by first being watched. That spectator never leaves.
claim.zh: 你是先被别人看着，才学会看自己的。那个旁观者从此不再离开。

detail.en: Smith's spectator is not a metaphor for conscience but an account of where conscience came from: you were judged before you could judge, and you built the judge out of what you saw. Once assembled, it operates in private and feels entirely your own. That makes his answer to this question uncomfortable — the faculty you would use to check your inherited beliefs was itself inherited.
detail.zh: 斯密的「旁观者」不是良知的比喻，而是关于良知从何而来的论述：在你能够评判之前你已被评判，而你用所见之物造出了那个评判者。一旦组装完成，它便在私下运作，并且感觉完全属于你自己。这使他对本题的回答令人不适 — 你用来检验继承信念的那个官能，本身就是继承来的。

quote.en: We suppose ourselves the spectators of our own behaviour, and endeavour to imagine what effect it would, in this light, produce upon us.
quote.zh: 我们把自己设想为自身行为的旁观者，并努力想象在这种目光下它会对我们产生什么影响。

label.en: Smith, The Theory of Moral Sentiments, III.1
label.zh: 斯密《道德情操论》第三卷第一章

claim.en: Watch yourself closely enough and there is no independent vantage point left to find.
claim.zh: 把自己看得够近，就再也找不到一个独立的立足点。

detail.en: Twenty years of watching himself produced this, and it is a finding rather than a complaint: the same person differs from himself across moods, seasons and company more than he differs from other people. Montaigne's answer to this question is that there is no stable vantage point to be independent from — the self doing the checking keeps moving too.
detail.zh: 二十年的自我观察得出了这句话，而它是一个发现而非抱怨：同一个人在不同情绪、季节与同伴之间与自己的差别，大于他与他人的差别。蒙田对本题的回答是：根本没有一个稳定的立足点可供「独立」 — 那个进行检验的自我也一直在移动。

quote.en: There is as much difference between us and ourselves, as between us and others.
quote.zh: 我们与自己之间的差别，和我们与他人之间的差别一样大。

label.en: Montaigne, Essays II.1, trans. Charles Cotton
label.zh: 蒙田《随笔集》第二卷第一章，科顿 译

claim.en: History has an author, so your suffering is not waste — though you may never be shown what it was for.
claim.zh: 历史有其作者，因此你的苦难不是浪费 — 尽管你可能永远不会被告知它是为了什么。

detail.en: Providence holds that events fall inside an intended arc. The difficulty this tradition takes on directly is why the arc includes suffering, and its answers range from discipline to mystery.
detail.zh: 天意认为一切事件都落在一条被安排好的轨迹内。这一传统直接面对的难题是：为何轨迹中包含苦难；其回答从磨炼到不可知的奥秘各有不同。

quote.en: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God.
quote.zh: 我们晓得万事都互相效力，叫爱神的人得益处。

label.en: Romans 8:28, King James Version
label.zh: 《罗马书》8:28，钦定版

claim.en: What looks arbitrary inside one life is part of a much longer accounting.
claim.zh: 在一生之内看似随意的事，属于一本长得多的账目。

detail.en: Karma in the Gita is continuity of action rather than reward and punishment. Krishna's counsel is to act rightly and release the claim on outcomes, because the ledger is longer than one life.
detail.zh: 《薄伽梵歌》中的业是行动的延续，而非奖惩。克里希那的劝告是正确地行动并放下对结果的执着，因为这本账簿长于一生。

quote.en: Let right deeds be thy motive, not the fruit which comes from them.
quote.zh: 以正当的行为为动机，而非行为带来的果实。

origin.zh: 印度，约公元前 2 世纪

label.en: Bhagavad Gita 2.47, trans. Edwin Arnold
label.zh: 《薄伽梵歌》2.47，阿诺德 译

claim.en: Nothing arrives with a meaning attached. You are the one who assigns it, and you cannot avoid the job.
claim.zh: 没有什么东西自带意义。是你在赋予它意义，而这份工作你无法推卸。

detail.en: For Sartre existence precedes essence: there is no prior purpose a life is fulfilling. The meaning of a coincidence is authored after the fact, by you, whether or not you notice doing it.
detail.zh: 对萨特而言存在先于本质：不存在人生所要实现的先在目的。巧合的意义是事后被赋予的 — 由你赋予，无论你是否察觉。

quote.en: Man is condemned to be free; because once thrown into the world, he is responsible for everything he does.
quote.zh: 人是被判定为自由的：一旦被抛入世界，他就要为自己所做的一切负责。

label.en: Sartre, Existentialism Is a Humanism, 1946
label.zh: 萨特《存在主义是一种人道主义》，1946 年

claim.en: Ask what a story about meaning does for the person telling it. That is not a cynical question.
claim.zh: 问一问「意义故事」为讲述它的人做了什么。这不是一个犬儒的问题。

detail.en: The pragmatist test is what a belief is worth in practice. On that reading the story you build after a coincidence is neither true nor false so much as load-bearing or not.
detail.zh: 实用主义的检验标准是信念在实践中值多少。据此，你在巧合之后建立的故事与其说是真是假，不如说是承重还是不承重。

quote.en: The true is the name of whatever proves itself to be good in the way of belief.
quote.zh: 「真」是一切在信念方面证明自己为好的东西的名称。

label.en: James, Pragmatism, Lecture II
label.zh: 詹姆斯《实用主义》第二讲

claim.en: There is pattern here, but no planner. Things tend a certain way; work with the grain instead of asking why.
claim.zh: 有规律而无安排者。事物有其倾向，顺着纹理行事，而不是追问为什么。

detail.en: Daoism describes a world with reliable tendencies and no supervisor. Wu wei follows from that: you work with the grain rather than negotiating with an intention.
detail.zh: 道家描述的世界有稳定的倾向而无监管者。由此有「无为」：顺着纹理行事，而不是与某个意图谈条件。

quote.en: The Dao in its regular course does nothing, and so there is nothing which it does not do.
quote.zh: 道常无为而无不为。

origin.zh: 中国，约公元前 4 世纪

label.en: Tao Te Ching 37, trans. James Legge
label.zh: 《道德经》第三十七章，理雅各 译

claim.en: A coincidence can carry meaning without anything having caused it. That is a claim about experience, not physics.
claim.zh: 巧合可以带有意义，却没有任何东西造成它。这是关于经验的主张，不是关于物理学的。

detail.en: Jung coined synchronicity for meaningful coincidence without a causal link, and treated it as psychology rather than physics. Read as a claim about how events are experienced, it is not testable — and he largely accepted that.
detail.zh: 荣格用「共时性」指称没有因果联系却带有意义的巧合，并将其视为心理学而非物理学。作为关于「事件如何被经验」的主张，它无法被检验 — 这一点他大体上接受。

quote.en: Synchronicity: a meaningful coincidence of two or more events, where something other than the probability of chance is involved.
quote.zh: 共时性：两个或多个事件的有意义的巧合，其中涉及的不只是偶然的概率。

label.en: Jung, Synchronicity: An Acausal Connecting Principle, 1952
label.zh: 荣格《共时性：一种非因果的联系原则》，1952 年

claim.en: We feel causes we never observe. The connection is in the mind, laid down by repetition.
claim.zh: 我们感觉到从未观察到的原因。那种联系在心里，由重复所铺设。

detail.en: Hume's analysis of causation is that we observe one thing following another and supply the necessary link ourselves. Reading purpose into a coincidence is that same habit, running harder.
detail.zh: 休谟对因果的分析是：我们观察到一事随另一事而来，而那必然的联系是我们自己补上的。在巧合中读出目的，正是同一个习惯在更用力地运作。

quote.en: All inferences from experience suppose, as their foundation, that the future will resemble the past.
quote.zh: 一切来自经验的推论，都以「未来将类似过去」为其基础。

label.en: Hume, An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding, IV.2
label.zh: 休谟《人类理解研究》第四章第二节

claim.en: Some things simply swerve. Once nobody is arranging your life, the universe gets kinder, not colder.
claim.zh: 有些事情就是偏斜了。一旦没有人在安排你的人生，宇宙会变得更温和，而不是更冷。

detail.en: Epicurus built chance into physics with the swerve of atoms, breaking strict determinism. The payoff was ethical: no gods are watching or arranging, so fear of them can be set down.
detail.zh: 伊壁鸠鲁以原子的偏斜把偶然写进物理，打破严格决定论。其收益是伦理上的：没有神在注视或安排，因此对神的恐惧可以放下。

quote.en: A blessed and indestructible being neither has trouble itself nor causes trouble to another.
quote.zh: 一个有福而不朽的存在，自身没有烦扰，也不给他人带来烦扰。

label.en: Epicurus, Principal Doctrines I, trans. Robert Drew Hicks
label.zh: 伊壁鸠鲁《主要教义》第一条，希克斯 译

claim.en: Believing something because it helps is not a reason for thinking it is so.
claim.zh: 因为某个信念有用就相信它，并不构成认为它为真的理由。

detail.en: Russell's proposal is that we withhold assent wherever the grounds are absent, and he notes plainly how few beliefs would survive the rule.
detail.zh: 罗素的提议是：凡缺乏依据之处便悬置赞同；他也直白指出，能通过这条规则的信念寥寥无几。

quote.en: It is undesirable to believe a proposition when there is no ground whatever for supposing it true.
quote.zh: 当一个命题毫无理由被认为为真时，相信它是不可取的。

label.en: Russell, Sceptical Essays, 'On the Value of Scepticism'
label.zh: 罗素《怀疑论集》，〈论怀疑的价值〉

claim.en: Some questions will not wait for evidence. Refusing to decide is itself a decision, with its own risk.
claim.zh: 有些问题不会等待证据。拒绝决定本身就是一种决定，也带着自己的风险。

detail.en: James limits the licence carefully: it applies where a question is live, forced and momentous, and evidence cannot settle it in time. Within that box, the practical stakes may decide.
detail.zh: 詹姆斯谨慎地限制了这一许可：它只适用于活的、被迫的、重大的问题，且证据无法及时裁决。在这个范围内，实践上的利害可以决定。

quote.en: We cannot escape the issue by remaining sceptical, for although we do avoid error in that way if religion be untrue, we lose the good, if it be true.
quote.zh: 保持怀疑并不能让我们回避这个问题：若宗教不真，我们固然因此避开了错误；但若它为真，我们就失去了那份好处。

label.en: James, The Will to Believe, section X
label.zh: 詹姆斯《信仰的意志》第十节

claim.en: The question is not what is true in general. It is what is true in a way you can actually live by.
claim.zh: 问题不是「一般而言什么是真的」，而是「什么样的真理你真的能据以生活」。

detail.en: Kierkegaard wrote this at twenty-two and never really left it. The demand is not that truth be private, but that a truth you cannot live by has not yet done anything.
detail.zh: 克尔凯郭尔二十二岁写下这句，此后未曾真正离开它。他要求的不是真理成为私人的，而是：一个你无法据以生活的真理，还什么都没做成。

quote.en: The thing is to find a truth which is true for me, to find the idea for which I can live and die.
quote.zh: 关键是找到一个对我为真的真理，找到那个我可以为之生、为之死的理念。

label.en: Kierkegaard, Journals, 1 August 1835
label.zh: 克尔凯郭尔《日记》，1835 年 8 月 1 日

claim.en: Taking a symbol literally is the standard way to misunderstand it.
claim.zh: 按字面理解象征，正是误解它的标准方式。

detail.en: Tillich's distinction is that a symbol participates in what it points to and cannot be exchanged for a factual report. Asking whether it literally happened is the wrong question put to the wrong object.
detail.zh: 蒂利希的区分在于：象征参与于它所指向之物，无法被换成一份事实报告。追问「它是否真的发生过」，是对错误的对象提错误的问题。

quote.en: Faith is the state of being ultimately concerned.
quote.zh: 信仰是「被终极地关切」的状态。

label.en: Tillich, Dynamics of Faith, chapter 1, opening line
label.zh: 蒂利希《信仰的动力》第一章开篇

claim.en: The moment you can state it exactly, you are no longer talking about the thing.
claim.zh: 当你能够精确地说出它时，你谈论的已经不是那个东西了。

detail.en: The opening line of the Tao Te Ching makes its own inadequacy the first teaching. A text that begins by disqualifying its own literal reading is not making a factual claim.
detail.zh: 《道德经》开篇即以自身的不足为第一教诲。一部开篇就取消自身字面读法的文本，并不是在提出事实主张。

quote.en: The Dao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Dao.
quote.zh: 道可道，非常道。

origin.zh: 中国，约公元前 4 世纪

label.en: Tao Te Ching 1, trans. James Legge
label.zh: 《道德经》第一章，理雅各 译

claim.en: If you would refuse a machine that supplies the experience without the reality, you already value truth over usefulness.
claim.zh: 如果你会拒绝一台「只给体验、没有现实」的机器，那你已经把真相看得比有用更重。

detail.en: Nozick's machine separates wanting good feelings from wanting a real life. Most people decline it, which is evidence that a belief's usefulness is not all they were after.
detail.zh: 诺齐克的机器把「想要好感受」与「想要真实人生」分开。多数人拒绝接入，这说明有用性并非他们所求的全部。

quote.en: Plugging into the machine is a kind of suicide.
quote.zh: 接入那台机器是一种自杀。

label.en: Nozick, Anarchy, State, and Utopia, chapter 3
label.zh: 诺齐克《无政府、国家与乌托邦》第三章

claim.en: A belief held without evidence is not a private matter. You act on it, and others live with the acting.
claim.zh: 无证据而持有的信念不是私事。你会依它行动，而他人要承担这行动的后果。

detail.en: Clifford opens with a shipowner who talks himself into believing his vessel seaworthy. The ship sinks. The point is that belief is never inert — it is the thing conduct runs on.
detail.zh: 克利福德以一位船主开篇：他说服自己相信船是适航的。船沉了。要点在于信念从不惰性 — 它正是行为所依凭之物。

quote.en: It is wrong always, everywhere, and for anyone, to believe anything upon insufficient evidence.
quote.zh: 在任何时候、任何地方、对任何人而言，基于不充分的证据去相信任何事，都是错的。

label.en: Clifford, The Ethics of Belief, part I
label.zh: 克利福德《信念的伦理》第一部分

claim.en: Over your own body and mind you are the only rightful authority. The line is harm to others, not their disapproval.
claim.zh: 对自己的身体与心灵，你是唯一正当的权威。界线是对他人的伤害，而不是他人的不赞成。

detail.en: Mill draws the limit narrowly on purpose. He expected the real pressure on individuals to come from society's opinion rather than from law, and wrote the principle to hold against it.
detail.zh: 密尔刻意把界线划得很窄。他预期个人所受的真正压力来自社会舆论而非法律，这条原则正是为抵御舆论而写。

quote.en: Over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is sovereign.
quote.zh: 对于他自己，对于他自己的身体与心灵，个人就是主权者。

label.en: Mill, On Liberty, chapter 1
label.zh: 密尔《论自由》第一章

claim.en: Freedom from interference and freedom to become someone are different things, and they can pull apart.
claim.zh: 「免于干涉的自由」与「成为某种人的自由」是两回事，而且可能彼此拉扯。

detail.en: Berlin's distinction explains why removing every constraint does not produce a life anyone wants. Having no obstacles is not the same as having somewhere to go.
detail.zh: 伯林的区分解释了为何去掉一切约束并不会产生任何人想要的人生。没有障碍，不等于有地方可去。

quote.en: I am normally said to be free to the degree to which no man or body of men interferes with my activity.
quote.zh: 通常说我是自由的，程度取决于没有任何人或任何群体干涉我的活动。

label.en: Berlin, Two Concepts of Liberty, 1958
label.zh: 伯林《两种自由概念》，1958 年

claim.en: Mastery of yourself is not the opposite of freedom. It is the form freedom takes when it has somewhere to go.
claim.zh: 克己不是自由的反面。它是自由有了去处之后所呈现的形式。

detail.en: The Confucian answer treats restraint as the medium of a good life rather than a tax on it. Ritual here is not decoration; it is the structure that makes conduct legible to others.
detail.zh: 儒家的回答把约束视为好生活的媒介，而非对它的征税。此处的「礼」不是装饰，而是使行为对他人可读的结构。

quote.en: To subdue one's self and return to propriety, is perfect virtue.
quote.zh: 克己复礼为仁。

label.en: Analects 12.1, trans. James Legge
label.zh: 《论语·颜渊》12.1，理雅各 译

claim.en: People hand freedom away with relief far more often than they fight for it.
claim.zh: 人们如释重负地交出自由，远比为它抗争更常见。

detail.en: The Grand Inquisitor's charge is that freedom is a burden most would trade for bread and authority. Dostoevsky puts it in the mouth of a villain: the trade is real, and the novel treats it as a loss.
detail.zh: 《宗教大法官》的控诉是：自由是重担，多数人愿以之换取面包与权威。陀思妥耶夫斯基把这段话放进反派口中：这种交换是真实的，而小说把它当作一种失去。

quote.en: There is no more ceaseless or tormenting care for man, when he has become free, than to find someone to bow down to as soon as possible.
quote.zh: 人一旦获得自由，就没有比尽快找到一个可以跪拜的对象更持久、更折磨人的牵挂了。

label.en: Dostoevsky, The Brothers Karamazov, 'The Grand Inquisitor', trans. Constance Garnett
label.zh: 陀思妥耶夫斯基《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》〈宗教大法官〉，加尼特 译

claim.en: Freedom without belonging produces anxiety, and anxious people look for someone to submit to.
claim.zh: 没有归属的自由制造焦虑，而焦虑的人会寻找可以服从的对象。

detail.en: Fromm published this in 1941, arguing that modern freedom severed older bonds and left an isolation people escape through submission. The date is part of the argument.
detail.zh: 弗洛姆于 1941 年出版此书，论现代自由切断了旧有纽带，留下一种人们通过服从来逃离的孤立。出版年份本身就是论证的一部分。

quote.en: Freedom, though it has brought him independence and rationality, has made him isolated and, thereby, anxious and powerless.
quote.zh: 自由虽给人带来了独立与理性，却也使他孤立，并因此焦虑而无力。

label.en: Fromm, Escape from Freedom, chapter 1
label.zh: 弗洛姆《逃避自由》第一章

claim.en: A person outside a community is not a freer person. They are a less complete one.
claim.zh: 脱离共同体的人不是更自由的人，而是更不完整的人。

detail.en: Aristotle's claim is constitutive, not sentimental: the capacities that make someone fully human — speech, justice, deliberation — only operate among others. Solitude is not liberty here.
detail.zh: 亚里士多德的主张是构成性的，而非感伤的：使人成其为人的能力 — 言语、正义、审议 — 只在他人之间运作。此处的独处不是自由。

quote.en: Man is by nature a political animal; and he who by nature and not by mere accident is without a state, is either above humanity, or below it.
quote.zh: 人天生是政治的动物；凡因本性而非偶然无邦可属者，不是超乎人类，就是低于人类。

label.en: Aristotle, Politics I.2, trans. Benjamin Jowett
label.zh: 亚里士多德《政治学》1.2，乔伊特 译

claim.en: You do not only want to be approved of. You want to be the kind of thing that deserves it.
claim.zh: 你想要的不只是被认可，而是成为配得上认可的那种人。

detail.en: Smith's distinction between being loved and being lovely turns belonging into a standard rather than a comfort. It is other people who supply the standard.
detail.zh: 斯密对「被爱」与「可爱」的区分，把归属变成一种标准而非慰藉。而这标准由他人提供。

quote.en: Man naturally desires, not only to be loved, but to be lovely.
quote.zh: 人天然渴望的不只是被爱，而是成为可爱的。

label.en: Smith, The Theory of Moral Sentiments, III.2
label.zh: 斯密《道德情操论》第三卷第二章

claim.en: Do a thing often enough and it stops being a thing you do. It becomes a thing you are.
claim.zh: 一件事做得够多，它就不再是你做的事，而成了你之所是。

detail.en: Aristotle's settled dispositions are laid down by repetition. On this account performance and character are not opposites: performance repeated is precisely how character gets made.
detail.zh: 亚里士多德所说的稳定倾向由重复奠定。据此，扮演与品格并不对立：重复的扮演正是品格形成的方式。

quote.en: We become just by doing just acts, temperate by doing temperate acts, brave by doing brave acts.
quote.zh: 我们通过做公正之事而成为公正的人，通过做节制之事而成为节制的人，通过做勇敢之事而成为勇敢的人。

label.en: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics II.1, trans. W. D. Ross
label.zh: 亚里士多德《尼各马可伦理学》2.1，罗斯 译

claim.en: You have a front stage and a back stage, and the audience is never fully absent from either.
claim.zh: 你有前台，也有后台，而观众从未真正从任何一边缺席。

detail.en: Goffman describes social life as managed impression: we present a version fitted to the situation. His point is not that people are fake, but that presentation is the ordinary medium of social life.
detail.zh: 戈夫曼把社会生活描述为被管理的印象：我们呈现出适配情境的版本。他的重点不是人虚伪，而是呈现本就是社会生活的常态媒介。

quote.en: Life itself is a dramatically enacted thing.
quote.zh: 生活本身就是一件被戏剧性地演出的事。

label.en: Goffman, The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life, conclusion
label.zh: 戈夫曼《日常生活中的自我呈现》结论

claim.en: Naming a kind of person creates a kind of person to be.
claim.zh: 命名一种人，就创造出一种可以去成为的人。

detail.en: Berger and Luckmann describe the loop: arrangements people made come to feel like facts, and then shape the people who inherit them. The description and the described stop being independent.
detail.zh: 伯格与卢克曼描述了这个回路：人所造的安排逐渐感觉像事实，进而塑造继承它们的人。描述与被描述者不再彼此独立。

quote.en: Society is a human product. Society is an objective reality. Man is a social product.
quote.zh: 社会是人的产物。社会是客观实在。人是社会的产物。

label.en: Berger and Luckmann, The Social Construction of Reality, part II
label.zh: 伯格与卢克曼《现实的社会建构》第二部分

claim.en: Anyone who watches themselves honestly for long enough stops finding a fixed thing to report.
claim.zh: 任何诚实地长期观察自己的人，最终都不会再找到一个固定之物可供报告。

detail.en: Montaigne spent twenty years on this and concluded that inconsistency was the finding, not the failure. He describes movement because movement is what was there.
detail.zh: 蒙田为此花了二十年，结论是：不一致本身就是发现，而不是失败。他描述流动，因为在那里的正是流动。

quote.en: I do not paint his being, I paint his passage.
quote.zh: 我描绘的不是他的存在，而是他的经过。

label.en: Montaigne, Essays III.2, trans. Charles Cotton
label.zh: 蒙田《随笔集》第三卷第二章，科顿 译

claim.en: Look for the self and you find changing parts. Nobody is home, and that is the good news.
claim.zh: 去找那个自我，你只会找到不断变化的部分。没有人在家 — 而这是好消息。

detail.en: The teaching runs through each component of a person in turn and finds none of them a self. If so, asking whether a label found the real you assumes something the analysis says is not there.
detail.zh: 这一教法逐一检视构成人的各个成分，发现没有一个是「我」。若如此，追问某个标签是否找到了真正的你，就预设了这一分析认为并不存在的东西。

quote.en: Form is not-self. Were form self, then this form would not lead to affliction.
quote.zh: 色非我。若色是我，则色不应导致苦恼。

origin.zh: 印度，约公元前 5 世纪

label.en: Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta, Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.59
label.zh: 《无我相经》，《相应部》22.59

claim.en: There is no doer sitting behind the deed. The doer was added afterwards, by grammar.
claim.zh: 行为背后并没有一个「行为者」端坐其中。那个行为者是事后被语法加上去的。

detail.en: Nietzsche's target is the grammatical habit of requiring a subject for every verb, and then mistaking that requirement for a discovery about the world.
detail.zh: 尼采针对的是这样一种语法习惯：要求每个动词都有主语，然后把这一要求误认作关于世界的发现。

quote.en: There is no 'being' behind doing, effecting, becoming; 'the doer' is merely a fiction added to the deed — the deed is everything.
quote.zh: 在行动、作用、生成的背后并没有「存在」；「行为者」只是被添加到行为之上的虚构 — 行为就是一切。

label.en: Nietzsche, On the Genealogy of Morals I.13, trans. Horace Samuel
label.zh: 尼采《道德的谱系》第一章第 13 节，塞缪尔 译

claim.en: Look inward and you catch perceptions, never the thing having them.
claim.zh: 向内看，你捕捉到的是知觉，从来不是那个拥有知觉的东西。

detail.en: Hume reports that introspection turns up particular impressions and no observer behind them. The traits may be real enough; the unified owner is the part he cannot find.
detail.zh: 休谟报告说，内省找到的是一个个具体印象，而没有它们背后的观察者。特征或许足够真实；他找不到的是那个统一的拥有者。

quote.en: They are nothing but a bundle or collection of different perceptions, which succeed each other with an inconceivable rapidity.
quote.zh: 它们不过是一束或一组不同的知觉，以不可思议的速度彼此接续。

label.en: Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, I.4.6
label.zh: 休谟《人性论》第一卷第四章第六节

claim.en: What makes you the same person is the thread of memory, not the body or the century.
claim.zh: 让你成为同一个人的是记忆的线索，而不是身体或世纪。

detail.en: Locke ties identity to continuity of consciousness rather than substance. A self relocated to 1526 stays the same self exactly as far as the remembering reaches, and no further.
detail.zh: 洛克把同一性系于意识的连续性而非实体。被移到 1526 年的自我，其同一性延伸到记忆所及之处为止，不再更远。

quote.en: Consciousness always accompanies thinking, and it is that which makes every one to be what he calls self.
quote.zh: 意识总是伴随思想，正是它使每个人成为他所谓的「自我」。

label.en: Locke, An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, II.27.9
label.zh: 洛克《人类理解论》第二卷第 27 章第 9 节

claim.en: The tendency is constant. What it runs into is not.
claim.zh: 倾向是恒常的，它所遭遇的东西则不是。

detail.en: Mencius argues that human nature inclines toward good the way water inclines downward, and that circumstance can dam or divert it without changing the inclination. Temperament travels; its expression does not.
detail.zh: 孟子论人性向善如水就下，环境可以壅塞或改道，却不改变那份倾向。性情可以迁移，其表现则不能。

quote.en: The tendency of man's nature to good is like the tendency of water to flow downwards.
quote.zh: 人性之善也，犹水之就下也。

label.en: Mencius 6A.2, trans. James Legge
label.zh: 《孟子·告子上》6A.2，理雅各 译

claim.en: Identity may not be what matters. What matters is continuity, and it comes in degrees.
claim.zh: 同一性也许并不是重要的东西。重要的是连续性，而它是有程度的。

detail.en: Parfit argues personal identity is not an all-or-nothing further fact. Change enough of the connections and 'is it still me?' stops having a determinate answer — not because it is hard, but because it is empty.
detail.zh: 帕菲特论证人格同一性并非非此即彼的额外事实。改变足够多的联系，「这还是我吗」就不再有确定答案 — 不是因为难，而是因为它空洞。

quote.en: Personal identity is not what matters.
quote.zh: 人格同一性并不是重要的东西。

label.en: Parfit, Reasons and Persons, part III
label.zh: 帕菲特《理与人》第三部分

claim.en: I dreamt I was a butterfly and cannot say which way round it goes. Your grip on 'you' is looser than it feels.
claim.zh: 我梦见自己是蝴蝶，说不清究竟哪个是哪个。你对「你」的把握，比你感觉的要松。

detail.en: Zhuangzi is not being sceptical for sport. He is loosening the assumption that there is one settled standpoint from which the question of who you really are gets answered.
detail.zh: 庄子不是为怀疑而怀疑。他松动的是这样一个预设：存在某个确定的立足点，可以从那里回答「你究竟是谁」。

quote.en: He did not know whether it was Zhou dreaming that he was a butterfly, or a butterfly dreaming that he was Zhou.
quote.zh: 不知周之梦为胡蝶与，胡蝶之梦为周与。

origin.zh: 中国，约公元前 4 世纪

label.en: Zhuangzi, Inner Chapters 2, trans. James Legge
label.zh: 《庄子·内篇·齐物论》，理雅各 译

claim.en: A person is made, not issued. Change the making and you have not moved someone — you have made someone else.
claim.zh: 人是被造就的，不是被发放的。改变造就的过程，你并没有搬动某个人 — 你造出了另一个人。

detail.en: Beauvoir's argument that a social role is produced rather than born into generalises past its original subject: what feels like your nature is largely the shape a situation pressed you into.
detail.zh: 波伏娃关于社会角色是被生产而非天生的论证，可以超出其原初主题：那些感觉像本性的东西，大体上是处境把你压成的形状。

quote.en: One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.
quote.zh: 女人不是天生的，而是被造就的。

label.en: Beauvoir, The Second Sex, Book II opening line
label.zh: 波伏娃《第二性》第二卷开篇

claim.en: There is no observer sitting behind the perceptions to be relocated in the first place.
claim.zh: 知觉背后本来就没有一个观察者可供搬迁。

detail.en: If the self is a succession of perceptions rather than a thing having them, then moving it to another century is not moving anything. There is only a different succession.
detail.zh: 如果自我是知觉的接续而非拥有知觉之物，那么把它移到另一个世纪并没有移动任何东西。只是有了另一段接续。

quote.en: I never can catch myself at any time without a perception, and never can observe any thing but the perception.
quote.zh: 我从来不能在没有某个知觉的情况下捕捉到我自己，也从来只能观察到知觉本身。

label.en: Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, I.4.6
label.zh: 休谟《人性论》第一卷第四章第六节

claim.en: A number is not an argument. Adding people to a mistake does not improve it.
claim.zh: 数量不是论证。给一个错误增加人数，并不会让它变好。

detail.en: Kierkegaard's objection is that a crowd relieves each member of responsibility for the judgement, so its confidence is manufactured rather than earned. The unanimity is the symptom.
detail.zh: 克尔凯郭尔的反对在于：群众免除了每个成员对判断的责任，因此它的确信是被制造的而非挣得的。一致本身就是症状。

quote.en: The crowd is untruth.
quote.zh: 群众即不真。

label.en: Kierkegaard, The Point of View, 'That Individual'
label.zh: 克尔凯郭尔《我的著作活动的观点》〈那个单独的个体〉

claim.en: When the people who actually know agree, holding out is no longer independence.
claim.zh: 当真正懂行的人意见一致时，坚持己见就不再是独立。

detail.en: Russell's rule is not deference to numbers but to competence: an expert consensus is evidence, and treating your own contrary hunch as its equal is not scepticism.
detail.zh: 罗素的准则不是服从人数，而是服从能力：专家共识本身就是证据，把自己的相反直觉与之等量齐观，并不是怀疑主义。

quote.en: When the experts are agreed, the opposite opinion cannot be held to be certain.
quote.zh: 当专家意见一致时，相反的意见就不能被认为是确定的。

label.en: Russell, Sceptical Essays, 'On the Value of Scepticism'
label.zh: 罗素《怀疑论集》，〈论怀疑的价值〉

claim.en: A third of people will call a clearly shorter line longer, if enough others say so first.
claim.zh: 如果足够多的人先这么说，约三分之一的人会把明显更短的线说成更长。

detail.en: Asch put one real participant among actors giving an obviously wrong answer. The correct answer was never in doubt, which is what makes the conformity rate the finding rather than a measurement error.
detail.zh: 阿希把一名真实被试放进一群给出明显错误答案的演员中。正确答案毫无疑问 — 正因如此，从众率是发现本身，而非测量误差。

quote.en: That reasonably intelligent and well-meaning young people are willing to call white black is a matter of concern.
quote.zh: 相当聪明且善意的年轻人竟愿意指白为黑，这是值得忧虑的事。

label.en: Asch, 'Opinions and Social Pressure', Scientific American, 1955
label.zh: 阿希〈意见与社会压力〉，《科学美国人》，1955 年

claim.en: You learned to judge yourself by first being judged. That spectator does not leave when the room empties.
claim.zh: 你是先被他人评判，才学会评判自己的。屋子空了，那个旁观者也不会离开。

detail.en: Smith's impartial spectator is assembled out of other people's responses and then carried inside. On that account each member of a group judges partly through the others, so their agreement can be one judgement echoed rather than many reached apart.
detail.zh: 斯密的公正旁观者由他人的反应拼装而成，然后被带进内心。据此，群体中的每个人都在部分地借他人来判断，因此他们的一致可能只是一个判断的回声，而不是各自独立得出的许多判断。

quote.en: We suppose ourselves the spectators of our own behaviour, and endeavour to imagine what effect it would, in this light, produce upon us.
quote.zh: 我们把自己设想为自身行为的旁观者，并努力想象在这种目光下它会对我们产生什么影响。

label.en: Smith, The Theory of Moral Sentiments, III.1
label.zh: 斯密《道德情操论》第三卷第一章

claim.en: Weigh the testimony against how likely it is that these particular people are mistaken.
claim.zh: 把证言与「这些特定的人出错的可能性」放在一起权衡。

detail.en: Hume's treatment of testimony is comparative rather than deferential: how improbable is the claim, set against how improbable it would be for these witnesses to be wrong. Whose consensus it is does most of the work.
detail.zh: 休谟对证言的处理是比较性的而非顺从性的：该主张有多不可能，对照这些证人出错有多不可能。「这是谁的共识」承担了大部分工作。

quote.en: A wise man, therefore, proportions his belief to the evidence.
quote.zh: 因此，明智的人使他的相信程度与证据相称。

label.en: Hume, An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding, X.1
label.zh: 休谟《人类理解研究》第十章第一节

claim.en: A consensus formed where dissent was cheap is worth far more than one formed where it was costly.
claim.zh: 在「异见代价很低」的环境中形成的共识，远比在「异见代价高昂」中形成的更有价值。

detail.en: Mill's test is whether the agreement survived challenge. Where nobody could safely disagree, the unanimity tells you about the conditions, not about the question.
detail.zh: 密尔的检验标准是：这份一致是否经受过挑战。在无人能安全地表示异议之处，一致告诉你的是环境，而非那个问题。

quote.en: Truth gains more even by the errors of one who, with due study and preparation, thinks for himself, than by the true opinions of those who only hold them because they do not suffer themselves to think.
quote.zh: 一个经过适当研究与准备而独立思考者所犯的错误，比那些仅因不容自己思考而持有正确意见者，更有益于真理。

label.en: Mill, On Liberty, chapter 2
label.zh: 密尔《论自由》第二章

claim.en: Pain is the thing to be reduced. That it happens to be useful somewhere is a reason to find a better tool.
claim.zh: 痛苦本身就是要被减少的东西。它碰巧在某处有用，是去找更好工具的理由。

detail.en: Bentham makes suffering the direct measure, which puts the burden on any defence of pain to show it produces more good than removing it would. That argument gets harder as substitutes improve.
detail.zh: 边沁把痛苦作为直接尺度，这就把举证责任交给了任何为痛苦辩护的人：必须证明它带来的好处大于消除它。随着替代手段变好，这个论证越来越难。

quote.en: Nature has placed mankind under the governance of two sovereign masters, pain and pleasure.
quote.zh: 自然把人类置于两位主权者的统治之下：痛苦与快乐。

label.en: Bentham, An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation, chapter 1
label.zh: 边沁《道德与立法原理导论》第一章

claim.en: The whole path begins by refusing to accept suffering as simply given.
claim.zh: 整条道路的起点，就是拒绝把苦当作理所当然。

detail.en: The first noble truth names suffering plainly, and the tradition's entire claim is that it can end. Where it differs from a technical fix is in the method, not in the goal.
detail.zh: 苦谛平实地点出苦，而这一传统的全部主张是：苦可以止息。它与技术解决方案的差别在方法，而不在目标。

quote.en: Birth is suffering, ageing is suffering, illness is suffering, death is suffering; union with what is displeasing is suffering.
quote.zh: 生是苦，老是苦，病是苦，死是苦；怨憎会是苦。

origin.zh: 印度，约公元前 5 世纪

label.en: Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta, Saṃyutta Nikāya 56.11
label.zh: 《转法轮经》，《相应部》56.11

claim.en: The right response to something genuinely bad is to feel bad about it. Feeling nothing would be the defect.
claim.zh: 对真正糟糕的事，恰当的反应就是感到糟糕。什么都感觉不到才是缺陷。

detail.en: Aristotle's virtue is not the absence of feeling but its calibration. Fear at real danger and grief at real loss are functioning correctly; flatness is the malfunction.
detail.zh: 亚里士多德的德性不是没有感受，而是感受的校准。面对真实危险的恐惧与真实丧失的悲伤是正常运作；麻木才是故障。

quote.en: To feel them at the right times, with reference to the right objects, towards the right people, with the right motive, and in the right way, is what is both intermediate and best.
quote.zh: 在恰当的时机、针对恰当的对象、对恰当的人、以恰当的动机、以恰当的方式去感受，才既是中道也是最好。

label.en: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics II.6, trans. W. D. Ross
label.zh: 亚里士多德《尼各马可伦理学》2.6，罗斯 译

claim.en: What you would edit out is often what did the shaping.
claim.zh: 你想删掉的东西，往往正是塑造了你的东西。

detail.en: Nietzsche is not recommending suffering for its own sake. He is warning that a life optimised for painlessness may turn out to have been optimised for smallness.
detail.zh: 尼采并非为受苦而推崇受苦。他警告的是：一个为无痛而优化的人生，可能最终被证明是为渺小而优化的。

quote.en: The discipline of suffering, of great suffering — do you not know that only this discipline has created all enhancements of man so far?
quote.zh: 苦难的磨练，巨大苦难的磨练 — 你不知道迄今为止人的一切提升都只由这种磨练造就吗？

label.en: Nietzsche, Beyond Good and Evil §225, trans. Helen Zimmern
label.zh: 尼采《善恶的彼岸》第 225 节，齐默恩 译

claim.en: Keep the signal, drop the torment. Nothing says a warning has to hurt as much as it does.
claim.zh: 保留信号，去掉折磨。没有任何理由说明警告必须这么疼。

detail.en: Epicurus defines the goal as the absence of pain rather than the presence of intensity. On that account distress that outlasts its usefulness is simply waste, and removing it costs nothing.
detail.zh: 伊壁鸠鲁把目标定义为「没有痛苦」，而非「拥有强烈感受」。据此，超出其效用期的痛苦纯属浪费，消除它没有代价。

quote.en: By pleasure we mean the absence of pain in the body and of trouble in the soul.
quote.zh: 我们所说的快乐，是指身体没有痛苦、灵魂没有烦扰。

label.en: Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus, trans. Robert Drew Hicks
label.zh: 伊壁鸠鲁《致美诺伊凯的信》，希克斯 译

claim.en: A guaranteed pleasant life you did not actually live is not the thing you wanted.
claim.zh: 一段你并未真正活过的、被保证愉悦的人生，并不是你想要的东西。

detail.en: The experience machine separates wanting good feelings from wanting a real life. That most people decline is evidence the felt quality of a life was never the only thing being optimised.
detail.zh: 「体验机」把「想要好感受」与「想要真实人生」分开。多数人拒绝接入，这说明生活的感受质量从来不是唯一被优化的东西。

quote.en: Plugging into the machine is a kind of suicide.
quote.zh: 接入那台机器是一种自杀。

label.en: Nozick, Anarchy, State, and Utopia, chapter 3
label.zh: 诺齐克《无政府、国家与乌托邦》第三章

claim.en: Grief is the shape love takes when its object is gone. Remove it and you have edited the love.
claim.zh: 悲伤是爱在失去对象后所呈现的形状。删掉它，你就编辑了那份爱。

detail.en: Frankl's claim is that suffering is not a separate object that can be lifted out. Where it carries meaning it stops being mere affliction, and where it is stripped out the meaning goes with it.
detail.zh: 弗兰克尔的主张是：痛苦不是一个可以单独取出的东西。当它承载意义时，它就不再只是折磨；而把它剥离，意义也会一同离开。

quote.en: Suffering ceases to be suffering at the moment it finds a meaning.
quote.zh: 痛苦在找到意义的那一刻，就不再是痛苦。

label.en: Frankl, Man's Search for Meaning, part two
label.zh: 弗兰克尔《活出意义来》第二部

claim.en: Leisure was never idleness. It is the condition under which the best activities become possible at all.
claim.zh: 闲暇从来不是无所事事。它是最好的活动得以可能的条件。

detail.en: For Aristotle the point of work is to reach a state where work is unnecessary, and the point of that state is contemplation, friendship and civic life. Abundance does not create the problem; it removes the obstacle.
detail.zh: 对亚里士多德而言，劳作的目的是抵达无需劳作的状态，而那种状态的目的是沉思、友爱与城邦生活。富足不制造问题，它移除障碍。

quote.en: We are busy that we may have leisure, and make war that we may live in peace.
quote.zh: 我们忙碌是为了得闲，作战是为了和平地生活。

label.en: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics X.7, trans. W. D. Ross
label.zh: 亚里士多德《尼各马可伦理学》10.7，罗斯 译

claim.en: Satisfaction is not the measure. A dissatisfied person with a wider life is not worse off.
claim.zh: 满足不是尺度。一个不满足却拥有更宽阔生活的人，并没有更糟。

detail.en: Mill breaks with simple hedonism by ranking kinds of pleasure, not just amounts. Abundance on this reading is only worth having if it buys the higher sort.
detail.zh: 密尔通过为快乐分级而非只计数量，与简单享乐主义分道。据此，富足只有在能买到更高级的那一类时才值得拥有。

quote.en: It is better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied; better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied.
quote.zh: 做一个不满足的人，胜过做一头满足的猪；做一个不满足的苏格拉底，胜过做一个满足的傻瓜。

label.en: Mill, Utilitarianism, chapter 2
label.zh: 密尔《功利主义》第二章

claim.en: He predicted a fifteen-hour week within a century. The productivity arrived; the short week did not.
claim.zh: 他预测一百年内每周工作十五小时。生产率来了，短工时没有。

detail.en: Keynes forecast that the economic problem would be largely solved and leave us the harder question of what to do. The productivity half came true, which makes the failure of the leisure half the interesting data.
detail.zh: 凯恩斯预测经济问题将基本解决，留给我们「该做什么」这个更难的问题。生产率那一半应验了 — 这使闲暇那一半的落空成为有趣的数据。

quote.en: For the first time since his creation man will be faced with his real, his permanent problem — how to use his freedom from pressing economic cares.
quote.zh: 自受造以来，人将第一次面对他真正的、永恒的问题 — 如何使用他从紧迫经济忧虑中获得的自由。

label.en: Keynes, Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren, 1930
label.zh: 凯恩斯〈我们后代的经济前景〉，1930 年

claim.en: When goods stop being scarce, the scarce thing becomes standing — and standing is zero-sum by construction.
claim.zh: 当物品不再稀缺，稀缺的就变成地位 — 而地位在结构上就是零和的。

detail.en: Veblen describes consumption as display: what is purchased is position. Positional goods cannot be made abundant, because their value consists precisely in others not having them.
detail.zh: 凡勃伦把消费描述为展示：被购买的是位置。位置性商品无法变得充裕，因为其价值恰恰在于他人没有。

quote.en: Conspicuous consumption of valuable goods is a means of reputability to the gentleman of leisure.
quote.zh: 对贵重物品的炫耀性消费，是有闲绅士获取名望的手段。

label.en: Veblen, The Theory of the Leisure Class, chapter 4
label.zh: 凡勃伦《有闲阶级论》第四章

claim.en: Take away the struggle for food and the need to matter does not go anywhere.
claim.zh: 拿走对食物的争夺，「需要自己重要」这件事并不会消失。

detail.en: Becker argues that cultures supply ranked ways of being significant because mortality makes significance urgent. Material abundance changes the currency of that contest without ending it.
detail.zh: 贝克尔论证文化提供了「变得重要」的等级序列，因为死亡使「重要性」变得紧迫。物质富足改变了这场竞争的货币，却没有终结它。

quote.en: Society is a codified hero system, which means that society everywhere is a living myth of the significance of human life.
quote.zh: 社会是一套被编码的英雄体系；这意味着任何地方的社会都是关于「人生意义」的活神话。

label.en: Becker, The Denial of Death, chapter 1
label.zh: 贝克尔《拒斥死亡》第一章

claim.en: The problem was never effort. It was work you do not own and cannot recognise yourself in.
claim.zh: 问题从来不是努力，而是不属于你、你在其中认不出自己的劳动。

detail.en: Marx locates the harm in the relation to the product and the process rather than in exertion. Abundance that leaves the direction of work unchanged does not touch the thing he is describing.
detail.zh: 马克思把伤害定位在与产品和过程的关系，而非用力本身。若富足没有改变劳动的支配方式，就没有触及他所描述的东西。

quote.en: The worker therefore only feels himself outside his work, and in his work feels outside himself.
quote.zh: 因此，工人只有在工作之外才感到自在，而在工作之中则感到不在自身。

label.en: Marx, Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, 'Estranged Labour'
label.zh: 马克思《1844 年经济学哲学手稿》〈异化劳动〉

note.en: A minority school in antiquity; standard on modern syllabi
note.zh: 古代的少数派学派；现代课程的标准内容

note.en: State philosophy of Roman elites; the acknowledged source of modern CBT
note.zh: 罗马精英的主流哲学；现代认知行为疗法公认的源头

origin.zh: 古以色列，约公元前 3 世纪

note.en: Canonical in Judaism and Christianity; read for over two millennia
note.zh: 犹太教与基督教的正典；流传两千余年

note.en: One of the most-read philosophical essays of the 20th century
note.zh: 20 世纪最广为阅读的哲学随笔之一

note.en: Over 16 million copies sold; foundational to logotherapy
note.zh: 销量逾 1600 万册；意义治疗的奠基之作

note.en: Central to modern political theory; widely taught
note.zh: 现代政治理论的核心人物；被广泛讲授

origin.zh: 中国，约公元前 4 世纪

note.en: Canonical Chinese text, continuously read for 2,300 years
note.zh: 中国经典文本，2300 年来持续被阅读

note.en: Pulitzer Prize, 1974; foundational to terror management theory
note.zh: 1974 年普利策奖；恐惧管理理论的源头

note.en: Shaped law, family and civil service across East Asia for two millennia
note.zh: 两千年来塑造东亚的法律、家庭与官僚体系

image.credit: Anonymous Chinese painter of the Western Han period

origin.zh: 印度，约公元前 5 世纪

note.en: Core doctrine for ~500m Buddhists
note.zh: 约 5 亿佛教徒的核心教义

note.en: Foundational to modern empiricism; standard on every syllabus
note.zh: 现代经验论的奠基者；各类课程的标准内容

note.en: On Liberty shaped modern liberal democracies
note.zh: 《论自由》塑造了现代自由民主制度

note.en: The two-concepts-of-liberty distinction is standard in political theory
note.zh: 「两种自由概念」是政治理论的标准区分

note.en: The Grand Inquisitor is among the most discussed passages in literature
note.zh: 《宗教大法官》是文学史上最受讨论的段落之一

note.en: The leading figure of 20th-century existentialism
note.zh: 20 世纪存在主义的代表人物

note.en: The Second Sex founded modern feminist philosophy
note.zh: 《第二性》奠定了现代女性主义哲学

note.en: Among the most cited sociologists of the 20th century
note.zh: 20 世纪被引用最多的社会学家之一

note.en: Among the most replicated findings in social psychology
note.zh: 社会心理学中重复验证最多的发现之一

note.en: The memory theory of identity is where the modern debate begins
note.zh: 记忆同一性理论是现代讨论的起点

note.en: Reasons and Persons reshaped personal-identity philosophy
note.zh: 《理与人》重塑了人格同一性哲学

note.en: Canonical in the Confucian Four Books; shaped East Asian moral education
note.zh: 儒家四书之一；塑造东亚道德教育

note.en: Among the most cited philosophers of the last century
note.zh: 上个世纪被引用最多的哲学家之一

note.en: The experience machine is the standard objection to hedonism
note.zh: 「体验机」是对享乐主义的标准反驳

note.en: The working framework of modern policy and cost-benefit reasoning
note.zh: 现代政策与成本效益推理的实际框架

origin.zh: 印度，约公元前 5 世纪

note.en: The opening claim of Buddhism; taught wherever it is practised
note.zh: 佛教的起点主张；凡佛教流传处皆有传授

note.en: A famous forecast, now testable against a century of data
note.zh: 著名预测，如今可用一个世纪的数据检验

note.en: Conspicuous consumption entered ordinary language
note.zh: 「炫耀性消费」已进入日常语言

note.en: Foundational to Western ethics; on syllabi since antiquity
note.zh: 西方伦理学的奠基者；自古代起即为课程内容

note.en: Among the most influential accounts of work in the modern era
note.zh: 现代关于劳动最具影响力的论述之一

origin.zh: 中国，约公元前 4 世纪

note.en: Canonical in China for 2,400 years; the Tao Te Ching is widely translated
note.zh: 在中国流传 2400 年；《道德经》译本极多

note.en: Founding figure of American psychology and pragmatism
note.zh: 美国心理学与实用主义的奠基人物

note.en: A dominant framework across the social sciences
note.zh: 社会科学中的主导框架之一

note.en: Nobel laureate; among the most read philosophers of the century
note.zh: 诺贝尔奖得主；20 世纪最广为阅读的哲学家之一

note.en: Widely known through Jungian therapy; contested as a claim
note.zh: 借荣格学派疗法广为人知；作为主张仍受质疑

note.en: Held in some form by most of the world's ~2.4bn Christians and ~2bn Muslims
note.zh: 世界上约 24 亿基督徒与约 20 亿穆斯林中的多数以某种形式持有

origin.zh: 印度，约公元前 2 世纪

note.en: ~1.2bn Hindus; the Gita is among the most printed texts in history
note.zh: 约 12 亿印度教徒；《薄伽梵歌》是史上印量最大的文本之一

note.en: A major figure in 20th-century theology; shaped how symbol is understood
note.zh: 20 世纪神学的重要人物；塑造了对「象征」的理解

note.en: The origin of the modern idea of a leap of faith
note.zh: 现代「信仰跃升」观念的源头

note.en: A standard account of why people surrender freedom voluntarily
note.zh: 关于人为何自愿交出自由的经典论述

note.en: The Theory of Moral Sentiments, on how we see ourselves through others
note.zh: 《道德情操论》，论我们如何透过他人看自己

note.en: Created the essay as a form of writing; the first long, honest study of a self that keeps changing
note.zh: 开创了随笔这一文体；第一部长篇、坦诚地书写一个不断变化的自我的作品

note.en: The Ethics of Belief is the standard statement of evidentialism
note.zh: 《信念的伦理》是证据主义的标准陈述

image.credit: William Kingdon Clifford (editors Leslie Stephen and Fredick Pollock)

origin.zh: 尼科波利斯，约公元 125 年

note.en: The Enchiridion has stayed in print for nineteen centuries and carries Stoicism into modern self-help
note.zh: 《手册》流传十九个世纪未曾绝版，也是斯多葛思想进入现代自助读物的主要来源

note.en: A founder of the Arts and Crafts movement and a socialist critic of industrial labour — one of the few to join technology, craft and the meaning of work in one argument
note.zh: 工艺美术运动的奠基者，也是工业劳动的社会主义批评者 — 少数把技术、手艺与劳动意义放在同一个论证里的人

origin.zh: 马萨诸塞州康科德，1860 年
马萨诸塞州康科德，1849 年

title.en: Meditations

desc.en: Private notes by a Roman emperor on accepting fate and governing himself.
desc.zh: 罗马皇帝关于接受命运与自我治理的私人笔记。

why.en: A working notebook, not a treatise — you watch someone talk himself into accepting what he cannot control.
why.zh: 一本工作笔记而非论著：你会看到一个人如何说服自己接受无法控制之事。

title.en: Ecclesiastes

desc.en: A wisdom book on the vanity of effort and the shortness of memory.
desc.zh: 一卷智慧书，论劳碌的虚空与记忆的短暂。

why.en: The bleakest book in the canon, and the one that refuses every easy consolation.
why.zh: 正典中最冷峻的一卷，拒绝一切廉价安慰。

title.en: The Myth of Sisyphus

desc.en: An essay on how to live once the world offers no reasons.
desc.zh: 一篇关于世界不提供理由时如何生活的随笔。

why.en: The clearest statement of what to do when explanation runs out and you still have to live.
why.zh: 当解释走到尽头而你仍要活下去时该怎么办 — 最清晰的陈述。

title.en: Man's Search for Meaning

desc.en: A psychiatrist's account of finding meaning in the camps.
desc.zh: 一位精神科医师关于在集中营中寻得意义的记述。

why.en: The case that meaning is found in a situation rather than supplied by the universe.
why.zh: 论意义在处境中被找到，而非由宇宙提供。

title.en: The Human Condition

desc.en: On labour, work and action, and what it means to appear in public.
desc.zh: 论劳动、工作与行动，以及「在公共中显现」意味着什么。

why.en: Where the argument lives that a life is judged by what it starts, not what it accumulates.
why.zh: 「一生应以其开启之事而非积累之物来衡量」这一论证的出处。

title.en: The Denial of Death

desc.en: An argument that culture is machinery for avoiding mortality.
desc.zh: 论文化是回避死亡的机器。

why.en: An argument that most of culture is machinery for not thinking about mortality.
why.zh: 论大部分文化都是「不去想死亡」的机器。

title.en: Zhuangzi

desc.en: Stories and paradoxes that loosen fixed positions.
desc.zh: 以故事与悖论松动固定立场。

why.en: Stories and paradoxes that unsettle fixed positions rather than replacing them with new ones.
why.zh: 以故事与悖论动摇固定立场，而不是用新立场取代它们。

title.en: Analects

desc.en: Fragments of Confucius on conduct, ritual and office.
desc.zh: 孔子论行事、礼与为官的片段记录。

why.en: Confucius redirecting metaphysical questions toward conduct, recorded in fragments.
why.zh: 孔子把形而上的问题引向行事，以片段记录下来。

title.en: On Liberty

desc.en: The case for individual freedom and its limits.
desc.zh: 为个人自由及其边界辩护。

why.en: Still the sharpest statement of why the majority being sure is not the same as the majority being right.
why.zh: 关于「多数人确信」不等于「多数人正确」的最锐利陈述。

image.credit: John Stuart Mill (author), John W. Parker and Son (publisher)

title.en: Two Concepts of Liberty

desc.en: The distinction between freedom from interference and freedom to become.
desc.zh: 区分「免于干涉的自由」与「成为自己的自由」。

why.en: The essay that made it impossible to say 'freedom' without saying which kind.
why.zh: 这篇文章之后，说「自由」就必须说清是哪一种。

title.en: The Brothers Karamazov

desc.en: A novel containing the Grand Inquisitor's case against freedom.
desc.zh: 小说中包含《宗教大法官》对自由的控诉。

why.en: The Grand Inquisitor chapter argues people hand freedom away with relief — read it before deciding you want more.
why.zh: 《宗教大法官》一章论人们如释重负地交出自由 — 在你确信想要更多自由前读它。

title.en: The Second Sex

desc.en: On how a person is made rather than born into a social role.
desc.zh: 论一个人如何被造就，而非生来就属于某个社会角色。

why.en: The origin of the argument that identity is produced by situation, not discovered in nature.
why.zh: 「身份由处境造就而非在自然中被发现」这一论证的源头。

title.en: The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life
title.zh: The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life

desc.en: Social life described as staged performance, with front and back regions.
desc.zh: 把社会生活描述为舞台表演，区分前台与后台。

why.en: Once you have read it you cannot stop noticing the performance, including your own.
why.zh: 读过之后，你会不断注意到表演 — 包括你自己的。

title.en: Reasons and Persons

desc.en: On identity, continuity and what matters in survival.
desc.zh: 论同一性、连续性，以及存续中真正重要的是什么。

why.en: The thought experiments that make 'am I the same person?' a much harder question than it looks.
why.zh: 一系列思想实验，让「我还是同一个人吗」变得远比看上去困难。

title.en: An Essay Concerning Human Understanding

desc.en: Where personal identity is first tied to continuity of memory.
desc.zh: 首次把人格同一性系于记忆的连续性。

why.en: Book II chapter 27 is where the modern conversation about personal identity starts.
why.zh: 第二卷第 27 章是现代人格同一性讨论的起点。

image.credit: The original uploader was Olaf Simons at German Wikipedia.

title.en: Anarchy, State, and Utopia

desc.en: Contains the experience machine, the standard objection to hedonism.
desc.zh: 书中提出「体验机」，对享乐主义的标准反驳。

why.en: One short thought experiment that most people fail, and learn something from failing.
why.zh: 一个简短的思想实验，多数人「答错」，并从答错中有所得。

title.en: On the Genealogy of Morals

desc.en: Morality read as a history with interests behind it.
desc.zh: 把道德读作背后带着利益的历史。

why.en: Nietzsche asking not whether a value is true but who it served — a question that does not switch off.
why.zh: 尼采问的不是某价值是否为真，而是它服务于谁 — 这个问题一旦问出便无法关闭。

title.en: Nicomachean Ethics

desc.en: On virtue, habit and what a life well lived consists in.
desc.zh: 论德性、习惯，以及好的一生由什么构成。

why.en: The origin of the idea that character is built by repetition, not chosen in a moment.
why.zh: 「品格由重复养成，而非一念之间选定」这一想法的源头。

title.en: Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren

desc.en: A forecast that abundance would arrive and leave us short of purpose.
desc.zh: 预测富足终将到来，而我们将缺少目的。

why.en: A century old and now checkable — he got the productivity right and the working week wrong.
why.zh: 写于近百年前，如今可以核对：生产率他猜对了，工时他猜错了。

title.en: The Theory of the Leisure Class
title.zh: The Theory of the Leisure Class

desc.en: On status competition and consumption as display.
desc.zh: 论地位竞争与作为展示的消费。

why.en: Written about the Gilded Age and embarrassingly applicable to now.
why.zh: 写的是镀金时代，读来却尴尬地贴合当下。

title.en: Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844

desc.en: The account of alienated labour.
desc.zh: 关于异化劳动的论述。

why.en: The alienation argument, before the economics — about what work does to a person.
why.zh: 在经济学之前的异化论证 — 关于劳动对人做了什么。

title.en: The Will to Believe

desc.en: An argument that some questions cannot wait for evidence.
desc.zh: 论有些问题无法等待证据。

why.en: James's argument that some questions are forced, aimed at people who prefer to abstain.
why.zh: 詹姆斯论有些问题是被迫的，专为倾向弃权的人而写。

title.en: Tao Te Ching

desc.en: Eighty-one short chapters on acting with the grain of things.
desc.zh: 八十一章短文，讲顺物之纹理而行。

why.en: Short, aphoristic, and the primary source for pattern without a planner.
why.zh: 简短、格言式，是「有规律而无安排者」的原始文本。

title.en: What the Buddha Taught

desc.en: A plain introduction to no-self and dependent origination.
desc.zh: 关于无我与缘起的平实导论。

why.en: A compact introduction to no-self and dependent origination without much jargon.
why.zh: 关于无我与缘起的简明导论，几乎没有术语。

title.en: The Social Construction of Reality

desc.en: How shared reality is built and then experienced as given.
desc.zh: 共享的现实如何被建构，又如何被体验为理所当然。

why.en: The book that made 'socially constructed' a phrase, for better and worse.
why.zh: 让「社会建构」成为流行说法的那本书 — 有好有坏。

title.en: Synchronicity

desc.en: Jung's account of coincidences that carry meaning without cause.
desc.zh: 荣格论无因果却有意义的巧合。

why.en: Useful for seeing where the claim is psychological and where it overreaches.
why.zh: 用来看清这一主张在哪里属于心理学，在哪里越界。

title.en: The Bhagavad Gita

desc.en: A dialogue on duty and detachment set on the eve of a battle.
desc.zh: 战前夕关于义务与不执著的对话。

why.en: The origin of the act-without-attachment argument.
why.zh: 「行动而不执著于结果」这一论证的源头。

title.en: Dynamics of Faith

desc.en: On symbol, and why a religious claim is not a factual report.
desc.zh: 论象征，以及宗教主张为何不是事实报告。

why.en: The clearest statement that taking a symbol literally is the way to misunderstand it.
why.zh: 「按字面理解象征即是误解象征」最清晰的陈述。

title.en: Escape from Freedom

desc.en: Why people hand freedom to authority, written as it was happening.
desc.zh: 人为何把自由交给权威 — 写于此事正在发生之时。

why.en: Written in 1941 about why people choose submission — the timing is the argument.
why.zh: 写于 1941 年，论人为何选择服从 — 写作时机本身就是论证。

title.en: Marriage and Morals

desc.en: The book whose reception cost Russell a teaching post.
desc.zh: 这本书的反响让罗素失去了一个教职。

why.en: Contains his flattest line about how little popularity proves.
why.zh: 书中有他最直白的一句：流行说明不了什么。

title.en: The Theory of Moral Sentiments

desc.en: On sympathy, and the impartial spectator we build inside ourselves.
desc.zh: 论同情，以及我们在内心建立的公正旁观者。

why.en: The other Smith — on why we cannot stop watching ourselves being watched.
why.zh: 另一个斯密 — 论我们为何无法停止看着自己被看。

title.en: Essays

desc.en: A man studying himself over twenty years and finding no fixed thing.
desc.zh: 一个人用二十年研究自己，却找不到固定之物。

why.en: The first writer to treat his own inconsistency as the finding rather than the failure.
why.zh: 第一位把自身的不一致当作发现而非失败的作者。

title.en: Sceptical Essays

desc.en: On how much confidence the evidence actually licenses.
desc.zh: 论证据究竟容许多少确信。

why.en: Opens with a proposal so demanding Russell admits it would be revolutionary.
why.zh: 开篇提出的要求之高，连罗素自己都承认是革命性的。

title.en: The Ethics of Belief

desc.en: An argument that believing without evidence is a moral failure, not just an error.
desc.zh: 论无证据而信是道德过失，而不只是错误。

why.en: The shipowner parable at the start does more work than the argument that follows.
why.zh: 开篇的船主寓言比后面的论证更有力。

title.en: Journals

desc.en: The notebooks where his idea of a truth one can live by first appears.
desc.zh: 「可据以生活的真理」这一想法最早出现的笔记。

why.en: Written at twenty-two, and already the whole programme is there.
why.zh: 写于二十二岁，整个纲领已在其中。

title.en: Mencius

desc.en: On the goodness of human nature and what circumstance does to it.
desc.zh: 论人性之善，以及环境对它做了什么。

why.en: The water metaphor is the clearest ancient statement of nature versus circumstance.
why.zh: 水的比喻是关于「本性与环境」最清晰的古代陈述。

title.en: Politics

desc.en: On the city, and why a human outside one is not fully human.
desc.zh: 论城邦，以及为何人在城邦之外不成其为完整的人。

why.en: Where belonging is argued to be constitutive rather than optional.
why.zh: 归属在此被论证为构成性的，而非可选的。

title.en: Utilitarianism

desc.en: A defence of welfare as the measure, with room for higher pleasures.
desc.zh: 为以福利作为尺度辩护，并为高级快乐留出位置。

why.en: The dissatisfied-Socrates passage is where Mill breaks with simple hedonism.
why.zh: 「不满足的苏格拉底」一段，是密尔与简单享乐主义分道之处。

title.en: An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation
title.zh: An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation

desc.en: The founding statement of utilitarian calculation.
desc.zh: 功利计算的奠基性陈述。

why.en: The opening sentence is the whole doctrine in one line.
why.zh: 开篇一句就是整套学说。

title.en: Opinions and Social Pressure

desc.en: The line-judgement experiments, reported by the man who ran them.
desc.zh: 线段判断实验，由实验者本人报告。

why.en: Short, plain, and the numbers are still uncomfortable seventy years later.
why.zh: 简短平实，七十年后那些数字依然令人不安。

title.en: The Point of View for My Work as an Author
title.zh: The Point of View for My Work as an Author

desc.en: Kierkegaard explaining, after the fact, what he had been doing.
desc.zh: 克尔凯郭尔事后解释自己一直在做什么。

why.en: Contains his flattest statement about crowds, and it is not a compliment.
why.zh: 书中有他关于群众最直白的一句 — 那不是赞美。
